For those representations we were left with two options: certain one dimensional module is a ghost space or not. Here we find the $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3)$ has ghost classes. It means that it is generated by a class from the cohomology of the Borel subgroup. With the techniques developed here, we show that the $d_2$ map of the spectral sequence for the boundary cohomology of $GL_4(\Z)$ is non-trivial if and only if there is a ghost class in $GL_3(\Z)$ (see Propositions 11 and 12.) We use a result of Elbaz-Vincent, Gangl and Soule to show that a spectral sequence related to $GL_4(\Z)$ does not degenerate at $E_2$-level. Then $d_2$ is non-trivial. Therefore, we obtain that $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3))$ is a ghost space, where $V_3$ is the standard representation.
papers.comments: The main result of the preprint regarding ghost classes is incorrect. I knew that and I should have withdrawn it a few years ago. Very recently I learned that there is a proof by Tien-Duy Nguyen showing that there are not ghost classes in SL3(Z). The proof is clear and directly to the point

papers.title: Constant solutions of the SU(2) Yang-Mills-Dirac equations: classification and explicit form
papers.abstract: We present a complete classification of all constant solutions of the ${\rm SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Dirac equations in Minkowski space ${\mathbb R}^{1,3}$. The method combines the hyperbolic singular value decomposition of the real matrix of the gauge potential with the two-sheeted covering of ${\rm SO}(3)$ by ${\rm SU}(2)$. In the degenerate case of zero potential, we classify the solutions by the causal structure of the current. For nondegenerate solutions with $Ψ\neq 0$ and $A\neq 0$, the equations force a sharp dichotomy: a nonzero constant current requires a nonzero mass, and massless solutions necessarily have zero current. The massive branch gives a constant non-Abelian field configuration with nonvanishing invariant $F^2=F_{μν}F^{μν}$. The remaining (degenerate) solutions are classified for completeness. For each case we give explicit formulas for the spinor $Ψ$, the potential $A$, the current $J$, and the invariant $F^2$, and we summarize the classification in a table. Nonconstant solutions can be sought as perturbation-theory series around constant solutions. We write the linear equations for the first-order correction, which reduce to linear partial differential equations with constant coefficients, and find explicit plane-wave solutions of these equations in the massless case.

papers.title: A note on split extension classifiers of perfect objects
papers.abstract: It is well known that the automorphism group of a perfect group has trivial center. This is a consequence of the fact that for a perfect group the centralizer of the normal subgroup of inner automorphisms of its automorphism group is trivial. We find a categorical explanation for this fact by showing that for a semi-abelian category $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying (WNH), if $X$ is a perfect object in $\mathbb{C}$ such that the split extension classifier $[X]$ exists, then the centralizer of the \emph{conjugation} morphism $c_X : X\to [X]$ is trivial and hence the center of $[X]$ is trivial. Our proof depends on the following fact, which we show holds in an arbitrary semi-abelian category satisfying (WNH). If $f:X\to Y$ is a central extension and $θ_1$, $θ_2$ and $φ$ are internal object actions of $B$ on $X$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, such that $f:(X,θ_i)\to (Y,φ)$ is an internal $B$-action morphism, then $θ_1$ and $θ_2$ restrict to the same action on $[X,X]$. Using this latter fact we also prove that (UCE) is a consequence of (WNH) alone (rather than of (WNH) together with (SH) as previously known).

papers.title: Functional equation, upper bounds and analogue of Lindelöf hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta function
papers.abstract: The functional equations of the Riemann zeta function, the Hurwitz zeta function, and the Lerch zeta function have been well known for a long time, and there is great importance in studying these zeta functions. For example, fundamental properties such as the upper bounds, the distribution of zeros, and the zero-free regions in the Riemann zeta function derive from functional equations. In this paper, we consider the functional equations for the Barnes double zeta-function $ ζ_2 (s, α; v, w ) = \sum_{m=0}^\infty \sum_{n=0}^\infty (α+vm+wn)^{-s} $. Additionally, by applying this functional equation and the Phragmén-Lindelöf convexity principle, we obtain some upper bounds for $ ζ_2(σ+ it, α; v, w) $ with respect to $ t $ as $ t \rightarrow \infty $. Furthermore, we prove that an analogue of the Lindel"of hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta-function is equivalent to suitable upper bounds for its positive even moments on vertical lines in the critical strip.
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Ramanujan mathematical Society, Vol. 41, No. 4 (2006), pp. 311-324

papers.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
papers.abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.
papers.comments: 71 pages, 10 figures. v3: added discussions of the Cardy relation and of morphisms of topological Frobenius algebras. Various other minor changes. This is the final version of the paper, accepted for publication in EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences

papers.title: Uniformly Expanding Coupled Maps: Self-Consistent Transfer Operators and Propagation of Chaos
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation, uniformly in time, for systems of $N$ deterministic uniformly expanding heterogeneously coupled maps. The local dynamics and interactions may vary between coordinates, so exchangeability is not required. Under assumptions (independent of the dimension) on expansion, regularity, and weak-coupling, we construct self-consistent transfer operators whose product evolutions approximate every fixed finite marginal. For a class of weakly dependent initial laws (containing products), the error is $O(N^{-1})$ on fixed time intervals and $O(\log N/N)$ uniformly in time. The finite-time rate is optimal within this class. An explicit family exhibits error of order $\sqrt{\log N}/N$ at times of order $\log N$, proving that a uniform $O(N^{-1})$ bound is impossible in general; the optimal correction remains open. The proof is based on ergodic theory: expansion preserves classes of regular, weakly dependent densities, while transfer-operator contraction controls error accumulation. These classes yield concentration estimates and allow direct comparison of densities, giving strong propagation of chaos without external noise. Under additional assumptions, we also obtain Gaussian approximation for empirical observables on fixed time intervals and invariant neighbourhoods of stable fixed points of the self-consistent operator.
papers.comments: Substantially revised. The main result remains uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for uniformly expanding coupled maps. Additions include optimal O(1/N) finite-time rates, O(log N/N) uniform-in-time bounds, Gaussian fluctuations, and an example showing that a correction to the uniform O(1/N) rate is necessary. Proofs and exposition revised

papers.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
papers.abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

papers.title: Isoparametric functions on Finsler space forms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that each connected regular level hypersurface of a transnormal function on a Finsler space form $(N(c),F)$ has constant principal curvatures under suitable conditions. This result extends Miyaoka's refinement of Q. M. Wang's classical theorem on transnormal functions in Riemannian space forms to the Finsler setting. On forward Finsler space forms $(\overrightarrow{N}(c),F)$, we discuss the relationship between umbilic hypersurfaces and isoparametric hypersurfaces, and construct global and local isoparametric functions using the distance function.

papers.title: The pro-$\mathcal{C}$ anabelian geometry of number fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathcal{C}$ a nontrivial full class of finite groups. Write $K^{\mathcal{C}}/K$ for the maximal pro-$\mathcal{C}$ Galois extension of $K$ and $G_K^{\mathcal{C}}$ for its Galois group. Write $Σ(\mathcal{C})$ for the set of prime numbers $p$ such that $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{C}$. We prove that, for two such pairs $(K_i,\mathcal{C}_i)$, every isomorphism $G_{K_1}^{\mathcal{C}_1}\simeq G_{K_2}^{\mathcal{C}_2}$ is induced by a unique isomorphism between $K_2^{\mathcal{C}_2}/K_2$ and $K_1^{\mathcal{C}_1}/K_1$, provided that $Σ(\mathcal{C}_i)$ has positive upper Dirichlet density for at least one $i$. As a consequence, we generalize reconstruction results of Uchida and Sueyoshi to Galois extensions $Ω_i/K_i$ such that $Ω_i$ has no nontrivial abelian pro-$Σ$ extension, where $Σ$ has positive upper Dirichlet density. We also prove a relative version of the first result without a density assumption: the same conclusion holds if the group isomorphism is compatible with the canonical restriction maps to the maximal abelian pro-$Σ(\mathcal{C}_1)$ quotient of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}$, and if $2\inΣ(\mathcal{C}_1)$ or at least one of $K_1,K_2$ has a complex prime. This relative result applies, in particular, to maximal pro-$p$ quotients under these conditions.

papers.title: The complete dynamics description of positively curved metrics in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$
papers.abstract: The family of invariant Riemannian manifolds in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$ is described by three parameters $(x,y,z)$ of positive real numbers. By restricting such a family of metrics in the \emph{tetrahedron} $\cal{T}:= x+y+z = 1$, in this paper, we describe all regions $\cal R \subset \cal T$ admitting metrics with curvature properties varying from positive sectional curvature to positive scalar curvature, including positive intermediate curvature notion's. We study the dynamics of such regions under the \emph{projected Ricci flow} in the plane $(x,y)$, concluding sign curvature maintenance and escaping. In addition, we obtain some results for positive intermediate Ricci curvature for a path of metrics on fiber bundles over $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$, further studying its evolution under the Ricci flow on the base.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 12 figures. Accepted version. To appear in Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2305.06119

papers.title: Metric-Measure Concentration and Strong Cosmic Censorship in Vacuum Gowdy Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy maximal globally hyperbolic development is $C^2$-inextendible if its asymptotic velocity differs from one on a dense subset of the singular circle. This is the implication posed in Section~14.2 of Ringström's 2010 review. The proof compares the spacetime volume of a timelike boundary collar with that of a shrinking angular cone, using Killing transport and the Einstein constraint. We connect this criterion to Gromov's observable distance: the physical spatial mm-spaces satisfy the lower bound $d_{\rm conc}(X_τ,*)\ge L(τ)/(4+L(τ))$, where $L(τ)$ is the length of the orbit circle. If $L(τ)\to0$, then $v_\infty\ge1$ everywhere, the critical set $\{v_\infty=1\}$ has Lebesgue measure zero, and the development is $C^2$-inextendible. Thus physical point concentration is sufficient for inextendibility, but is not necessary. We also give explicit, non-perturbative subcritical characteristic conditions on vacuum Cauchy data ensuring quantitative Kretschmann blow-up without using Gowdy asymptotic theorems in the curvature estimate. The exact volume-transfer identity yields predictive monotonicity criteria and distinguishes coordinate localization from intrinsic metric collapse. In the transversely expanding regime, observable rescalings with an extended transverse-length limit are classified as a point, a measured circle, or the maximal pyramid; a uniform spectral estimate eliminates all nontrivial toroidal Fourier sectors, including in the presence of spikes. The geometric framework is completed by quantitative tube estimates, a local CMC redistribution theorem, and constrained variational descriptions of the reduced energy current and normalized-volume flow.

papers.title: Embedding Capabilities of Neural ODEs
papers.abstract: Neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs) are a class of neural networks that have gained particular interest in recent years. We study input-output relations of neural ODEs using dynamical systems theory and prove several results about the exact embedding of maps in different neural ODE architectures in low and high dimensions. The embedding capability of a neural ODE architecture can be increased by adding, for example, affine linear layers or augmenting the phase space. However, there is currently no systematic theory available, and our work contributes towards this goal by developing various embedding results as well as identifying situations where no embedding is possible. Our core mathematical techniques include iterative functional equations, Morse functions, and suspension flows, as well as several further ideas from analysis. Although in practice mostly universal approximation theorems are used, our geometric dynamical systems viewpoint on universal embedding provides a fundamental understanding of why certain neural ODE architectures perform better than others.

papers.title: The universal Euler characteristic and Burnside group for definable groupoids
papers.abstract: We introduce the universal Euler characteristic of orbit space definable groupoids, a class of groupoids containing cocompact proper Lie groupoids as well as translation groupoids associated to proper definable group actions. We show that every additive and multiplicative invariant of orbit space definable groupoids with an additional local triviality hypothesis arises as a ring homomorphism applied to the universal Euler characteristic. This in particular includes the $Γ$-orbifold Euler characteristic introduced by the first and third authors when $Γ$ is a finitely presented group. For definable groupoids, where the object and arrow spaces as well as the structure maps are definable, we also introduce a Burnside group which is an analog of the classical Burnside ring associated to compact Lie groups and, for a transitive groupoid with compact isotropy, admits a partial multiplication.
papers.comments: 38 pages. Significant revision from version 2. Clarified hypotheses and corrected errors in Section 5; edited to improve exposition throughout. Accepted version to appear in the Journal of Algebra

papers.title: Ruin Theory Problems in Simple SDE Models with Large Deviation Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We examine hitting probability problems for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes and Geometric Brownian motions (GBM) with respect to exponential boundaries related to problems arising in risk theory and asset and liability models in pension funds. In Section 2 we consider the OU process described by the Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) $dX_t = μX_t dt + σdW_t$ with $X_0=x_0$ evolving between a lower and an upper deterministic exponential boundary. Both the finite horizon ``ruin probability'' problem and the corresponding infinite horizon problem is examined in the low noise case, using the Wentzell-Freidlin approach in order to obtain logarithmic asymptotics for the probability of hitting either the lower or the upper boundary. The resulting variational problems are studied in detail. The exponential rate characterizing the ruin probability and the ``path to ruin'' are obtained by their solution. Logarithmic asymptotics for the meeting probability in a pair of OU processes with different positive drift coefficients, driven by independent Brownian motions is also obtained using Wentzell-Freidlin techniques. The optimal paths followed by the two processes and the meeting time $T$ are determined by solving a variational problem with transversality conditions. In Section 3 a corresponding problem involving a Geometric Brownian motion is considered. Since in this case, an exact, closed form solution is also available and we take advantage of this situation in order to explore numerically the quality of the Large Deviations results obtained using the Wentzell-Freidlin approach.
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, vol. 477, 2026

papers.title: A convergence result for a local planning problem for mean field games and rigorous proof of a Freidlin-Ventchel-type Large Deviations Principle for the $1+1$ KPZ equation
papers.abstract: We study an innovative connection between a very singular optimal transport variational problem with a congestion term connecting two Dirac measures, which is related to the planing problem in mean field games or gases with negative pressure, and a large deviation principle for the KPZ equation. The main result proves a limit of a singular approixmate problem with vanishing diffusive flux and a relaxed initial condition. The paper also provides a rigorous justification for the informal analysis of the ad hoc large deviation principle for the KPZ equation appearing in the physics literature.
papers.journal_ref: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis (2026)

papers.title: Functional weak convergence of stochastic integrals for moving averages and continuous-time random walks
papers.abstract: There is an extensive theory of weak convergence for moving averages and continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) with respect to Skorokhod's M1 and J1 topologies. Here we address the fundamental question of how this translates into functional limit theorems in the M1 or J1 topology for stochastic integrals driven by these processes. As an important application, we provide weak approximation results for general SDEs driven by time-changed Lévy processes. Such SDEs and their associated fractional Fokker--Planck--Kolmogorov equations are central to models of anomalous diffusion in statistical physics. Our results yield a rigorous functional characterisation of these as continuum limits of the underlying models driven by CTRWs. With regard to strictly M1 convergent moving averages and correlated CTRWs, it turns out that the convergence of stochastic integrals can fail decidedly and fundamental new challenges arise compared to the J1 setting. Nevertheless, we identify natural classes of integrand processes for which there is M1 convergence of the stochastic integrals. We also show that these results are flexible enough to yield functional limit theorems in the M1 topology for certain stochastic delay differential equations driven by moving averages.

papers.title: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Combinatorial Theory Series B 182 (2027), 106-125

papers.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $λ\in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > λ$. In this paper, we construct, for each given $ε>0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_ε,d_ε) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > λ$, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_ε) \leq ε$, and $X_ε$ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_ε$ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_ε$ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition. However, our method involves removing an infinite number of balls from $X$, allowing us to construct in the general case of dimensions greater than or equal to $3$. As a corollary, we provide a solution to an open problem posed by Naber in the $3$-dimensional case.

papers.title: Resolving Gilbert's Conjecture: Dimensional Dependencies in Hardy Spaces Valued in Clifford Modules
papers.abstract: This article provides a thorough investigation into Gilbert's Conjecture, pertaining to Hardy spaces in the upper half-space valued in Clifford modules. We explore the conjecture proposed by Gilbert in 1991, which seeks to extend the classical principle of representing real $L^p$ functions on the real line as boundary values of Hardy holomorphic functions to higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces valued in any Clifford module. We present a complete resolution to this conjecture, demonstrating that its validity is contingent upon the dimension $n$, specifically holding true when \(n \not\equiv 6, 7 \mod 8\) and failing otherwise. The pivotal discovery that Gilbert's conjecture can be reformulated as a set of algebraic conditions is underscored in this work. To navigate these conditions, we employ a novel strategy that leverages the octonions, revealing their instrumental role in addressing issues related to Clifford modules and spinors. This innovative approach not only provides explicit realization through the generalization of the Hilbert transform to the Riesz transform but also establishes a significant advancement in the understanding of Hardy spaces within higher dimensions.
papers.comments: 25pages. It corrects the proofs for the cases 8k+3 and 8k+5 in the previous version, and also corrects how the proof of Theorem 5.1 for general Clifford modules is stated

papers.title: Operator dependent para-controlled calculus, periodic homogenisation and singular PDEs
papers.abstract: We develop a variant of the para-controlled distributions framework based on operator dependent (generalised) Besov spaces. This in particular covers the class of oscillatory operators from periodic homogenisation. We then apply the framework to study periodic homogenisation problems for a class of singular stochastic PDEs. One novel viewpoint is to measure regularity via the geometry induced by the operators at hand rather than classical Fourier basis. The generalised Besov spaces were introduced by Kerkyacharian-Petrushev. In contrast to the Fourier decomposition in the classical setting, they are built from spectral decomposition of general self-adjoint elliptic operators. A major difference is that products of two spectrally localised functions in general have ``frequencies" spread over the whole spectrum. We obtain a decay estimate on ``high frequency" component of the product of two spectrally-localised functions. This enables us to obtain uniform bounds for the naturally associated para-product and commutator operations over a class of operators. This in particular includes the family of periodic homogenisation operators uniform in the oscillation parameter. Next, we show convergence properties of these operations in the periodic homogenisation setting. A key ingredient is a sharp quantitative convergence of the generalised Littlewood-Paley block operators. The proof utilises the Helffer-Sjöstrand's formula for self-adjoint operators. Finally, we apply this framework to periodic homogenisation problems for dynamical $φ^4_3$, $2$D gPAM, and $1$D KPZ. Assuming the convergence of stochastic objects to their homogenised limits, we show that the solutions and fluxes also converge to the corresponding limits. The convergence of the explicit stochastic terms with suitable renormalisations will be treated in a separate note.
papers.comments: 110 pages now. Compared to the previous version, we updated the abstract, and also have made the following four main changes in the content: we added the 2D gPAM model (Theorem 1.3); extended the KPZ equation to general oscillatory coupling coefficient (Theorem 1.4); also simplified the proofs for both the uniform decay estimate (Proposition 2.7) and convergence of blocks (Theorem 3.1)

papers.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by Félix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.

papers.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
papers.abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.

papers.title: Reduced Basis method for finite volume simulations of parabolic PDEs applied to porous media flows
papers.abstract: In the context of underground gas storage (of CO2 typically) in saline aquifers, numerical simulation is a highly valuable tool to evaluate the impact of the uncertainties of various model parameters and to optimize, e.g., injection-production scenarios. For this purpose, finite volume approximations of Darcy's parabolic model for flows in porous media are usually run many times, for many values of parameters like permeability and porosity, at costly computational efforts. We study the relevance of reduced basis methods as a way to lower the overall simulation cost of multi-point finite volume approximations to Darcy's parabolic model for flows in porous media for different values of the parameters such as permeability. We aim to quickly evaluate any linear form (or quantity of interest) of the pressure for many parameter values. To this end, we construct reduced bases by a standard POD-Greedy algorithm. Our POD-Greedy algorithm uses two new goal-oriented error estimators designed from a discrete space-time energy norm independent of the parameter. We provide some numerical experiments that validate the efficiency of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Fractional Laplace operator and related Schrödinger equations on locally finite graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first define a discrete version of the fractional Laplace operator $(-Δ)^{s}$ through the heat semigroup on a stochastically complete, connected, locally finite graph $G = (V, E, μ, w)$. Secondly, we define the fractional divergence and give another form of $(-Δ)^s$. The third point, and the foremost, is the introduction of the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,2}(V)$, which is necessary when we study problems involving $(-Δ)^{s}$. Finally, using the mountain-pass theorem and the Nehari manifold, we obtain multiplicity solutions to a discrete fractional Schrödinger equation on $G$. We caution the readers that though these existence results are well known in the continuous case, the discrete case is quite different.
papers.journal_ref: Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 64 (2025), no. 7, Paper No. 227, 27 pp

papers.title: Surface elevation errors in finite element Stokes models for glacier evolution
papers.abstract: The primary data which determine the evolution of glaciation are the bedrock elevation and the surface mass balance. From this data, which we assume is defined over a fixed land region, the glacier's geometry solves a free boundary problem which balances the time derivative of the surface elevation, the surface velocity from the Stokes flow of the ice, and the surface mass balance rate. This problem can be posed in weak form as a variational inequality over a cone of admissible surface elevation functions, those which are above the bedrock topography. After some preparatory theory for the Stokes problem, we conjecture that the corresponding continuous-space, implicit time-step variational inequality problem is well-posed if the surface kinematical equation is appropriately regularized. This conjecture is supported by physical arguments and numerical evidence. We then prove a general theorem which bounds the numerical error made by finite element approximations of nonlinear-operator variational inequalities in Banach spaces. This bound is a sum of error terms of different types, special to variational inequalities. When it is applied to the implicit time-step glacier problem there are three terms in the bound: an error from discretizing the bed elevation primarily near the glacier margin, an error from numerically solving for the Stokes velocity, and finally a Céa-type best-approximation error for the finite element space representation of the surface elevation. The design of glacier models is then reconsidered based on this mostly a priori error analysis.

papers.title: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
papers.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

papers.title: Well-posedness and long-time behavior for self-consistent Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations with general potentials
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness, steady states and long time behavior of solutions to Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with external confinement potential and nonlinear self-consistent interactions. Our analysis introduces newly characterized conditions on the interaction kernel that ensure the local asymptotic stability of the unique steady state. Compared to previous works on this topic, our results allow for large, singular and non-symmetric interactions. As a corollary of our main results, we show exponential decay of solutions to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation in dimension $3$, for low regularity initial data. In the repulsive case, the result holds in strongly nonlinear regimes (i.e. for arbitrarily small Debye length). Our techniques rely on the design of new Lyapunov functionals based on hypocoercivity and hypoellipticity theories. We use norms which include part of the interaction kernel, and carefully mix ``macroscopic quantities based''--hypocoercivity with ``commutators based''--hypocoercivity.

papers.title: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
papers.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

papers.title: Parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields) on a formal principal bundle with parahoric structures. This generalizes the reduction theory due to Hukuhara-Levelt-Turrittin and Babbitt-Varadarajan in the case without parahoric structures [7], and Boalch's result in the case of regular singularity [14]. As applications, we first prove that a formal connection is intrinsically regular if and only if it is a parahoric formal connection, in combination with the works of Bremer-Sage [45] and Chen-Kamgarpour [20], providing various criteria for the regularity of formal connections. We then introduce a notion of relative regularity for formal connections and give criterions. Finally, we demonstrate a parahoric version of Frenkel-Zhu's Borel reduction theorem of formal connections [33].
papers.comments: Revised version, 35 pages, comments are welcome!

papers.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].
papers.comments: 26 pages. Incorporated the comments of the referees. Journal version

papers.title: Iwasawa theory for unitary groups via Eisenstein congruences and its applications
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime number. In this article, we study automorphic aspects of Iwasawa theory for unitary groups, focusing on the $p$-primitivity of Klingen Eisenstein series and their $p$-adic families on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n+1)$, which is a key component in establishing lower bounds for Selmer groups in Iwasawa theory for $\mathrm{U}(m,n)$. First, we compute the Gan--Gross--Prasad period integral of a Klingen Eisenstein series on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n+1)$ against a cuspidal automorphic form on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n)$, and relate it to special Rankin--Selberg $L$-values. We then interpolate these period integrals $p$-adically as both forms vary in Hida families, thereby producing a Rankin--Selberg type $p$-adic $L$-function for $\mathrm{U}(m,n) \times \mathrm{U}(m+1,n)$ as a byproduct. This method is designed to replace the computation of Fourier--Jacobi coefficients used in the existing literature to establish the $p$-primitive property of Klingen Eisenstein series, which so far treats only cases where $m+n \leq 2$. As an application, we consider the case $\mathrm{U}(m,n)=\mathrm{U}(1,0)$ and obtain a new proof of M.-L. Hsieh's Iwasawa main conjecture for CM elliptic curves over a totally real field $F$ with CM field $M$ and good ordinary reduction at all places above $p$, for all primes $p \geq 5$ unramified in $F$. Our approach removes the assumption in Hsieh's original work that $p$ does not divide the relative class number of $MF/F$.
papers.comments: Major revision with corrections of typos and errors, and substantial expansion to include applications to Iwasawa main conjectures for CM fields. Based on the author's doctoral thesis. Further revisions are planned. Comments are very welcome

papers.title: Arthur packets for metaplectic groups
papers.abstract: For metaplectic groups over a local field of characteristic zero, we define the Arthur packet attached to any Arthur parameter $ψ$ as a multi-set of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterized by endoscopic character relations. Over number fields, we obtain a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete $L^2$-automorphic spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and $ε$-factors, by leveraging the trace formula for metaplectic groups. This confirms a conjecture of Gan, and extends earlier results of Gan-Ichino on the Shimura-Waldspurger correspondences, whereas their works play a critical role in our proof. Furthermore, all these are shown to be compatible with existing results in rank one (Waldspurger) and two (Gan-Ichino).
papers.comments: 97 pages with an index. Minor revision with some gaps fixed

papers.title: Extremely amenable automorphism groups of countable structures
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the isomorphism relation of extremely amenable non-Archimedean Polish groups from the point of view of descriptive set theory. Our main result is that this relation is more complex than any isomorphism relation of countable structures in the Borel reducibility hierarchy.

papers.title: Shortest Path Lengths in Poisson Line Cox Processes: Approximations and Applications
papers.abstract: We study street-constrained ($\ell_1$) shortest paths in a Poisson line Cox process (PLCP), where Poisson points of linear intensity $μ$ lie on the lines of an underlying Poisson line process (PLP) of density $λ$. Under a one-turn restriction, we derive closed-form expressions for the distribution of the nearest-neighbor path length from (i) the typical PLCP point and (ii) the typical PLP intersection, by explicitly evaluating the relevant void probabilities via a geometric decomposition of the feasible path-length set. For the intersection case, we further provide analytically tractable upper and lower bounds that capture the impact of $λ$ and $μ$. Allowing two turns from the typical point, we obtain a computable upper bound using a feasible-set shrinking argument and identify regimes in which it is tight. We also delineate parameter ranges where a one-turn route from a typical intersection can outperform a two-turn route from a typical point. Finally, we discuss how the results enable statistical performance characterization of ride-hailing services in terms of service guarantee, trip time, and consequently, derive dimensioning insights. We also illustrate qualitatively, how the results can be employed to study vehicle-to-vehicle communication broadcast messages near intersections.

papers.title: Differential forms and Brauer classes in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $p$-torsion Brauer classes in positive characteristic arising from differential forms. We relate this construction to the Brauer group of supersingular K3 surfaces and analyze the contribution of these classes to the Brauer-Manin obstruction. As an application, we examine the Brauer-Manin set of supersingular K3 surfaces and of varieties admitting many differential forms.
papers.comments: Some mistakes have been fixed. Improved exposition

papers.title: New codes from algebras of direct products of groups
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the algebraic-combinatorial description of group codes by using the Wedderburn-Artin decomposition of semisimple group algebras. Concretely, we give a detailed description of the Wedderburn-Artin decomposition of the semisimple group algebra associated with a direct product of finite groups that are cyclic, dihedral, or generalised quaternion. This, in turn, provides a group-algebraic framework for computing all linear codes generated by such groups. As a consequence, we find new linear codes that improve the best-known minimum distance for their length and dimension. We conclude the paper by discussing how group codes arised from some explicit Wedderburn-Artin decomposition can be utilised to construct quantum codes in a systematic way.

papers.title: Duality for Arithmetic $p$-adic Pro-étale Cohomology of Analytic Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that the arithmetic $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of smooth partially proper spaces over $K$ satisfies a duality, as conjectured by Colmez, Gilles and Nizioł. We derive it from the geometric duality on the Fargues-Fontaine curve by Galois descent techniques of Fontaine.
papers.comments: Fix a gap in functional analysis. Changed the manuscript according to referee comments

papers.title: K-moduli with real coefficients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an algebraic K-stability theory (e.g. special test configuration theory and optimal destabilization theory) for log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs, and construct a proper K-moduli space to parametrize K-polystable log Fano $\mathbb R$-pairs with some fixed invariants (e.g. dimension, volume, coefficients). All of these are well-known for log Fano $\mathbb Q$-pairs, and the strategy in this paper is trying to reduce the problems (in many cases) to $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case rather than rebuilding the whole program as in $\mathbb Q$-coefficients case.
papers.comments: Final version, accepted by Advances in Mathematics

papers.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over quartic fields
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a quartic field $K$. By the Mordell-Weil theorem, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated group. We determine all the possibilities for the torsion group $E(K)_{tor}$ where $K$ ranges over all quartic fields $K$ and $E$ ranges over all elliptic curves over $K$. We show that there are no sporadic torsion groups, or in other words, that all torsion groups either do not appear or they appear for infinitely many non-isomorphic elliptic curves $E$. Proving this requires showing that numerous modular curves $X_1(m,n)$ have no non-cuspidal degree $4$ points. We deal with almost all the curves using one of 3 methods: a method for the rank 0 cases requiring no computation; the Hecke sieve, a local method requiring computer-assisted computations; and the global method, an argument for the positive rank cases also requiring no computation. We deal with the handful of remaining cases using ad hoc methods.
papers.comments: 38 pages, final published version with 2 minor corrections added

papers.title: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
papers.abstract: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of twisted maps to smooth pairs
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of twisted maps to a smooth pair in arbitrary genus, and give geometric explanations for the known comparisons between orbifold and logarithmic Gromov--Witten invariants. We classify the irreducible components of the space of twisted maps to the universal target in terms of tropical data, and show that each is built from torsors under semi-abelian varieties coming from Jacobians of the domain curves. Natural morphisms between these spaces for different rooting parameters measure how each component grows: for rooting parameters sufficiently large and divisible, the growth is monomial, with exponent between $0$ and $\max(0,2g-1)$, and the main component is the only one with exponent $0$. In genus $1$ the virtual class is the fundamental class, which recovers the polynomiality results of Tseng and You. We conclude with geometric examples, beginning with Maulik's original genus $1$ example.

papers.title: Localisation for the second-order Beckmann problem: bimartingale couplings and leaf decompositions
papers.abstract: We develop a second-order localisation theory for optimal transport based on leaf decompositions and bimartingale couplings, which impose martingale constraints in opposite directions on complementary orthogonal subspaces. It provides a second-order analogue of the classical decomposition of optimal transport into transport rays and monotone couplings: transport rays are replaced by the leaves of the $1$-Lipschitz derivative map $Du$ of an optimal dual potential $u\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$, while monotone couplings are replaced by bimartingale couplings. We apply this framework to the three-marginal optimal transport problem introduced by Bolbotowski and Bouchitté, whose relaxation is the second-order Beckmann problem. We characterise the existence of bimartingale couplings through a convex-concave order condition. This yields a generalisation of Strassen's theorem from convex order to the convex-concave setting. Equivalently, the dual problem associated with the second-order Beckmann problem admits an optimiser whose derivative is an isometry. For absolutely continuous measures with common barycentre, assuming the existence of an optimal plan with absolutely continuous third marginal, we prove that every optimal plan decomposes into a family of problems on the leaves of $Du$. On each leaf, all optimal plans are completely described by bimartingale couplings between the corresponding conditional measures. Without this absolute continuity assumption on the third marginal, we show that the leaf decomposition persists in a more general form: optimal plans are mixtures of plans concentrated on triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $x\in \mathcal{S}_1$, $y\in \mathcal{S}_2$, and $z\in \mathcal{S}_1\cap \mathcal{S}_2$, where $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are neighbouring leaves of $Du$.
papers.comments: 53 pages, 3 figures; version accepted in the Calculus of Variations and Partial Differential Equations; comments are welcome

papers.title: Primitivity Testing in Free Group Algebras via Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a free group. By a classical result of Cohn and Lewin, the free group algebra $K\left[F\right]$ is a free ideal ring (FIR): a ring over which the submodules of free modules are themselves free, and of a well-defined rank. Given a finitely generated right ideal $I\leq K\left[F\right]$ and an element $f\in I$, we give an explicit algorithm determining whether $f$ is part of some basis of $I$. More generally, given free $K[F]$-modules $M\le N$, we provide algorithms determining whether $M$ is a free summand of $N$, and whether $N$ admits a free splitting relative to $M$. These can also be used to obtain analogous algorithms for free groups $H\le J$. As an aside, we also provide an algorithm to compute the intersection of two given submodules of a free $K\left[F\right]$-module. A key feature of this work is the introduction of a duality, induced by a matrix with entries in a free ideal ring, between the respective algebraic extensions of its column and row spaces.
papers.comments: 37 pages. Added Remarks 3.7 and 6.1. Journal version
papers.journal_ref: J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), no. 6, e70599

papers.title: Bridgeland Stability of Sheaves on del Pezzo Surface of Picard Rank Three
papers.abstract: We study the stability of line bundles and torsion sheaves under divisorial Bridgeland stability conditions. On the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at two general points, we characterize stability and semistability of a line bundle, or of its shift in the tilted heart, in terms of the three $(-1)$-curves. We also prove that, on any smooth projective surface, the pushforward of a torsion-free sheaf of rank $1$ on an integral curve of nonpositive self-intersection is stable for every divisorial stability condition.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 1 figure v3: major revision throughout

papers.title: A Computational Study for Solving Decision-Dependent Robust Problems as Bilevel Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: Both bilevel and robust optimization are established fields of mathematical optimization and operations research. However, only until recently, the similarities in their mathematical structure has neither been studied theoretically nor exploited computationally. Based on the recent results by Goerigk et al. (2025), this paper is the first one that provides an extensive computational study for solving strictly robust optimization problems with decision-dependent uncertainty sets as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. If the uncertainty set can be dualized, the respective bilevel techniques to obtain a single-level reformulation are very similar compared with the classic dualization techniques used in robust optimization but lead to larger single-level problems to be solved. Our numerical study shows that this usually leads to larger computation times. For the more challenging case of decision-dependent uncertainty sets represented by mixed-integer linear models, one cannot apply classic dualization techniques from robust optimization. Thus, we compare the presented bilevel approach with an established method from the literature, which is based on quantified mixed-integer linear programs. Our numerical results indicate that, for the problem class of decision-dependent robust optimization problems with mixed-integer linear uncertainty sets, the bilevel approach performs better in terms of computation times.

papers.title: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: quantitative aspects
papers.abstract: This paper relates to the Fourier decay properties of images of self-similar measures $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under nonlinear smooth maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}$. For example, we prove that if the linear parts of the similarities defining $μ$ commute and the graph of $f$ has non-vanishing Gaussian curvature and $κ_2 > k/2$, then the Fourier dimension of the image measure is at least $\frac{2(2κ_2 - k)}{4 + 2κ_* - k}$, where $κ_2$ is the lower correlation dimension of $μ$ and $κ_*$ is the Assouad dimension of the support of $μ$. Under some additional assumptions on $μ$, we use recent breakthroughs in the fractal uncertainty principle to obtain further improvements for the decay exponents. We give several applications to nonlinear arithmetic of self-similar sets $F$ in the line. For example, we prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (\sqrt{65} - 5)/4 = 0.765\dots$ then the arithmetic product set $F \cdot F = \{ xy : x,y \in F \}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, while if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (-3 + \sqrt{41})/4 = 0.850\dots$ then $F \cdot F \cdot F$ has non-empty interior. One feature of the above results is that they do not require any separation conditions on the self-similar sets.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 1 figure. v2: typo corrections including statement of Prop. 4.11, and some numbering changes. v3: further typo corrections. To appear in Peking Math. Journal

papers.title: Lyapunov Exponent Bounds for Random Products of Relaxed Projections
papers.abstract: Current performance bounds for randomized iterated projections, such as the Kaczmarz method, are often considered tight under per-iteration analyses, yet they are notoriously loose in practice. We derive asymptotic performance bounds that narrow this theory-practice gap, leveraging a new technique for bounding the spectral radii of operators arising in the Lyapunov exponent analysis of randomized iterations. The asymptotic analysis also uncovers the previously unexplained role of relaxation in improving performance, thereby resolving an open problem posed by Strohmer and Vershynin in 2007.

papers.title: A Majorana Relativistic Quantum Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in (1+1)-Dimensional Rindler Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We present a Hilbert--Pólya approach to the Riemann zeta function via a Mellin--Barnes integral for massive Majorana modes in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler spacetime. The boost spectrum is continuous on the full wedge and discrete with a reflecting wall. Summing positive momentum modes on a transverse circle yields $ζ(2s)$ in the radial Mellin transform. Building on our one-sided Cesàro criterion for additive correlations of $Λ(n)-1$, we assign each prime $p$ a chiral channel of optical length $\tfrac12\log p$. Its $k$th return at $u=k\log p$ carries weight $\log p$. The centered correlation obeys $C(u)\le C(0)$ for all real $u$ exactly when the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds. For a Majorana oscillator with linear mass profile, a bounded self-adjoint function of its Hamiltonian assigns period $kT_1$ to mode pair $k$. The first $n$ pairs have least common period $T_n=T_1\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)$, so $\log(T_n/T_{n-1})=Λ(n)$ for $n\ge2$. Set $m=\lceil\sqrt{x}\rceil$, $N=\lfloor mx\rfloor$, and $ψ(y)=\sum_{n\le y}Λ(n)$. The signed revival mean $A(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}(N/j-ψ(N/j))$ satisfies $A(x)=R(x)+o(\sqrt{x})$, where $R(x)=\sum_{n\le x}Λ(n)(x/n-1)-x\log x+(1+γ_{\mathrm E})x$. At each zeta zero $ρ$ of multiplicity $d$ with $\Re(ρ)>1/2$, the meromorphic continuation of $\int_2^\infty A(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx$ has a simple pole of residue $d/[ρ(1-ρ)]$. For fixed $λ>1$, $1/2<θ<\Re(ρ)$ and $K>0$, the Kaczorowski--Pintz theorem gives $A(x)>Kx^θ$ at some $x\in[Y,Y^λ]$ for all large $Y$. Thus RH follows if for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $C_\varepsilon$ with $A(x)\le C_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ throughout $[Y,Y^λ]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$. For $λ=3/2$, the independent theta-lift estimate reported by Alpöge and Claude for $G=R$ gives this bound for $A$.
papers.comments: 38 pages + appendix for a total of 108 pages 3 Figures in tikzpicture, updated and in agreement with Alpöge - Claude route to RH as Hilbert Pólya approach with Majorana fields

papers.title: Glued tree lattices with only compact localized states
papers.abstract: Flat band physics is a central theme in modern condensed matter physics. By constructing a tight--binding single particle system that has vanishing momentum dispersion in one or more bands, and subsequently including more particles and interactions, it is possible to study physics in strongly interacting regimes. Inspired by the glued trees that first arose in one of the few known examples of quantum supremacy, we define and analyze two infinite families of tight binding single particle Bose--Hubbard models that have only flat bands, and only compact localized states despite having any nonnegative number of translation symmetries. The first class of model that we introduce is constructed by replacing a sufficiently large fraction of the edges in a generic countable graph with glued trees modified to have complex hoppings. The second class arises from thinking of complex weighted glued trees as rhombi that can then be used to tile two dimensional space, giving rise to the familiar dice lattice and infinitely many generalizations thereof, of which some are Euclidian while others are hyperbolic.

papers.title: Coarse chain recurrence and Morse graphs with finite errors
papers.abstract: This paper provides a unified framework connecting dynamical systems with tools from topological data analysis and geometric topology and inspires new interactions among dynamical systems, topology, and nonlinear analysis. To this end, we introduce a one-parameter family of ``chain recurrences'' that generalizes chain recurrence and induces a natural filtration on the underlying metric space of a dynamical system. In particular, the forward directions of the filtrations characterize the level of control required to return to the original position, and the backward directions capture the robustness of the recurrence. The resulting filtrations yield potentials and bifurcation diagrams of dynamical systems that encode the evolution of recurrent sets under bounded total or stepwise perturbations. In addition, we extend Morse graphs to one-parameter families of ``coarse Morse graphs,'' which evolve through vertex collapses reflecting coarse recurrence transitions. These constructions not only refine Conley's decomposition but also reveal singular limit behaviors as the perturbation level vanishes. Furthermore, we establish analogous filtrations for difference equations to bridge the theoretical framework with numerical analysis.

papers.title: Solvable Structures for Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric framework connecting solvable structures and integrable Hamiltonian systems. For a completely integrable Hamiltonian system with $n$ degrees of freedom, we construct a solvable structure consisting of $2n$ Hamiltonian vector fields that allows us to integrate Hamilton's equations by quadratures. Explicit expressions are derived for the associated Pfaffian forms whose integration yields both the solutions of Hamilton's equations and action-angle variables. This provides a novel interpretation of the Arnold-Liouville theorem in the context of solvable structures. We illustrate the theory by deriving explicit solutions and canonical variables of action-angle type for the open Toda lattice and the rational Calogero-Moser system.

papers.title: Amenability of group actions on compact spaces and the associated Banach algebras
papers.abstract: For a topological group $G$, amenability can be characterized by the amenability of the convolution Banach algebra $L^1(G)$. Here a Banach algebra $A$ is called amenable if every bounded derivation from $A$ into any dual--type $A$--$A$--Banach bimodule is inner. We extend this classical result to the case of discrete group actions on compact Hausdorff spaces in our main theorem Theorem 5.2. By using a Banach algebra naturally associated with the action and adopting a suitably weakened notion of amenability for Banach algebras, we obtain an analogous characterization of amenable actions. As a lemma, we also proved a fixed--point property for amenable actions in Theorem 4.4 that strengthens the theorem of Dong and Wang (2015).
papers.comments: 26 pages. Revised proof of the fixed-point theorem and new direct proof of the reverse implication of the main theorem

papers.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(Γ,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $Γ$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $Γ$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $Γ$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.
papers.comments: 40 pages, 3 figures. Minor corrections and improvements. To appear in J. Amer. Math. Soc

papers.title: Conjugate continuous-discrete projection filter via sparse-Grid quadrature
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the continuous-discrete projection filter for exponential-family manifolds with conjugate likelihoods. We first derive the local projection error of the prediction step of the continuous-discrete projection filter. We then derive the exact Bayesian update algorithm for a class of discrete measurement processes with additive Gaussian noise. To control the stiffness of the natural parameters' ordinary differential equations, we introduce a regularization method via projection to the Fisher information metric's eigenspace. Lastly, we apply the proposed method to approximate the filtering density of a modified Van der Pol oscillator problem and a coupled stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo system. The proposed projection filter shows superior performance compared to several state-of-the-art parametric continuous-discrete filtering methods.
papers.journal_ref: Systems Science & Control Engineering Volume 14, 2026 - Issue 1

papers.title: Lyapunov exponents for products of truncated orthogonal matrices
papers.abstract: We study the Lyapunov exponents for products of $N$ independent truncated Haar orthogonal matrices of size $n$. We prove that, in principle, provided that $N/n \to \infty$ , the first $k$ Lyapunov exponents are approximately independent and Gaussian in a non-asymptotic sense, where $k$ may depend on $N$ and $n$.

papers.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.

papers.title: Regular polygons
papers.abstract: The construction of regular polygons with a compass and straightedge is a well-known task and this problem has interested mathematicians for a long time. In particular, for a long time they could not answer the question of whether is it possible to construct a regular 17-gon with a compass and straightedge. C. F. Gauss solved this problem in 1796. He proved later that it is possible to construct with a compass and straightedge the regular polygons with $n=2^m n_1\cdots n_l$ sides, where $n_1,\cdots, n_l$ are different prime numbers of the form $\; n_k=2^{2^{ν_k}}+1$. P. Wantzel proved in 1837 that only these regular polygons can be constructed. Essential is here the construction of the regular polygons with $n_k=2^{2^{ν_k}}+1$ sides. The currently known prime numbers of the form $n=2^{2^ν}+1$ are $3, 5, 17, 257$ and $65537$. In the paper we present a new approach for solving this task. Among other things we analyze in detail the case of $n=65537$. J. G. Hermes announced in 1894 that he had a full description of the construction of the 65537-gon. This was the result of 10 years of work, but his text was too extensive and was never published. We show exactly and without gaps how the regular 65537-gon can be constructed.
papers.comments: The invariant setts described more accurately. It is pointed out that the solutions of the relevant quadratic equations are real values

papers.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty
papers.abstract: Motivated by inequalities in Fourier analysis, we present an improvement on the lower bound for the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane in high dimensions. Additionally, our methods can be used to match the existing Torquato-Stillinger lower bounds for the Cohn-Elkies linear program for sphere packing.

papers.title: Distribution free M-estimation
papers.abstract: The basic question of delineating those statistical problems that are solvable without making any assumptions on the underlying data distribution has long animated statistics and learning theory. This paper characterizes when a convex M-estimation or stochastic optimization problem is solvable in such an assumption-free setting, providing a precise dividing line between solvable and unsolvable problems. The conditions we identify show, perhaps surprisingly, that Lipschitz continuity of the loss being minimized is not necessary for distribution free minimization, and they are also distinct from classical characterizations of learnability in machine learning.

papers.title: An Introduction to Algebraic Combinatorics
papers.abstract: This is an introduction to algebraic combinatorics, written for a quarter-long graduate course. It starts with a rigorous introduction to formal power series with some combinatorial applications, then discusses integer partitions (proving Jacobi's triple product identity), permutations (Lehmer codes, cycles) and subtractive methods (alternating sums, cancellations and inclusion-exclusion principles, with a particular focus on sign-reversing involutions and determinants). The last chapter introduces symmetric polynomials and proves the Littlewood--Richardson rule using Bender--Knuth involutions (a la Stembridge). The appendix contains over 200 exercises (without solutions).
papers.comments: 724 pages. v2 adds a few exercises and corrects errors; also an unnecessary restriction on skew partitions is removed, and all three Newton-Girard identities are proved. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: Fractional Sobolev spaces and fractional $p$-Laplace equations on locally finite graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first define a discrete version of the fractional Laplace operator $(-Δ)^{s}$ through the heat semigroup on a stochastically complete, connected, locally finite graph. Moreover, we introduce a fractional Sobolev space, which is necessary when we study problems involving $(-Δ)^{s}$. Thirdly, we define the fractional divergence, and then give another form of $(-Δ)^s$, which leads to a formula of integration by parts. Finally, using the mountain-pass theorem and the Nehari manifold, we obtain multiplicity solutions to a discrete fractional Schrödinger equation. We caution the readers that though these existence results are well known in the continuous case, the discrete case is quite different.

papers.title: Infinite polynomial patterns in large subsets of the rational numbers
papers.abstract: Inspired by a question of Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, we prove two new results about infinite polynomial configurations in large subsets of the rational numbers. First, given a finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}$, we show that there exists an infinite set $B = \{b_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ such that $$\{b_i, b_i^2 + b_j : i < j\}$$ is monochromatic. Second, we prove that every subset of positive density in the rational numbers contains a translate of such an infinite configuration. The corresponding results in the integers are both known to be false, so our results provide natural and relatively simple examples of combinatorial structures that distinguish between the Ramsey-theoretic properties of the rational numbers and the integers. The proofs of our main results build upon methods developed in a series of papers by Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson to translate from combinatorics into dynamics, where the core of the argument reduces to understanding the behavior of certain polynomial ergodic averages. The new dynamical tools required for this analysis are a Wiener--Wintner theorem for polynomially-twisted ergodic averages in $\mathbb{Q}$-systems and a structure theorem for Abramov $\mathbb{Q}$-systems.
papers.comments: 66 pages. Includes a new section (Section 11) with counterexamples to further justify the ordering in the ordered sumset configurations. To appear in Journal de l'École Polytechnique - Mathématiques

papers.title: The Hamilton cycle space of random graphs
papers.abstract: The cycle space of a graph $G$, denoted $\mathcal{C}(G)$, is a vector space over ${\mathbb F}_2$, spanned by all incidence vectors of edge-sets of cycles of $G$. If $G$ has $n$ vertices, then $\mathcal{C}_n(G)$ denotes the subspace of $\mathcal{C}(G)$, spanned by the incidence vectors of Hamilton cycles of $G$. A classical result in the theory of random graphs asserts that for $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$, asymptotically almost surely the necessary condition $δ(G) \geq 2$ is also sufficient to ensure Hamiltonicity. Resolving a problem of Christoph, Nenadov, and Petrova, we augment this result by proving that $\mathcal{C}_n(G) = \mathcal{C}(G)$ holds asymptotically almost surely for $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$, with $n$ being odd and $p := p(n) \geq (\log n + 2 \log \log n + ω(1))/n$. That is, not only does $G$ typically have a Hamilton cycle, but its Hamilton cycles are typically rich enough to span its cycle space. It is known and easy to show that if $p := p(n) \leq (\log n + 2 \log \log n - ω(1))/n$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{C}_n(G) \neq \mathcal{C}(G)$ unless $G$ is a forest.

papers.title: Hall--Littlewood expansions of chromatic quasisymmetric functions using linked rook placements
papers.abstract: In this work, we obtain a Hall--Littlewood expansion of the chromatic quasisymmetric function arising from a natural unit interval order and describe the coefficients in terms of linked rook placements. Applying the Carlsson--Mellit relation between chromatic quasisymmetric functions and unicellular LLT polynomials, we also obtain a combinatorial description for the coefficients of the unicellular LLT polynomials expanded in terms of the modified transformed Hall--Littlewood polynomials.

papers.title: Exact Solutions to the Klein--Gordon Equation via Reduction Algebras
papers.abstract: Reduction algebras (also known as generalized Mickelsson algebras, Zhelobenko algebras, or transvector algebras) are well-studied associative algebras appearing in the representation theory of Lie algebras. In the 1990s, Zhelobenko noted that reduction algebras have a connection to field equations from physics, whereas Howe's study of dual pairs in the 1980s signifies that the link originated even earlier. In this paper, we revisit the simplest case of a massless scalar field, in arbitrary spacetime dimension $n\ge 3$ and arbitrary flat metric $η_{ab}$; the field equation then specializes to the Laplace equation and to the massless Klein--Gordon equation. The relevant reduction algebra comes from a representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (technically, $\mathfrak{sp}_2$) by differential operators. We give a complete presentation of this reduction algebra. Its raising operators produce bosonic states $|a_1a_2\cdots a_\ell\rangle$, polynomial solutions of degree $\ell$ to the field equation, and we show that the natural bilinear form on these states is computed by symmetrizers built from the rational dynamical R-matrix. Along the way we give explicit formulas for the states, and a self-contained proof, for a general metric, of Zhelobenko's results that they span the polynomial solutions and that the solution space is an irreducible module over the reduction algebra.
papers.comments: v2: corrected Theorem 3.22 and examples; relation to Zhelobenko's work clarified; revised introduction; minor corrections. 20 pages

papers.title: The Balmer spectrum of integral permutation modules
papers.abstract: We study the Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules of a finite group over a commutative Noetherian ring. In this generality, we obtain a set-theoretic description of the spectrum. Under certain mild additional assumptions on the base ring, we describe its topology by reducing the problem first to the modular locus and then to the case of elementary abelian groups. Furthermore, we introduce a twisted cohomology ring in this context, which allows us to realize the spectrum, in the case of elementary abelian $p$-groups, as a Dirac scheme. This extends recent work of Balmer and Gallauer from the setting of ground fields to the more general setting of commutative Noetherian rings.
papers.comments: V2: several arguments that were based on an erroneous construction have been corrected; 39 pages; comments welcome

papers.title: Dirac reduction algebra
papers.abstract: There is a homomorphism of associative superalgebras from the enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to the Weyl-Clifford superalgebra $A(2n|n)$ with $2n$ even Weyl algebra generators and $n$ odd Clifford algebra generators. Under this homomorphism, the positive odd root vector $x\in\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is sent to the Dirac operator $γ^μ\partial_μ\in A(2n|n)$ and generates a left ideal $I$. The corresponding reduction (super)algebra, denoted $Z_n$, is the normalizer of $I$ in $A(2n|n)$ modulo $I$. By construction, $Z_n$ acts on the space of all Clifford algebra-valued polynomial solutions to the (massless) Dirac equation. This setting goes back to Zhelobenko, who described generators of this reduction algebra and commutation relations among them. In this paper, we find a complete presentation of (a localization of) this so-termed Dirac reduction algebra, with full proofs. We give a closed formula for products of the raising operators in the reduction algebra and use it to write down explicitly the polynomial solutions to the Dirac equation in $n$-dimensional flat spacetime that they generate. Finally, we show that for $n\neq 2$ the space of polynomial solutions is irreducible over the reduction algebra tensored with the opposite Clifford algebra when $n$ is even, and is a direct sum of two irreducible submodules when $n$ is odd.
papers.comments: v2: corrected Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2; irreducibility (Theorem 7.5) extended to odd n; relation to Zhelobenko's work clarified; minor corrections. 33 pages

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Decentralized Stochastic Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We study decentralized stochastic nonconvex Polyak--Łojasiewicz minimax problems. Motivated by local SGD in federated learning, we improve communication efficiency by allowing agents to perform several local updates before the communication stage. Existing work gives a communication bound of $\mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{κ^3\varepsilon^{-2}}{(1-λ)^2}\Big)$ for local decentralized gradient descent--ascent using $\mathcal{O}\Big(\varepsilon^{-2}+\frac{κ^2\varepsilon^{-2}}{K(1-λ)}\Big)$ local updates per round. Here $\varepsilon$ is the target accuracy, $1-λ$ is the spectral gap and $κ\ge1$ is the condition number. However, too many local updates can leave available communication resources underused and increase local drift, as agents follow their own objectives for longer before exchanging information. We therefore pursue improved communication efficiency while keeping the number of local steps small. To this end, we propose DiMA, a structured local--global learning strategy that uses local updates to build an accelerated momentum and perform decentralized learning through either standard gossip or accelerated mixing. By exploiting the positive semidefiniteness of the mixing matrix, we derive complexity bounds for DiMA under different updating strategies. Experiments on robust logistic regression demonstrate improved performance over several existing baselines.

papers.title: Finite element conformal complexes in three dimensions
papers.abstract: This paper develops three-dimensional finite element conformal Hessian and conformal elasticity complexes through a local-bubble Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand (BGG) construction parameterized by smoothness vectors. These complexes incorporate higher-order differential operators, including the linearized Cotton-York operator, and require conformal tensor spaces (i.e., symmetric and traceless tensor spaces) with nontrivial smoothness and trace conditions. We apply the discrete BGG framework at the level of local bubble complexes parameterized by vertex, edge, and face smoothness vectors, together with geometric bubble decompositions and a reduction operation. This yields exact bubble complexes over explicit admissible regularity ranges, together with the face-bubble exactness needed to assemble families of global conforming complexes with varying vertex, edge, and face smoothness. The construction recovers known conformal Hessian and conformal elasticity complexes as particular choices, while producing broader smoothness-parameterized families, including new exact conformal elasticity complexes with strictly weaker interelement continuity. The resulting complexes provide structure-preserving finite element building blocks for applications in relativity, Cosserat elasticity, and fluid mechanics.

papers.title: Distributed Constraint-coupled Resource Allocation: Anytime Feasibility and Violation Robustness
papers.abstract: This paper considers distributed resource allocation problems (DRAPs) with a coupled constraint for real-time systems. Based on primal-dual methods, we adopt a control perspective for optimization algorithm design by synthesizing a safe feedback controller using control barrier functions to enforce constraint satisfaction. On this basis, a distributed anytime-feasible resource allocation (DanyRA) algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the DanyRA algorithm converges to the exact optimal solution of DRAPs while preserving feasibility of the coupled inequality constraint from a feasible initialization. To address constraint violations caused by external disturbances, we develop a recover-after-violation mechanism using a virtual queue with a minimum buffer, enabling feasibility recovery within a prescribed number of iterations. We characterize the trade-off between convergence accuracy and violation robustness for a fixed positive buffer and establish exact convergence with a suitably decaying buffer. DanyRA is further specialized to coupled equality constraints, with constraint preservation and an explicit linear convergence rate established.
