Finally, a numerical example is provided for verification.

papers.title: Validity and Power of Heavy-Tailed Combination Tests under Asymptotic Dependence
papers.abstract: Heavy-tailed combination tests, such as the Cauchy combination test and harmonic mean p-value method, are widely used for testing global null hypotheses by aggregating dependent p-values. Existing theoretical guarantees, however, are largely restricted to the case of asymptotically independent p-values, leaving the behavior of these tests under broader dependence structures poorly understood. We develop a unified framework based on multivariate regularly varying copulas, a flexible class defined by a mild regularity condition on the joint behavior of p-values near zero, that accommodates a wide range of dependence structures. Within this framework, heavy-tailed combination tests are asymptotically valid when the transformation distribution has tail index $γ\leq 1$, with $γ= 1$ maximizing power while preserving validity. We further show that combination tests with $γ= 1$ achieve strictly greater asymptotic power than Bonferroni's method if and only if the p-values are not asymptotically independent and signals are not extremely sparse, with the power advantage growing as dependence strengthens. Bonferroni emerges as the $γ\to 0$ limit and becomes overly conservative under asymptotic dependence. These results provide theoretical support for using truncated Cauchy or Pareto combination tests, offering a principled approach to enhance power while controlling false positives under complex dependence.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in The Annals of Statistics. This revision adds an example on overlapping gene-set tests and updates the supplementary material

papers.title: Shintani invariants and cyclic quantum dilogarithms
papers.abstract: We express general Shintani invariants of real quadratic number fields in terms of cyclic quantum dilogarithms, which appear in the asymptotic expansion of $q$-Pochhammer symbols. We also explain how a formula from 1995 of Sczech for Shintani invariants can naturally be understood in this framework.

papers.title: Fractional domatic number and minimum degree
papers.abstract: The domatic number of a graph $G$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dominating sets of $G$. We are interested in the LP-relaxation of this parameter, which is called the fractional domatic number of $G$. We study its extremal value in the class of graphs of minimum degree $d$. The fractional domatic number of a graph of minimum degree $d$ is always at most $d+1$, and at least $(1-o(1))\, d/\ln d$ as $d\to \infty$. This is asymptotically tight even within the class of split graphs. Our main result concerns the case $d=2$; we show that, excluding $8$ exceptional graphs, the fractional domatic number of every connected graph of minimum degree (at least) $2$ is at least $5/2$. We also show that this bound cannot be improved if only finitely many graphs are excluded, even for bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth. This proves in a stronger sense a conjecture by Gadouleau, Harms, Mertzios, and Zamaraev (2024). This also extends and generalises results from McCuaig and Shepherd (1989), from Fujita, Kameda, and Yamashita (2000), and from Abbas, Egerstedt, Liu, Thomas, and Whalen (2016). Finally, we show that graphs of sub-exponential expansion and sufficiently large girth $g$ have fractional domatic number $3 - o_g(1)$.

papers.title: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 1 figure. Changes include the title, formulation of Conjecture 1 and Theorem 1(b) and proof of Theorem 1

papers.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
papers.abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
papers.comments: Added Remark 1.2. All comments are welcome

papers.title: Large scale dynamical response of interacting $1d$ Fermi systems
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of a class of weakly interacting, gapless $1d$ fermionic systems, in presence of small external perturbations slowly varying in space and in time. We consider the evolution of the expectation values of the charge density and of the current density, in the thermodynamic limit and for low enough temperatures. We prove the validity and the asymptotic exactness of linear response in the limit of vanishing space-time variation of the perturbation, and we provide the explicit expression of the response of the system. The proof relies on the representation of the real time Duhamel expansion in terms of Euclidean correlation functions, for which we provide sharp estimates using rigorous renormalization group methods. The asymptotic exactness of linear response holds thanks to a cancellation for the scaling limit of the correlations that is reminiscent of bosonization, and which is derived rigorously using emergent chiral Ward identities.

papers.title: A Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation for Automated Aircraft Arrival Routing and Scheduling
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing dynamic arrival routes (DARs) in a terminal maneuvering area (TMA) together with an automated scheduling of all the arrivals within a given time interval. DARs are aircraft arrival routes from all entry points of a TMA, which merge traffic in that time interval towards the runway, and are modeled as energy-efficient continuous-descent operations, such that separation based on wake-turbulence categories is guaranteed within the TMA. We propose a new model based on a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation of a previous model for this problem. As in the previous model, we include tree consistency across consecutive planning intervals. However, the reformulation enables us to further improve the model and also consider aircraft that remain in the TMA from the previous period, a feature critical for operational safety. In computational experiments for Stockholm Arlanda airport, the new model consistently outperforms the previous one: we obtain solutions within 5 seconds to 12.65 minutes compared to up tp 40.9 hours with the old model for instances of half hours with high traffic. In addition, we are able to solve instances of a full hour of arriving aircraft with high traffic (33 aircraft) within 22.22 to 58.57 minutes, whereas the old model could not solve these instances at all. While we schedule all aircraft as continuous-descent arrivals, our model can be applied to any type of speed profiles for the arriving aircraft.

papers.title: Bézout's theorem for abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X$, $Y$ be closed irreducible subvarieties of an absolutely simple abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field. If $\dim(X) + \dim(Y) \le g$, we prove that the addition morphism $X \times Y \to X + Y$ is semismall. As a consequence, we deduce that if $\dim(X) + \dim(Y) \ge g$, the subvarieties $X$ and $Y$ must meet (Bézout's theorem). If we drop the assumption that the abelian variety is absolutely simple, we prove that Bézout's theorem still holds if $X$ satisfies a nondegeneracy condition. These results were previously known only in characteristic zero. Our proof of the semismallness statement is based on the theory of perverse sheaves: using results of Krämer and Weissauer, we prove that for perverse sheaves $K$ supported on $X$, and $L$ supported on $Y$, the convolution product $K * L$ is again perverse.
papers.comments: Corrected version, 20 pages. To appear in Crelle's journal

papers.title: Dynamical feedback control with operator learning for the Vlasov-Poisson system
papers.abstract: To meet the demands of instantaneous control of instabilities over long time horizons in plasma fusion, we design a dynamic feedback control strategy for the Vlasov-Poisson system by constructing an operator that maps state perturbations to an external control field. In the first part of the paper, we propose learning such an operator using a neural network. Inspired by optimal control theory for linearized dynamics, we introduce a low-rank neural operator architecture and train it via adjoint state method. The resulting controller is effective at suppressing instabilities well beyond the training time horizon. To generalize control across varying initial data, we further introduce a novel cancellation-based control strategy that removes the destabilizing component of the electric field. This approach naturally defines an operator without requiring any training, ensures perturbation decay over infinite time, and demonstrates strong robustness under noisy feedback. Numerical experiments confirm the effectiveness of the method in both one- and multidimensional settings.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions to the unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes Equation
papers.abstract: The nonuniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions to the unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes equations is one of the central open problems in mathematical fluid dynamics. In this paper, we provide, to our knowledge, the first rigorous computer-assisted proof demonstrating such nonuniqueness. Inspired by earlier works in this area, we construct a Leray-Hopf solution in the self-similar setting and then establish the existence of a second solution by analyzing the stability of the linearized operator around this profile, showing that it corresponds to an unstable perturbation. To achieve this, we develop an innovative numerical method that computes candidate solutions with high precision and propose a framework for rigorously establishing exact solutions in a neighborhood of these candidates. A key step is to decompose the linearized operator into a coercive part plus a compact perturbation, which is further approximated by a finite-rank operator up to a small error. The invertibility of the linearized operator restricted to the image of this finite-rank approximation is then rigorously verified using computer-assisted proofs. This certifies the existence of an unstable eigenpair and, consequently, yields a second solution - indeed, infinitely many Leray-Hopf solutions.

papers.title: Flexible fixed-point iteration and its applications for nonsymmetric algebraic Riccati equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we reveal the intrinsic Toeplitz structure in the unique stabilizing solution for nonsymmetric algebraic Riccati equations by employing a shift-involved fixed-point iteration, and propose an RADI-type method for computing this solution for large-scale equations of this type with sparse and low-rank structure by incorporating flexible shifts into the fixed-point iteration. We present a shift-selection strategy, termed Leja shifts, based on rational approximation theory, which is incorporated into the RADI-type method. We further discuss important implementation aspects for the method, such as low-rank factorization of residuals, implicit update of large-scale sparse matrices, real arithmetics with complex shifts, and related equations of other type. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficiency of both the proposed method and the introduced shift-selection strategy.

papers.title: Kapranov $L_{\infty}[1]$ algebras
papers.abstract: Given any Kähler manifold $X$, Kapranov discovered a nontrivial $L_\infty[1]$ algebra structure on $Ω^{0,\bullet}_{X}(T^{1,0}X)$. Motivated by this result, we introduce the notion of an $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra, generalizing $L_\infty[1]$ algebras, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is a differential graded commutative algebra with unit. We extend standard notions such as quasi-isomorphism and linearization to this setting and establish a linearization theorem. As an application, we prove that any DG Lie algebroid $(\mathcal{L},Q_{\mathcal{L}})$ over a DG manifold $(\mathcal{M},Q)$ induces a distinguished isomorphism class of $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures on $Γ(\mathcal{L})$, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is the DG commutative algebra $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}),Q)$. Their unary bracket is $Q_{\mathcal{L}}$, while their binary bracket is a cocycle representative of the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid. All these isomorphic $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures are $\mathfrak{R}$-linearizable if and only if the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid vanishes. In contrast, the induced $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathbb{K}$-algebra structures on $Γ(\mathcal{L})$ are necessarily $\mathbb{K}$-linearizable, hence $\mathbb{K}$-homotopy abelian.
papers.comments: (26 pages) A new proof of the linearization theorem simplifies Section 2. To appear in Communications in Mathematical Physics

papers.title: Effective Dynamics for Weakly Interacting Bosons in an Iterated High-Density Thermodynamic Limit
papers.abstract: We study the time evolution of weakly interacting Bose gases on a three-dimensional torus of arbitrary volume. The coupling constant is supposed to be inversely proportional to the density, which is considered to be large and independent of the particle number. We take into account a class of initial states exhibiting quasi-complete Bose-Einstein condensation. For each fixed time in a finite interval, we prove the convergence of the one-particle reduced density matrix towards the projection onto the normalised order parameter describing the condensate - evolving according to the Hartree equation - in the iterated limit where the volume (and therefore the particle number), and subsequently the density go to infinity. The rate of convergence depends only on the density and on the decay of both the expected number of particles and the energy of the initial quasi-vacuum state.
papers.comments: 72 pages; Generalisation of the result - Accepted revision to appear in Annales Henri Poincaré

papers.title: Moments of the zeros of Faber polynomials of the Miller basis
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of modular forms in the Miller basis, a natural basis for the space of modular forms. We show that the zeros of their Faber polynomials have linear moments. By analyzing the moments we can extend the known range of the forms in the Miller basis for which at least one of the zeros is not on the arc - the circular part of the boundary of the fundamental domain. Additionally, for forms in the Miller basis of an index asymptotically linear in the weight such that all zeros are on the arc, we compute the limit distribution of the zeros, which depends on the asymptotic ratio of the index to the weight.

papers.title: Exploring the Scaling Crossover of Generalized Jeffreys-Type Law: Stochastic Modeling, Analysis, and High-Accuracy Numerical Computation
papers.abstract: The generalized Jeffreys-type law is formulated as a multi-term time-fractional Jeffreys-type equation (MT-TFJE), whose dynamics exhibit rich scaling crossover phenomena associated with different diffusion mechanisms. In this work, we provide a microscopic stochastic interpretation of the MT-TFJE through a continuous-time random walk (CTRW) framework with a generalized waiting-time distribution, elucidating the physical mechanisms underlying the scaling crossover. Based on the Laplace-Volterra formulation and spectral analysis, we establish the well-posedness and stability of the MT-TFJE and derive Sobolev regularity estimates under appropriate assumptions on the initial data and source term. We further develop a high-accuracy numerical scheme, termed CIM-CLG, which combines a contour integral method for temporal approximation with the Chebyshev-Legendre Galerkin method for spatial discretization. The proposed method achieves exponential temporal convergence under the stated regularity of the governing equation, together with high-order spatial accuracy. The temporal approximation involves $\mathcal{O}(N)$ independent contour evaluations, where $N$ is the number of contour points, while the FFT-based transforms have a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(M^n\log M)$ for spatial dimensions $n=1,2$, with $M$ denoting the number of modes per spatial dimension. The resulting algorithm is naturally parallelizable. Detailed implementation procedures and rigorous error estimates are presented. Extensive numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate the efficiency, accuracy, and robustness of the proposed method, providing a computationally effective framework for generalized nonlocal diffusion problems.
papers.comments: 48pages. This paper has been accepted and will be published soon in Vol. 30 (2027), at https://link.springer.com/journal/13540/

papers.title: Differential Equations for Macdonald's Hypergeometric Series
papers.abstract: We study differential equations for certain multivariable hypergeometric series, introduced by Macdonald in the 1980s, which generalize hypergeometric functions of matrix argument due to Bochner and Herz. Such equations are well studied in the one-variable case, where they serve to characterize the classical hypergeometric functions $_p F_q(z)$ and provide a route to many of their key properties. Accordingly, Macdonald asked for a similar characterization for the multivariate series. This problem, however, has remained open. Differential equations are known only for a handful of cases with $p\leq 3$ and $q\leq 2$. In this paper we give a complete solution to Macdonald's problem. In the multivariable case there are \emph{two} series $_p F_q(x)$ and $_p F_q(x,y)$, depending on $p+q+1$ parameters and one or two sets of variables, $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$. We give differential equations characterizing both series, for all values of $p$ and $q$. The proof involves several new ideas in the theory of symmetric functions, especially Jack polynomials and interpolation polynomials.
papers.comments: v2: Revised the title and abstract and expanded the introduction. Clarified the proof of Theorem B, corrected several formulas, and updated the references. 38 pages

papers.title: TWIN: Two window inspection for online change point detection
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of sequential change point tests based on two-window inspection (TWIN). TWIN scans for changes by comparing symmetric subsamples of data and combining them in a weighted maximum, similar to Levy's modulus of continuity. The TWIN detector generally admits a Gaussian approximation, which becomes an above-threshold approximation at Levy's critical weight. For this weight, the detector achieves rate-optimal detection delays. We present a version of TWIN for detecting mean changes and establish convergence even for weakly dependent data taking values in a separable Banach space. We also discuss the detection of general distributional changes. Controlling the Levy modulus of continuity of partial sum processes typically requires subgaussian data. However, we show that this requirement can be circumvented by an adaptive version of TWIN that requires only finite moments of low order. The adaptation is based on a data-dependent clock, that can be motivated by the Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz theorem. Simulations and an application to monitoring COVID-19 data illustrate the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: On the Least Colossally Abundant Exception to Robin's Inequality
papers.abstract: Robin's Inequality posits $G(n)<e^γ$ for $n>5040$. Robin also showed that if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is false, then $G(n)>e^γ\left(1+\displaystyle\frac{c}{(\log n)^{b}}\right)$ for infinitely many values of $n$. By analyzing the prime or semiprime quotient $\displaystyle\frac{n}{m}$ for consecutive Colossally Abundant (CA) numbers $m$ followed by $n$ (where $m$ satisfies Robin's Inequality and $n$ violates it), we demonstrate that if the Riemann Hypothesis is false, then the least CA counterexample, $n$, must be constrained to the band $e^γ<G(n)<e^γ\left(1+\displaystyle\frac{c}{(\log n)^b}\right)$ where $0 < b < 1/2$ and $c\ge\displaystyle\frac{2\operatorname{gpf}(m)+1}{\operatorname{gpf}(m)^{2}}(\log n)^{b}$, i.e. for $c$ satisfying this lower bound, excluded from the infinite set beyond the higher threshold. The lower bound on $c$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.
papers.comments: 8 pages. v2: The main theorem is proved with an exact bound on the ratio of abundancy indices of consecutive CA numbers and states an explicit lower bound for $c$ in terms of $\operatorname{gpf}(m)$. The lower bound on $c$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$. Corrected $e^γ< G(n)$ to $e^γ\le G(n)$. Unused results and references removed. Citations corrected, Morrill and Platt bound updated

papers.title: A Semi-Lagrangian Adaptive Rank (SLAR) Method for High-Dimensional Vlasov Dynamics
papers.abstract: We extend our previous work on a semi-Lagrangian adaptive rank (SLAR) integrator, in the finite difference framework for nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson systems, to the general high-order tensor setting. The proposed scheme retains the high-order accuracy of semi-Lagrangian methods, ensuring stability for large time steps and avoiding dimensional splitting errors. The primary contribution of this paper is the novel extension of the algorithm from the matrix to the high-dimensional tensor setting, which enables the simulation of Vlasov models in up to six dimensions. The key technical components include (1) a third-order high-dimensional polynomial reconstruction that scales as $O(d^2)$, providing a point-wise approximation of the solution at the foot of characteristics in a semi-Lagrangian scheme; (2) a recursive hierarchical adaptive cross approximation of high-order tensors in a hierarchical Tucker format, characterized by a tensor tree; (3) a low-complexity Poisson solver in the hierarchical Tucker format that leverages the FFT for efficiency. The computed adaptive rank kinetic solutions exhibit low-rank structures within branches of the tensor tree resulting in substantial computational savings in both storage and time. The resulting algorithm achieves a computational complexity of $O(d^4 N r^{3+\lceil\log_2d\rceil})$, where $N$ is the number of grid points per dimension, $d$ is the problem dimension, and $r$ is the maximum rank in the tensor tree, overcoming the curse of dimensionality. Through extensive numerical tests, we demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm and highlight its ability to capture complex solution structures while maintaining a computational complexity that scales linearly with $N$.

papers.title: Fine-grained deterministic hardness of the shortest vector problem
papers.abstract: Let $γ$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ be the decision version of the shortest vector problem in the $\ell_p$-norm with approximation factor $γ$, let $n$ be the lattice rank and $0<\varepsilon\leq 1$. We prove that there is no algorithm that solves $(2-\varepsilon)$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ uniformly for all $p\in\mathbb{N}$ in time\[ 2^{2^{o(p)}}\cdot 2^{o(n)},\] unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false. The proof is based on a deterministic Karp reduction from a constrained variant of the subset-sum problem to $\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ for fixed $p$. While most hardness results for the shortest vector problem in finite norms rely on randomized reductions, our method is entirely deterministic. As a consequence, we also obtain a deterministic Karp reduction from the standard subset-sum problem to $(2-\varepsilon)$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_{\infty}$.
papers.comments: 16 pages. v4: Extended introduction and more details in some arguments

papers.title: Classification of fractional, singular Yamabe metrics on a twice punctured sphere I
papers.abstract: The Delaunay metrics form a family of conformally flat, constant fractional Q-curvature metrics on a twice-punctured sphere. They are all (after a Möbius transformation) rotationally symmetric and periodic, and admit several elegant variational descriptions. We prove that, when s is close to but less than 1, any complete, conformally flat constant Q-curvature metric on a twice-punctured sphere is a Delaunay metric. Along the way, we prove a sharp a priori bound for the conformal factor of these metrics, which may be of independent interest.
papers.comments: V3: 27 pages. Previous versions had a gap in the proof of the sharp a priori bound. The present version circumvents this gap by first proving an a priori bound that is independent of s, and then using this bound to prove Cauchy uniqueness of solutions: if two solutions agree to first order at a point then they must coincide

papers.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded commutative algebras
papers.abstract: We call a standard graded commutative $\Bbbk$-algebra \textit{cyclotomic} if its $h$-polynomial has all its roots on the unit circle in the complex plane. Complete intersections provide typical examples of cyclotomic algebras, since the $h$-polynomial of any standard graded complete intersection is a product of polynomials of the form $1 + t + \cdots + t^{m-1}$. We refer to such polynomials as being \textit{of type CI}. A natural question is whether there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra whose $h$-polynomial is not of type CI. In this paper, we give a partial answer to this question. We show that the $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ of a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ is of type CI whenever $h_R(1) \in \{1, 4, 6\}$ or $h_R(1)$ is prime. On the other hand, if $n$ is a composite integer with $n \geq 8$, then there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ whose $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ is not of type CI and satisfies $h_R(1) = n$.

papers.title: Tensor ideals of abelian type and quantum groups
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of tensor ideals in linear rigid monoidal categories that are kernels of linear monoidal functors to abelian monoidal categories. We develop general methods and apply them to the category of tilting modules over quantum groups as well as to some representation categories of finite groups. In an appendix on Duflo involutions in monoidal categories, we make a connection between Duflo involutions in the affine Weyl group and tensor ideals for quantum groups, and prove some of Lusztig's conjectures for arbitrary Coxeter groups, at equal parameters, without invoking the boundedness hypothesis.

papers.title: A Riemannian Generalization of Wilks' Lambda for Testing Differences Among Brain Connectomes
papers.abstract: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) for grouped samples whose observations take values in a space with nontrivial geometric structure, either a differentiable manifold or a non-Euclidean metric space, is a problem that has received attention in recent years. This paper is concerned with brain connectomes. Functional data analysis is another important motivation. Most of the literature relies on approaches that assume very little about the geometric structure. The most prominent example is Fréchet ANOVA, a method that is valid in metric spaces under relatively weak hypotheses. We argue that the generality of these approaches has a price in statistical power. We propose an ANOVA test on the space of symmetric positive definite matrices with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric that exploits features specific to that space. The test is not easy to generalize to other settings, but we show that there is a notable difference in power relative to Fréchet ANOVA. We show it theoretically, by characterizing the asymptotic behavior of both tests for alternatives close to the null hypothesis. We also show it in practice, by describing the specific consequences of that difference for the analysis of brain imaging studies whose design involves collecting samples at multiple sites.

papers.title: BMO solvability with singular drifts on ample sawtooth domains implies $L^p$ solvability
papers.abstract: For a linear elliptic operator with a singular drift that satisfies a finite Carleson measure condition, we prove that there exist `ample' sawtooth domains of the unit ball $B(0,1)\subset \R^{n+1}$ so that a BMO solvability assumption in these sawtooth subdomains implies that the elliptic measure satisfies the weak $A_\infty$ condition with respect to the surface measure on this `ample' sawtooth domain. This is a quantifiable absolute continuity condition, which is equivalent to saying the $L^p$ Dirichlet problem is solvable for some $1<p<\infty$. Such singular drifts have been considered in the literature in the context of perturbative $L^p$ Dirichlet solvability problems, by Hofmann-Lewis and Kenig-Pipher. By an ample sawtooth domain, we mean a sawtooth domain whose boundary coincides with the boundary of the unit ball, except for an arbitrarily small fraction. The methods can be naturally extended to show the result for more general bounded Lipschitz domains.

papers.title: Some error estimates for semidiscrete finite element approximations of stable solutions to mean field game systems
papers.abstract: We derive a priori error estimates for semidiscrete finite element approximations of stable solutions to time-dependent mean field game systems with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Expressing solutions to the MFG system as zeros of a nonlinear abstract mapping, we show that the stability of solutions is equivalent to the invertibility of its differential. This characterization allows us to apply the Brezzi-Rappaz-Raviart approximation theorem in combination with discrete L^p maximal regularity estimates to prove existence of solutions to the semidiscrete MFG system and to derive the error estimate. Finally, for solutions satisfying sufficient regularity assumptions, we establish quasi-optimal error bounds, meaning the approximation achieves the best possible convergence rate when the solution has sufficient smoothness.

papers.title: Shallow-water convergence of the intermediate long wave equation in $L^2$
papers.abstract: We continue our study on the convergence issue of the intermediate long wave equation (ILW) on both the real line and the circle. In particular, we establish convergence of the scaled ILW dynamics to that of the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) in the shallow-water limit at the $L^2$-level. Together with the recent work by the first three authors and D. Pilod (2024) on the deep-water convergence in $L^2$, this work completes the well-posedness and convergence study of ILW on both geometries within the $L^2$-framework. Our proof equally applies to both geometries and is based on the following two ingredients: the complete integrability of ILW and the normal form method. More precisely, by making use of the Lax pair structure and the perturbation determinant for ILW, recently introduced by Harrop-Griffths, Killip, and Vişan (2026), we first establish weakly uniform (in small depth parameters) equicontinuity in $L^2$ of solutions to the scaled ILW, providing a control on the high frequency part of solutions. Then, we treat the low frequency part by implementing a perturbative argument based on an infinite iteration of normal form reductions for KdV.
papers.comments: 51 pages. We corrected an error in Section 4 and made minor updates. To appear in Proc. Lond. Math. Soc

papers.title: Anelastic approximation for the degenerate compressible Navier--Stokes equations revisited
papers.abstract: In this paper we revisit the joint low-Mach and low-Froude number limit for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations with degenerate, density-dependent viscosity. Employing the relative entropy framework based on the concept of kappa-entropy, we rigorously justify the convergence of weak solutions toward the generalized anelastic system in a three-dimensional periodic domain for well-prepared initial data. For general ill-prepared initial data, we establish high Reynolds convergence to the anelastic Euler system in the whole space, relying essentially on dispersive estimates for acoustic waves. Compared with the work of Fanelli and Zatorska [Commun. Math. Phys., 400 (2023), pp. 1463--1506], our analysis is conducted for the standard isentropic pressure law, thereby eliminating the need for the cold pressure term that played a crucial role in the previous approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first rigorous singular limit result for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with degenerate viscosity that requires no additional regularization of the system.

papers.title: Two energy methods for distributed port-Hamiltonian systems and their application to stability analysis
papers.abstract: We develop two local energy methods for distributed parameter port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems on one-dimensional spatial domains. The methods are applied to derive a characterization of exponential stability directly in terms of the energy passing through the boundary over a given time horizon. The resulting condition is verified for a network of vibrating strings where existing sufficient conditions cannot be applied. Moreover, we use a local energy method to study the short-time behavior of pH systems with boundary damping which was recently studied in the context of hypocoercivity.

papers.title: Minimally tough series-parallel graphs with toughness at least $1/2$
papers.abstract: Let $t$ be a positive real number. A graph is called \emph{$t$-tough} if the removal of any vertex set $S$ that disconnects the graph leaves at most $|S|/t$ components. The toughness of a graph is the largest $t$ for which the graph is $t$-tough. A graph is minimally $t$-tough if the toughness of the graph is $t$, and the deletion of any edge from the graph decreases the toughness. Series--parallel graphs are graphs with two distinguished vertices called terminals, formed recursively by two simple composition operations, series and parallel joins. They can be used to model series and parallel electric circuits. We characterize minimally $t$-tough series--parallel graphs for all $t\ge 1/2$. It is clear that there is no minimally $t$-tough series--parallel graph if $t>1$. We show that, for $1\ge t >1/2$, most of the series--parallel graphs with toughness $t$ are minimally $t$-tough, but most of the series--parallel graphs with toughness $1/2$ are not minimally $1/2$-tough.

papers.title: Seshadri Regions and the Asymptotic Shape of Multigraded Regularity
papers.abstract: We introduce the Seshadri region of a subvariety, a convex region packaging the classical Seshadri constants with respect to every line bundle simultaneously. We develop the theory of Seshadri regions as a measure of positivity along subvarieties and apply it to determine asymptotic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for ideal powers and symmetric powers on smooth projective toric varieties.

papers.title: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
papers.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, Vol. 230 (2026)

papers.title: The 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups
papers.abstract: We determine the 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups over S^4.
papers.comments: 16 pages, accepted for publication in Proc. Amer. Math. Soc

papers.title: A Weaker Notion of Atomicity in Integral Domains
papers.abstract: A nonzero element of an integral domain $D$ is called \emph{atomic} if it is a unit or can be written as a finite product of irreducible elements of $D$, and $D$ is called \emph{atomic} if every nonzero element of $D$ is atomic. Here, we introduce and study a weaker notion of atomicity, which relaxes the requirement that all elements admit a factorization into irreducibles. Namely, we say that an integral domain is \emph{sub-atomic} if every divisor of an atomic element is also atomic. Then, we investigate the basic properties of such domains, provide examples, and explore the behavior of the sub-atomic property under standard constructions such as localization and $D+M$ constructions. In particular, we prove that the sub-atomic property ascends to polynomial rings in the class of GL-domains. Our results highlight the independence of the sub-atomic property from other classical factorization properties, and it forms an important class of integral domains lying between atomic and antimatter domains (i.e., domains without atoms).

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. I
papers.abstract: This paper is the first in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. The Cullis' determinant is defined for every matrix of size $n\times k$, where $n \ge k \ge 1$ and is equal to the ordinary determinant if $n = k$. In this paper we solve the linear preserver problem for the Cullis' determinant for $k \ge 4, n \ge k + 2$ and $n + k$ is even. It appears that in this case all linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant are non-singular and could be represented by two-sided matrix multiplication. Note that the cases where $n = k$ or $n = k + 1$ admit slightly different description allowing (sub)matrix transposition and were completely studied before: the case where $n = k$ is a classical linear preserver problem for the ordinary determinant and was solved by Frobenius; the complete characterisation for the case where $n = k + 1$ was obtained in the previous paper by the authors.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. II
papers.abstract: This paper is the second in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we solve the linear preserver problem for the Cullis' determinant defined on the spaces of matrices of size $n\times k$ with $k \ge 4,\; n \ge k + 2$ and $n + k$ is odd. In comparison with the case when $n + k$ is even, in this case linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant could be singular and are represented as a sum of two linear maps: first is two-sided matrix multiplication and second is any linear map whose image consists of matrices, all rows of which are equal.

papers.title: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
papers.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.
papers.comments: 19 pages; made some further corrections and clarifications, and added Lemma 4.4 (stating that connected components of single-bubble isoperimetric minimizers have disjoint boundaries) for completeness

papers.title: Explicit analytic functions defining the images of simple wave-front singularities
papers.abstract: We construct explicit main-analytic functions for the images of the standard maps associated with simple wave-front singularities of types $A$, $D$, and $E$. The construction uses resultants of explicitly specified pairs of one-variable polynomials whose coefficients are expressed directly in the target coordinates of the standard maps. For types $A$ and $D$, it recovers one-variable discriminant representations. Using this, we give direct proofs of sharp bounds on the number of preimages of the standard map for types $A$ and $D$. For each of the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, there exists an additional square factor in the resultant. Removing this factor gives the corresponding main-analytic function.

papers.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for high dimensional Central Limit Theorem under moment conditions
papers.abstract: We characterize the dimension growth rate in the high dimensional central limit theorems (or CLTs) over hyper-rectangles. First, we find out the moment conditions that are both necessary and sufficient under the independence of the components. We consider four exhaustive classes, viz. when underlying random variables (I) have all polynomial moments, (II) have some polynomial moment of order higher than two, (III) have only second moment but no polynomial moment higher than two exists, and (IV) have infinite second moment, but belong to the domain of attraction of normal distribution. Next, we extend the sufficiency of the moment conditions in the Gaussian approximations of each of the aforementioned classes with same moment assumptions when the coordinates are dependent. For sub-Weibull marginals in Class (I), with $0<α\le1/6$, strong non-degeneracy yields the optimal range $\log p=o(n^{2α})$ which matches the rate obtained under coordinate-wise independence. However under marginal non-degeneracy, a Berry--Esseen bound gives the exponent $2α/(1+4α)$ up to logarithmic factors, and a counterexample proves that this exponent is optimal under marginal non-degeneracy. Under marginal non-degeneracy, Class (II) admits polynomial dimension growth up to logarithmic factors, while in Class (III) the marginal tails determine a growth rate, both of which again match with that when the coordinates are independent. In Class (IV), coordinate-wise normalization by truncated second moments yields a high dimensioonal CLT under additional tail and covariance conditions. Thus, we derive necessary and sufficient moment conditions for the validity of the CLT over hyper-rectangles in high dimensions in all possible regimes, showing that the CLT may hold under much weaker conditions compared to those present in the existing literature.

papers.title: Rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully nonlinear extrinsic geometric flows: Classification and Applications
papers.abstract: We study rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully non-linear extrinsic geometric flows in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ driven by positive $α$-homogeneous curvature functions, building on Rengaswami's classification of bowl-type translators. For positive ends at infinity and every $α>0$, we derive two correction terms beyond the leading order in the nondegenerate case and the growth rate in each degenerate regime. Imposing the translator equation across the neck on a signed extension of the curvature function, we construct catenoidal translators and classify their continuations according to a branch of the rotational level set. These yield complete embedded translators or maximal pieces, for which we determine the regularity at each transition and the shrinking-neck asymptotics; each alternative is realized in a model family of curvature functions. As applications of the tangency principle, we obtain rigidity and nonexistence results governed by the global geometry of the bowl-type solutions. When the bowl is entire, it is unique up to vertical translation among convex translators with a single graphical end asymptotic to it (also under a weighted condition in the strictly convex case), and its existence rules out both convex translating graphs over bounded domains that blow up at the boundary and entire ones growing uniformly faster or slower than the bowl. When the bowl is not entire, it may have finite height for $α>1$; in this setting, any strictly convex translating graph over a ball that is continuous up to the boundary and has vertical tangent planes there is necessarily a bowl of finite height.

papers.title: Topology, Hyperbolicity, and the Shafarevich Conjecture for Complex Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: This survey presents recent developments concerning the Shafarevich conjecture, non-abelian Hodge theories, hyperbolicity, and the topology of complex algebraic varieties, as well as the interplay among these areas. More precisely, we present the main ideas and techniques involved in the linear versions of the following conjectures: the Shafarevich conjecture, the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture, Kollár's conjecture on the holomorphic Euler characteristic, the de Oliveira-Katzarkov-Ramachandran conjecture, and Campana's nilpotency conjecture. In addition, we discuss characterizations of the hyperbolicity of complex quasi-projective varieties via representations of their fundamental groups, together with the generalized Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture in the presence of a big local system.
papers.comments: Final version, 72 pages, to appear in Algebraic Geometry: Fort Collins 2025, Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics

papers.title: On identity Seidel switches
papers.abstract: An identity Seidel switch of a graph is a vertex subset whose Seidel switch produces an isomorphic graph. We distinguish the elementary abelian group of switching operations from the family of identity switches of a fixed graph, which need not be a group. We obtain an edge-count condition for identity switches and deduce that every vertex-identity switch has degree half the number of remaining vertices. In particular, no graph of order at least two has every vertex as an identity switch. For a two-vertex switching set inducing an edge, we characterize the switches admitting an isomorphism that preserves the endpoint pair, in terms of automorphisms of the remaining induced subgraph. We establish modification results under this additional hypothesis and give explicit constructions of identity switches. Counterexamples show why edge-count conditions and unrestricted modification assertions do not suffice.
papers.comments: 14 pages; algebraic view of the Seidel switch

papers.title: Kantorovich Distance via Spanning Trees: Properties and Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study optimal transport between probability measures supported on the same finite metric space, where the ground cost is a distance induced by a weighted connected graph. Building on recent work showing that the resulting Kantorovich distance can be expressed as a minimization problem over the set of spanning trees of this underlying graph, we investigate the implications of this reformulation on the construction of an optimal transport plan and a dual potential based on the solution of such an optimization problem. In this setting, we derive an explicit formula for the Kantorovich potential in terms of the imbalanced cumulative mass (a generalization of the cumulative distribution in R) along an optimal spanning tree solving such a minimization problem, under a weak non-degeneracy condition on the pair of measures that guarantees the uniqueness of a dual potential. Our second contribution establishes the existence of an optimal transport plan that can be computed efficiently by a dynamic programming procedure once an optimal spanning tree is known. Finally, we propose a stochastic algorithm based on simulated annealing on the space of spanning trees to compute such an optimal spanning tree. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach for optimal transport on finite metric spaces.

papers.title: Energy-variational solutions for geodynamical two-phase flows: From logarithmic to double-obstacle potentials by variational convergence
papers.abstract: In [Nonlinear Anal. Real World Appl. 93(2026), art. id. 104652] we studied a Cahn--Hilliard two-phase model describing the flow of two viscoelastoplastic fluids in the framework of dissipative solutions using a logarithmic potential for the phase-field variable. This choice of potential has the effect that the fluid mixture cannot fully separate into two pure phases. The notion of dissipative solutions is based on a relative energy-dissipation inequality featuring a suitable regularity weight. In this way, this is a very weak solution concept. In the present work, we study the well-posedness of the geodynamical two-phase flow in the notion of energy-variational solutions. They feature an additional scalar energy variable that majorizes the system energy along solutions and they are further characterized by a variational inequality that combines an energy-dissipation estimate with the weak formulation of the system adding an error term that accounts for the mismatch between the energy variable and the system energy multiplied by a suitable regularity weight. We give a comparison of these two concepts. We further study different phase-field potentials for the geodynamical two-phase flow model. In particular, we address the variational limit from a potential with a logarithmic contribution to a double-obstacle potential, then also allowing for the emergence of pure phases. This study underlines that, thanks to its structure, the energy-variational solution is better suited for variational convergence methods than the dissipative solution.

papers.title: The non-ergodic Host-Kra-Ziegler structure theorem for $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions via measurable selections
papers.abstract: We establish a non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem for measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions. Our argument reduces the non-ergodic case to the ergodic theorem (for $d\ge 2$ due to Candela and Szegedy) via a measurable selection procedure. We also establish a non-ergodic vertical nilcharacter version of our main result. The non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem is a key input in the companion paper by the second author and Fraczyk classifying point processes (i.e. random subsets) of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ whose law is invariant under the group $\mathrm{ASL}_d(\mathbb{Z})$ of affine transformations.
papers.comments: v2: 20 pages, added non-ergodic vertical nilcharacter version and connection to the application in the companion paper arXiv:2605.16921; v3: 22 pages, added Example 2.4 and Remark 4.1; v4: 25 pages, final version accepted by TAMS, incorporating the referee's comments

papers.title: On subradically sifted sums related to Alladi's higher order duality between prime factors
papers.abstract: In this paper, I utilize a variant of the Selberg--Delange method to find quantitative estimates of the sums \[M_{k,ω}(x,y)=\sum_{\substack{p_{1}(n)> y\\ n\leq x} } μ(n) {ω(n)-1\choose k-1},\] where $y$ can grow with $x$ but we must have $y\leq Y_0\exp(\mathscr{p}\frac{\log x}{(\log\log (x+1))^{1+ε}})$ with $Y_0,\mathscr{p},ε>0$. Moreover, I give preliminary upper bounds for the general range $1.9\leq y\leq x^{\frac{1}{k}}$. In addition, I formalize the notions of subradical and radical dominance and discuss their relevance to the analytic approach to the study of arithmetic functions. Lastly, I give a fascinating formula related to the derivatives of the gamma function and the Hankel contour, which should be relevant for those employing the Selberg--Delange method to obtain higher-order terms.
papers.comments: This paper has been accepted at Research in Number Theory

papers.title: Global Recovery from Local Data: Interior Nudging for 2D Navier-Stokes equations in a Physical Domain
papers.abstract: In many real-world applications of data assimilation (DA), the strategic placement of observers is crucial for effective and efficient forecasting. Motivated by practical constraints in sensor deployment, we show that global recovery of the flow field can be achieved using observations available only in a subregion of the domain, possibly far from the boundary. We focus on the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations posed in a bounded physical domain with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Building on the continuous data assimilation framework of Azouani, Olson, and Titi (2014), we rigorously prove that the assimilated solution converges globally to the true solution under suitable conditions on the nudging parameter, spatial resolution, and the geometry of the observation region, specifically, when the maximum distance from any point in the domain to the observational subregion is bounded by a constant multiple of \( ν^{1/2} \) (in terms of scaling). Our computational results, conducted via finite element methods over complex geometries, support the theoretical findings and reveal even greater robustness in practice. Specifically, synchronization with the true solution is achieved even when the observational subregion lies farther from the rest of the domain than the theoretical threshold permits. Across all three tested scenarios, the local nudging algorithm performs comparably to full-domain assimilation, reaching global accuracy up to machine precision. Interestingly, observational data near the boundary are found to be largely uninformative. This demonstrates that full observability is not necessary: carefully chosen interior observations, even far from the boundary, can suffice.

papers.title: On a definitition of slice regular algebraic varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a complete correspondence between irreducible slice regular algebraic sets and quasi prime radical right ideals in the ring of quaternionic slice regular polynomials. In particular we make use of the definition of quasi prime ideals to give a characterization of irreducibility of slice regular algebraic sets. More precisely, we show that if $I$ is a radical and quasi prime right ideal, then $\mathbb S_{V_c(I)}$, the symmetrization of $V_c(I)$, is an irreducible slice regular algebraic set, where $V_c(I)$ denotes the set of common zeros with commuting components of polynomials in $I$. Combining this fact with the results of one of our previous papers, we obtain that for $I$ radical, $V_c(I)$ is irreducible if and only if $I$ is quasi prime. We also find a complete characterization of quasi prime radical right ideals, proving that either they are completely prime or the radical of the symmetrization $S(J)$ of a completely prime right ideal $J$.

papers.title: Soliton-type metrics associated with weighted constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics on Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish an existence equivalence between a weighted constant scalar curvature Kähler metric introduced by Lahdili and an associated soliton-type metric introduced in this article on Fano manifolds. We apply it to semisimple principal fibrations with Fano fiber. This yields a family of extremal Kähler metrics, including a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric, on a non-Fano complex four-fold with non-toric Fano fiber. A further application concerns Sasaki metrics on canonical circle bundles over $n$-dimensional Fano manifolds. For a fixed (possibly irregular) Reeb field, we show that there exists a Sasaki Mabuchi soliton if and only if there exists a Sasaki extremal metric whose transverse scalar curvature is strictly less than $n+1$. Finally, we characterize Reeb fields on the standard sphere $S^{2n+1}$ that admit Sasaki Mabuchi solitons.
papers.comments: 41 pages, The log-concavity assumption on the weight function in Theorem 1.2 was removed by a result of Jubert-Pan. An application to extremal metrics on a certain fibration was added in Section 5. An application to Sasaki extremal metrics and Sasaki Mabuchi solitons was added in Section 6. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: Global smoothing of singular Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study the problem of smoothing Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties with isolated Du Bois (equivalently, log canonical) lci singularities. For Fano varieties, we show that any such $Y$ admits a deformation to a Fano variety with only $1$-rational singularities, and if $Y$ has only non-$1$-rational hypersurface singularities, then $Y$ is smoothable. For Calabi-Yau varieties, we show first that any such $Y$ deforms to a Calabi-Yau with only $1$-Du Bois singularities. Moreover, if $Y$ has only non-$1$-Du Bois hypersurface singularities then $Y$ is smoothable. Both smoothing statements extend to lci singularities satisfying suitable local conditions. When we allow a Calabi-Yau to have $1$-liminal singularities, a global condition is needed, which we express in terms of the Hodge-Du Bois numbers of $Y$. These theorems recover and generalize results for threefolds of Friedman, Namikawa, Namikawa-Steenbrink, Gross, and Friedman-Laza. In higher dimensions, our results provide alternative smoothing conditions and also extend the work of Friedman-Laza from the case of rational hypersurface singularities to Du Bois lci singularities.
papers.comments: In v2, the second claims of Theorems 1.3-1.5 assumed lci singularities. I discovered that a result in the literature I relied on is incorrect. Our claims remain valid for hypersurfaces and hold in the lci case under an extra local hypothesis. Global examples show such an assumption is necessary

papers.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 20 figures, 4 tables. Corrections of: thm. 2, prop. 3.1, cor. 3.9, small typos

papers.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
papers.abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{Γ, λ}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $Γ$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{Γ,λ}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{Γ, λ}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{Γ, λ}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{Γ,λ}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{Γ,λ}$, whereas the converse fails.

papers.title: Uniform Property (S)
papers.abstract: We introduce and investigate a quantitative version of Steinhaus' property$(S)$ for Banach spaces, called the \emph{uniform property$(S)$}. A Banach space$X$ is said to have uniform$(S)$ if for every pair of distinct unit vectors $x,y\in X$ and every $a>0$, the difference of the perturbed norms $$ \sup_{\|z\|\le a}\big|\|x+z\|-\|y+z\|\big| $$ is bounded below by a positive function of$a$ and$\|x-y\|$. We compute this modulus exactly for the spaces $L_1(μ)$ with atomless measure$μ$, $$ U_{L_1(μ)}(d;a)=\Big(\tfrac{4a}{2+d}\wedge 1\Big)d. $$ The class of spaces with uniform$(S)$ is stable under ultrapowers, Bochner-$L_1$ constructions, and contains all Gurariĭ spaces as well as Banach lattices of almost universal disposition. In particular, every Banach space embeds isometrically into a non-strictly convex Banach space of the same density having uniform$(S)$. We further exhibit an explicit equivalent renorming of$\ell_1(Γ)$, $$ \|x\|_S=\big(\|x\|_1^2+\|x\|_2^2\big)^{1/2}, $$ which endows$\ell_1(Γ)$ and all its ultrapowers with uniform$(S)$. These results settle, in ZFC, several open questions about the quantitative geometry of property$(S)$ posed by Kochanek and the second-named author.
papers.comments: 24 pp, accepted for publication in Studia Mathematica

papers.title: Fast, High-Accuracy, Randomized Nullspace Computations for Tall Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop RLOBPCG, an efficient method for computing a small number of singular triplets corresponding to the smallest singular values of large, tall matrices. The algorithm combines randomized preconditioner from the sketch-and-precondition techniques with the LOBPCG eigensolver: a small sketch is used to construct a high-quality preconditioner, and LOBPCG is run on the Gram matrix to refine the singular vector. Under the standard subspace embedding assumption and a modest singular value gap between the two smallest singular values, we prove that RLOBPCG converges geometrically to the minimum singular vector. In numerical experiments, RLOBPCG achieves near-optimal accuracy on matrices with up to $10^6$ rows, outperforming classical LOBPCG and Lanczos methods by a speedup of up to $12\times$ and maintaining robustness when other iterative methods fail to converge.

papers.title: An Alternative Proof of an Erd\H os-Rényi Law for the Longest Consecutive Monotone Block in a Random Permutation
papers.abstract: $\{X_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of i.i.d.~($p$) coin-tosses, the longest run $L_n$ of heads in the first $n$ coin tosses approaches $\log_{1/p}n$ almost surely. In this paper we explore a formulation of this result in the case of random permutations and prove an Erd\H os-Rényi law for the longest consecutive monotone block in a random permutation. This problem has been studied before by several authors, and we offer a Poisson approximation viewpoint on this issue using the Stein-Chen method.

papers.title: Pathwise stability of Wasserstein contractive Markov chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: We study pathwise behaviour of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms. For chains satisfying a contraction assumption w.r.t. a Wasserstein distance we establish explicit deterministic rates that hold for single realisations on sets of high probability. Additionally, we show that the median of means estimator further increases the pathwise stability. To prove our main results we employ a well-known martingale decomposition technique based on solutions of Poisson's equation. Finally, we apply our results to concrete MCMC methods including the No-U-Turn-Sampler, the Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm and slice samplers.
papers.comments: 36 pages; major revision of the first version; results have been extended and the title has changed

papers.title: Quantile-Based Skewness for Fuzzy Numbers With Probabilistic Foundations: An Application in Portfolio Optimization
papers.abstract: This article quantifies asymmetry under imprecision by introducing a probabilistic interpretation for fuzzy numbers and a non-moment based skewness coefficient derived from it. The coefficient adapts classical quantile-based skewness measures (Bowley, Kelley, and Groeneveld-Meeden) to the $α$-cut representation of fuzzy numbers. Existing studies typically modify the classical Fisher-Pearson formula heuristically, substituting membership functions for probability densities without a rigorous semantic bridge between the two. Our coefficient, in contrast, is grounded in an explicit probabilistic interpretation, making it both mathematically meaningful and aligned with the semantics of fuzzy set theory. We interpret a fuzzy number's left and right membership function components as cumulative and survival probability functions of associated two random variables $X_L$ and $X_R$. This yields a reading of its $α$-cuts as generalized quantiles, i.e., intervals of values that are "at least $(1-α)$-probable", highlighting a duality between probability and possibility theory. As a quantile-based measure, the coefficient is invariant under scale and location transformations. Its point-based variant needs only a fixed number of quantile evaluations, constant time in the $α$-discretization, compared with the linear cost of moment-based alternatives. The coefficient comprises two complementary constituents: an "inner" measure quantifying the intrinsic skewness of the underlying probabilistic distributions, and an "outer" measure capturing the fuzzy number's overall profile asymmetry. We illustrate the measures within a fuzzy mean-variance-skewness portfolio optimization framework on historical equity data, comparing their performance with two of the most highly cited moment-based fuzzy skewness coefficients from the literature.

papers.title: Neural Learning of Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms: a Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: We combine neural learning and geometric diagnostics to investigate the rank and border rank of the \(3\times3\) matrix-multiplication tensor \(M_3\). Using the Bhattacharya--Mesner product, we derive \textsc{MatMulNet}, a differentiable architecture encoding bilinear maps. Constrained refinement yields a length-\(23\) numerical solution with machine-precision full-tensor residual and bounded decomposition weight. Along the explored length-\(22\) branch, the residual instead decreases as the gauge-invariant weight grows. This contrast supports \(R_{\mathbb R}(M_3)=23\) as a working hypothesis. A Laurent-parametrised extension probes border rank, giving a tentative, protocol-dependent motivation to investigate \(r=19\) and the adjacent \(r=18\) case. For \(M_4\), the same diagnostics distinguish bounded numerical solutions recovered from perturbed known schemes, structured residual plateaus, and weight-growing approximations, revealing the dependence of the search on initialisation. Together, the experiments connect approximation accuracy with decomposition growth and identify concrete targets for exact or certified investigation.

papers.title: The Expurgated Error Exponent is Not Universally Achievable
papers.abstract: We study the universal attainability of the expurgated error exponent for discrete memoryless channels (DMCs). While the random-coding exponent is known to be universally attainable for every fixed input distribution via maximum mutual information (MMI) decoding for DMCs, it remains open whether the expurgated exponent can be attained universally. We show that this is not the case in general. Specifically, we construct a family of DMCs for which no single sequence of codes can attain the expurgated exponent simultaneously for all channels in the family, even at rate zero. In addition, for the same channel family, we show that MMI decoding fails to achieve the expurgated exponent for any channel in the family.

papers.title: A Trust-Region Interior-Point Stochastic Sequential Quadratic Programming Method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a trust-region interior-point stochastic sequential quadratic programming (TR-IP-SSQP) method for solving optimization problems with a stochastic objective and deterministic nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. In this setting, exact evaluations of the objective function and its gradient are unavailable, but their stochastic estimates can be constructed. In particular, at each iteration our method builds stochastic oracles whose estimates of the objective value and gradient satisfy proper adaptive accuracy conditions with a fixed probability. To handle inequality constraints, we adopt an interior-point method (IPM), in which the barrier parameter is taken from a prescribed decreasing sequence and is reduced once a stochastic stationarity test is passed. Under standard assumptions, we show that, almost surely, the KKT residual vanishes along the iterations at which the barrier parameter is reduced, and every limit point of these iterates is a KKT point. We implement the method on a subset of problems from the CUTEst test set, as well as on constrained logistic regression problems, to demonstrate its practical performance.

papers.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang energy for a dilute gas of hard spheres: an upper bound
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum gas consisting of $N$ hard spheres with radius $\frak{a} > 0$, obeying bosonic statistics and moving in the box $Λ= [0;L]^3$ with periodic boundary conditions. We are interested in the ground state energy per unit volume in the thermodynamic limit, with $N, L \to \infty$ at fixed density $ρ= N / L^3$. We derive an upper bound for the ground state energy density, matching the famous Lee-Huang-Yang formula, up to lower order terms, in the dilute limit $ρ\frak{a}^3 \ll 1$.

papers.title: A Dyadic Frequency Law for a Perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-Recursion
papers.abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-recursion defined by $$Q(1)=Q(2)=1,\qquad Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n \quad(n\ge3).$$ for $n\ge3$. Cloître proved that the recursion is globally well-defined and encoded its odd- and even-indexed subsequences by binary arches and canonical plane forests. Let $F(s)=\#\{n\ge1:Q(n)=2s-1\}$, and let $ν_2(j)$ denote the exponent of $2$ in $j$. For every integer $k\ge0$, we prove the multiset identity $$ \{F(s):2^k\le s<2^{k+1}\}=\{3+ν_2(j):1\le j\le 2^k\}. $$ The proof expresses frequencies as sums of plateau lengths and folds reflected gap pairs to identify the excess frequencies $F(s)-3$ with the outdegrees of a canonical plane tree. For $k\ge2$, the maximum $k+3$ occurs at $s_k=\lceil 2^{k+2}/3\rceil$, and the second-largest frequency $k+2$ occurs at $s_k+1$. As a corollary, the sum with marks $z^{F(s)-3}$ and dyadic block weights $2^{-ku}$, multiplied by the Dirichlet eta function $η(u)$, has the Euler product of $ζ(u)$ with its factor at $2$ replaced by $(1-z2^{-u})^{-1}$. Finally, we prove that the dyadic defect $Q(2n)-2Q(n)$ attains order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ in absolute value along a subsequence.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 4 figures; Version 4 locates the two highest frequencies in each nonsingleton dyadic block and proves that the dyadic defect attains order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ along a subsequence. The eta-normalized marked block sum has the Euler product of $ζ(u)$ modified only at 2. We also shorten the proof of Lemma 5.2, update references, and add code checking the peak locations

papers.title: Pooled Inverse Optimization: Learning the Unique Optimal Decision from Repeated Observations
papers.abstract: Inverse optimization infers a decision-maker's objective from observed decisions. We study repeated noisy observations of one decision. Classical formulations impute a separate optimum for each observation, so their size grows with the sample, and may return one of many equally compatible objectives. With a bounded polyhedral feasible set and a cost vector drawn from a distribution with a density, the optimum is almost surely a unique vertex. Its compatible costs form a full-dimensional cone that repeated observations of the same decision cannot shrink. Pooled inverse optimization fits one optimum to all observations and reports its compatible cost cone. Under squared loss, the optimization model has fixed size after aggregation, the decision estimate has a finite-sample error bound, and guarded rounding recovers the true vertex and its full cone with probability tending to one. A single convex program sufficed in every linear scaling run. With 50 variables and 10,000 observations, median runtimes were 8 milliseconds under squared loss and 8 seconds under absolute loss. The standard mixed-integer formulation reached its time limit at 100 observations. At 10,000 observations, the remaining two exact formulations under absolute loss and two convex baselines reached their 10- to 60-minute limits. Using national survey data on women with hypertension and diabetes or prediabetes, the method finds in milliseconds the diet closest to each woman's mean reported intake subject to DASH-based nutrient bounds in a food-group model and identifies which bounds bind.
papers.comments: 35 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Substantially revised and retitled. Previous title: "From Non-Identifiability to Goal-Integrated Decision-Making in Parametric Inverse Optimization". This version treats the pooled model and its computational study; the goal-integrated models of version 1 are not included

papers.title: On Big-M Reformulations of Bilevel Linear Programs: Hardness of A Posteriori Verification
papers.abstract: A standard approach to solving optimistic bilevel linear programs (BLPs) is to replace the lower-level problem with its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions and reformulate the resulting complementarity constraints using auxiliary binary variables. This yields a single-level mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model involving big-$M$ parameters. While sufficiently large big-$M$s that preserve at least one bilevel-optimal solution can be computed in polynomial time, verifying a priori that given big-$M$s do not cut off any feasible or optimal lower-level solutions is known to be computationally difficult. In this paper, we establish two complementary hardness results. First, we show that, even with a single potentially incorrect big-$M$ parameter, it is coNP-complete to verify a posteriori whether a given optimal solution of the resulting MILP model is bilevel optimal. In particular, this negative result persists for min-max problems without coupling constraints and applies to strong-duality-based reformulations of mixed-integer BLPs. Second, we show that verifying global big-$M$ correctness remains computationally difficult a posteriori, even when an optimal solution of the MILP model is available.
papers.comments: The proof of Theorem 3 has been substantially revised

papers.title: On the size of $\{a: 1\leq a<n, n|a^2-1, a|n^2-1\}$ for number $n$: Connections to Fibonacci-like Sequences and Twin Primes
papers.abstract: For a positive integer n, let $\mathcal{A}(n)$ denote the set of integers $a$ satisfying $1 \leq a < n$ subject to the simultaneous modular conditions \(n \mid a^2 - 1\) and \(a \mid n^2 - 1\). In this paper, we investigate the structural properties and cardinality of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\). By establishing a precise algebraic correspondence between the elements of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\) and the integer evaluations of a family of Fibonacci-like sequences defined by a second-order recurrence, we prove that \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{} < \log_2 n +2\) for all composite $n > 1$. Trivially, $|\mathcal{A}(n)| = 2$ when $n$ is an odd prime power. Furthermore, we analyze the global distribution of these cardinalities, demonstrating that the asymptotic average of \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{}\), for $n\leq x$, approaches $2 + o(1)$ as $x \to \infty$. Guided by the properties of the underlying algebraic mapping and supported by computational verification for all $n < 10^{15}$, we formulate the conjecture that $|\mathcal{A}(n)| \le 3$ uniformly for all $n$. In connection with this conjecture, we show that every integer $N$ that is the product of a pair of twin primes satisfies $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$, providing an explicit family of integers $N$ with $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$.

papers.title: Cache-Aided Asymmetric MIMO Communications: Achievable DoF Analysis
papers.abstract: Integrating coded caching (CC) into multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications significantly enhances the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF). This paper investigates a practical cache-aided asymmetric MIMO configuration with cache ratio $γ$, where a server with $L$ transmit antennas communicates with $K$ users. The users are partitioned into $J$ groups, and each user in group $j$ has $G_j$ receive antennas. We propose four content-aware MIMO-CC strategies: \emph{min-$G$} enforces symmetry using the smallest antenna count among users; \emph{Grouping} maximizes intra-subset spatial multiplexing gain at the expense of some global caching gain; \emph{Super-grouping} aggregates users into optimized \emph{min-$G$}-based super-sets with identical effective receive multiplexing gains before applying \emph{Grouping} across them; and \emph{Phantom} redistributes spatial resources assuming "phantom" antennas at the users to bridge the performance gains of \emph{min-$G$} and \emph{Grouping}. We develop these asymmetric strategies under three reference symmetric CC placement-delivery policies with guaranteed linear decodability: a finite-search DoF-optimized policy attaining the best single-shot achievable DoF lower bound, and two closed-form policies, namely combinatorial and linear cyclic low-complexity constructions, with the cyclic policy attaining DoF performance close to the others in many operating regimes. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate significant DoF improvements across various system configurations, and that policy-strategy combinations offer flexible trade-offs between DoF and subpacketization complexity.

papers.title: Continuity of almost commutative manifolds for the spectral propinquity
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical metric spectral triples of a fixed compact connected spin manifold depend continuously, for the spectral propinquity, on the Riemannian metric endowed with the $C^1$ topology. This continuity extends to almost commutative spectral triples, allowing the Riemannian metric and the Dirac operator of a fixed finite dimensional factor to vary simultaneously. We also establish continuity for metric spectral triples arising from ergodic actions of compact connected Lie groups as the inner product on the Lie algebra varies. Our proofs use a common continuity criterion involving graph norms and commutator seminorms. As a consequence, eigenvalues in any compact interval whose endpoints avoid the limiting spectrum converge with multiplicity. These results relate classical variations of metric data to the geometry of metric spectral triples.
papers.comments: 34 pages. Revised version: exposition is improved, the focus is on convergence for the spectral propinquity. Changed title and abstract to reflect the new introduction and general presentation

papers.title: On CR manifolds of CR dimension 1
papers.abstract: We classify all maximal symmetry models of CR dimension 1, depending on their Bloom-Graham and Tanaka types, give coordinate realization to some of those models and prove a general extension principle.
papers.comments: This version is further revised and improved

papers.title: Geometry of Critical Couplings, Quartic Binding, and Spectral Shift for Concentric $δ$-Shells
