papers.abstract: We study the first zero-energy resonance of finitely many attractive concentric spherical $δ$-shells with fixed radii and variable strengths. The positive critical strengths form a smooth hypersurface in coupling space. For every nonzero tangent redistribution we calculate its second fundamental form as an explicit strictly positive quadratic form $C_a$ in cumulative weighted coupling changes. Along the straight perturbation $g_*+\varepsilon a$, the same coefficient determines the unique emerging bound state, $E_b=-C_a^2\varepsilon^4+O(|\varepsilon|^5)$, for either sign of $\varepsilon$, and the crossover of the canonically normalized total spectral shift on the scale $k\asymp\varepsilon^2$. We also give a global smooth parametrization of the positive critical surface by probability weights, determine the exact attainable interval of effective ranges, and reconstruct all critical strengths from individual threshold-pole responses. An exact coupling coordinate gives a uniform $O(k^3)$ spectral-shift normal form and a differentiated $O(k^2)$ estimate without a restriction on the ratio of coupling distance to wave number. The scattering determinant and general threshold exponents are established inputs. Our results give the model-specific curvature coefficient, its spectral consequences, and a complete local and global description of the first-critical configurations.

papers.title: The Integral Chow Ring of Smooth Non-strict Toric Stacks
papers.abstract: We extend the Stanley--Reisner ring to the non-strict stacky fans introduced by Geraschenko and Satriano. We then prove that this ring is isomorphic to the integral Chow ring of the associated toric stack when the underlying fan is smooth. More generally, we show that this ring is isomorphic to the integral Chow ring of the canonical stack over the associated toric stack for an arbitrary non-strict stacky fan. These generalize earlier results on the integral Chow rings of smooth toric varieties and several classes of toric stacks. We also give an explicit description of the pullback homomorphism induced by a morphism of non-strict stacky fans.
papers.comments: 12 pages. The main theorem has been strengthened, and its proof has been streamlined

papers.title: A family of groups extending McLain's
papers.abstract: Given a strict partial order $Δ$ on a set $Λ$ and an arbitrary ring $R$ with $1\neq 0$, the corresponding McLain group $M(Δ)$ has been studied in depth. We construct a larger family of McLain groups $G(Δ)$, where $Δ$ need be neither asymmetric nor transitive, while satisfying two weaker axioms. Structural properties common to all members~$G(Δ)$ of this new family are investigated, including a group presentation, a description of the factors of its descending central series, a canonical form for its elements relative to any total order on~$Δ$, and a recursive determination of its upper central series. In addition, we prove the natural isomorphism $G(Δ)/G(Γ)\cong G(Δ\setminusΓ)$, where $Γ$ is a normal subset of $Δ$, and $G(Γ)$ and $G(Δ\setminusΓ)$ are extended McLain groups on their own right. This result has no parallel in the classical context.

papers.title: Duality of operator Frobenius algebras and solution of Eisenhart-Stäckel problem in the non-diagonal case
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius algebras of operator fields and introduce a novel notion of duality for them. We show that, under the assumption that the operator fields forming the Frobenius algebra are mutual symmetries, the operator fields in the dual Frobenius algebra are also mutual symmetries. This result allows one to construct new infinite-dimensional integrable systems of hydrodynamic type starting from a given one. As the main application, we solve the long-standing Eisenhart--Stäckel problem for any Segre characteristic and in arbitrary dimension: namely, we describe all nondegenerate finite-dimensional integrable systems whose integrals are quadratic in momenta such that the corresponding $(1,1)$-tensors commute as operator fields.
papers.comments: 25 pages. The results in v2 are essentially the same as in v1; we corrected some misprints, updated references, and did some simplifications of the arguments

papers.title: One-sided certification of surrogate near-minimizers: exact worst-case envelopes under strong convexity and smoothness
papers.abstract: We study target suboptimality for points that approximately minimize a surrogate objective. Unlike standard uniform perturbation estimates, the available comparison is one-sided, thresholded at a certified lower target level, and restricted to the entire surrogate-selected sublevel set. We first show that selected comparison alone cannot yield a finite worst-case guarantee, even for strongly convex quadratics with identical Hessians. A single scalar upper bound on the surrogate minimum closes this information gap and leads to a sharp general estimate. For pairs of $μ$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth objectives, we then solve the associated worst-case information problem exactly. We obtain a sharp feasibility barrier and a dimension-free envelope; in its nontrivial regime, the value reduces to a scalar maximization over a compact interval. Explicit one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic objectives attain the bound while satisfying the one-sided constraint on the full selected set. We characterize when curvature strictly improves the general certificate and provide a threshold-preserving finite-net validation procedure. The results identify the best guarantee permitted by the prescribed partial information, independently of any particular optimization algorithm or additive perturbation model.

papers.title: Spectral Dehn Functions: Hyperbolicity, Filling Geometry and Diffusion
papers.abstract: We show that Dirichlet eigenvalues of van Kampen diagrams can distinguish groups whose Dehn functions have the same order. The Dehn function bounds the least filling area in terms of word length. We use the random walk on the faces, stopped at the exterior. For each null word we take the infimum, over its fillings, of the reciprocal of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, then maximize over words of length at most $n$. We call this the spectral Dehn function. Its coarse growth is a quasi-isometry invariant for presentations whose generators form a word ball and whose relators are all null words of length at most three. In such a presentation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the boundary word of a square can have a filling with more faces and a larger first eigenvalue than any of its least-area fillings. For two groups with quartic Dehn functions, it is at most $Cn^4$ for one and at least $cn^6/(\log n)^2$ for the other. The spectral Dehn function is bounded exactly for word-hyperbolic groups. For other finitely presented groups it grows at least as fast as $n^2/(\log n)^2$. In these presentations the bound is sharp for non-hyperbolic automatic groups and for non-hyperbolic groups acting properly and cocompactly by isometries on proper geodesic Lipschitz $1$-connected spaces. For the face walk we maximize the expected absorption time over starting faces. In these classes its supremum over least-area fillings of cyclically reduced null words of length at most $n$ has order $n^2$. Taking the infimum over all fillings of each null word before maximizing over words of length at most $n$ gives order $n^2/\log n$ in these presentations. Under a quadratic isoperimetric inequality, every non-hyperbolic group has, for each sufficiently large $n$, a null word of length at most $n$ whose least-area fillings have, for the face and vertex walks, $j$th Dirichlet eigenvalue of order $j/n^2$ for $1\le j\le cn^2$.

papers.title: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.title: Koszulity in the category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie Superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is to establish precisely which blocks in the Category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$ are Koszul. It is known that $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ has three blocks up to equivalence; one generic block and two integral blocks. The generic block is known to be Koszul, and the principle integral block is verifiably not Koszul. In this paper, we prove that the remaining of the three blocks of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul. Consequently every non-principal block of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul, which is the category $\mathcal{O}$ analogue, in the smallest case, of a known result for finite-dimensional modules over semisimple extensions of Takiff superalgebras. This is done by explicitly computing the endomorphism algebra of projective modules in this block and then proving that it is Koszul inductively. Along the way, we compute all $\mathrm{Ext}$ groups between simples in this block. To compute the endomorphism algebra we are aided by a computer algebra tool developed in Mathematica, inspired by a post on Stack Exchange.

papers.title: On the Chevalley-Bass number of a field
papers.abstract: We give upper and lower bounds on the Chevalley-Bass number of a field of characteristic zero, whenever this quantity is well-defined. We also describe an algorithm which computes the Chevalley-Bass number of a field, provided its maximal abelian subextension is known. As a primary application, we improve the value of a constant related to exponential Diophantine equations.
papers.comments: 19 pages. Minor changes, following a referee report and feedback from Claude Opus 5.5. Corollary 2.11 is new

papers.title: The Schwarzian Derivative for Convex Holomorphic Mappings in Several Complex Variables
papers.abstract: We study the two components of Oda's Schwarzian derivative, the tensor $S_f$ and the quadratic form $S^0_f$, for convex holomorphic mappings of the polydisk and for Roper--Suffridge extensions of convex functions to the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with norms taken in the Bergman metric. For the polydisk we obtain the sharp bound $\|S_f\|\leγ_n$, where $γ_n$ is the maximum of an explicit quartic form on the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with $γ_2=2$ and $γ_n\to2\sqrt2$, and the sharp bound $\|S^0_f\|\le 4/(n+1)$, $n\ge2$, in both cases the extremal mappings are products of half-plane mappings. For Roper--Suffridge extensions both norms are computed exactly in terms of the Schwarzian derivative of the one-variable function. In particular $S^0_f$ reduces to the classical Schwarzian derivative, and the theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood yields the sharp bounds $\|S_f\|\le1/\sqrt{n+1}$ and $\|S^0_f\|\le 1/(n+1)$, with equality for the parallel strip.

papers.title: The Dedekind completion of an Archimedean ordered vector space as a reflector
papers.abstract: We consider the category $\mathbf{AOVS}$ of Archimedean ordered vector spaces with linear maps which preserve all existing nonempty suprema, and its full subcategories $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$, consisting of directed spaces, Dedekind complete vector lattices and universally complete vector lattices, respectively. We deduce from some results in the literature that $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$ are reflective subcategories of $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, with the usual Dedekind completion being the reflector in $\mathbf{DVL}$. In contrast to these facts, we show that a non-directed Archimedean ordered vector space of dimension greater than $1$ has no reflector in either $\mathbf{DVL}$ or $\mathbf{UVL}$. In particular, there are no free Dedekind complete vector lattices over a set with more than one element. We also use the occasion to show that a free vector lattice with $α$ generators embeds into a free vector lattice with $β$ generators if and only if $α\leβ$, and explore the concept of the free completion of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong unit.

papers.title: On Higher-Order Geometric Refinements of Classical Covariance Asymptotics: An Approach via Intrinsic and Extrinsic Information Geometry
papers.abstract: Classical Fisher-information asymptotics describe the covariance of regular efficient estimators through the local quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood, and thus capture first-order geometry only. In curved models, including mixtures, curved exponential families, latent-variable models, and manifold-constrained parameter spaces, finite-sample behavior can deviate systematically from these predictions. We develop a coordinate-invariant, curvature-aware refinement by viewing a regular parametric family as a Riemannian manifold \((Θ,g)\) with Fisher--Rao metric, immersed in \(L^2(μ)\) through the square-root density map. Under suitable regularity and moment assumptions, we derive an \(n^{-2}\) correction to the leading \(n^{-1}I(θ)^{-1}\) covariance term for score-root, first-order efficient estimators. The correction is governed by a tensor \(P_{ij}\) that decomposes canonically into three parts, an intrinsic Ricci-type contraction of the Fisher--Rao curvature tensor, an extrinsic Gram-type contraction of the second fundamental form, and a Hellinger discrepancy tensor encoding higher-order probabilistic information not determined by immersion geometry alone. The extrinsic term is positive semidefinite, the full correction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, and it vanishes identically for full exponential families. We then extend the picture to singular models, where Fisher information degenerates. Using resolution of singularities under an additive normal crossing assumption, we describe the resolved metric, the role of the real log canonical threshold in learning rates and posterior mean-squared error, and a curvature-based covariance expansion on the resolved space that recovers the regular theory as a special case. This framework also suggests geometric diagnostics of weak identifiability and curvature-aware principles for regularization and optimization.
papers.comments: We included the LEAN files of the article. We rewrote parts of the texts that were ambiguous and corrected the main result by adjusting its hypotheses

papers.title: The Pentagon Graph Operator
papers.abstract: The pentagon graph $C_5(G)$ of a finite simple graph $G$ is the edge-intersection graph of its induced cycles of length five. We prove that the dodecahedral graph is mapped to the icosahedral graph $I$, which is a fixed point of the operator. Our principal result classifies every graph obtained by adjoining one vertex to $I$: it is eventually fixed if the added vertex belongs to no induced pentagon, and it is expanding otherwise. The proof shows that every new pentagon gives rise to a tadpole hat within at most two iterations. More generally, an induced icosahedral core with $h$ tadpole hats gives the lower bound $12+h2^k$ on the orders of the iterates. We also establish a replication principle and construct two vertex-disjoint induced copies of the Shrikhande graph in its pentagon graph, yielding the bound $16\cdot2^k$. The general vanishing--periodic--expanding trichotomy is included as background.
papers.comments: This version corrects the fixed-point isomorphism for the icosahedral graph, classifies its one-vertex extensions, and proves that the Shrikhande graph is pentagon-expanding

papers.title: Composition operators and Rational Inner Functions on the bidisc: A geometric approach
papers.abstract: We study composition operators acting on the weighted Bergman spaces on the bidisc, i.e. $C_Φ:A^2_β(\mathbb{D}^2)\to A^2_β(\mathbb{D}^2)$ where $Φ$ is induced by rational inner functions (RIFs) or a RIF and a smooth function (mixed case). Our approach is geometric. Our main result is a uniform criterion for all $β\in(-1,0]$ that can be summarized as follows: Boundedness of the composition operator is equivalent to transversal intersection of the level sets for non-smooth symbols, under the assumption that if any tangential intersection occurs on the singularity it must be of high order. This extends the characterization of Bayart-Kosiński to the non-smooth self maps of the bidisc. To reach our conclusions, we utilize results obtained by Anderson, Bergqvist, Bickel, Cima and Sola on Clark measures associated to RIFs and Puiseux factorizations.
papers.comments: 32 pages after comments from anonymous referee were incorporated, pictures from reference [17] as examples. Accepted for publication in the Journal of London Mathematical Society

papers.title: Convolution invertibility for constructible sheaves and functions
papers.abstract: We characterize convolution-invertible, compactly supported piecewise-linear sheaves on a finite-dimensional real vector space. We show that they factor, up to a shift, as convolutions of constant sheaves on two bounded convex sets, one closed and the other relatively open. To this end, we first establish a more general characterization of convolution invertibility for compactly supported constructible functions. In the piecewise-linear case, this yields a convex factorization which lifts to sheaves. The key step is a geometric characterization of invertibility in the dual projective space via the Radon transform.

papers.title: Structural Classes for Chollet's Permanent Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1982, Chollet conjectured that $\operatorname{per}(A\circ B)\le \operatorname{per}(A)\operatorname{per}(B)$ for Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$, where $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product. In this paper, we study natural structural classes for which the conjecture holds. We first show that a stronger inequality holds for a broad class of matrices with bipartite support. We then introduce a simple way of joining positive semidefinite matrices and give conditions under which Chollet's inequality is preserved under this operation. For graph Laplacians, this operation corresponds to vertex coalescence and gives larger structured graph families satisfying Chollet's inequality from simpler graph classes.
papers.comments: Appears in the Proceedings of the 52nd International Conference on Current Trends in Theory and Practice of Computer Science (Sofsem 2027)

papers.title: Factorization and monotonicity methods for reconstructing an impenetrable obstacle in inverse biharmonic scattering
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an impenetrable obstacle with a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition from far-field measurements. The associated data-to-pattern operators are noninjective, because the biharmonic scattered fields can be decomposed into propagative and evanescent components. We derive new symmetric factorizations of the far-field operator and analyzie the middle operators on the closures of the ranges of the adjoint data-to-pattern operators to establish range identities. These identities yield factorization criteria for the support of the obstacle when the wavenumber is not an associated transmission eigenvalue. Furthermore, we derive monotonicity criteria without excluding transmission eigenvalues. Numerical experiments for Dirichlet obstacles illustrate the reconstruction methods and show their performance with noisy data and for wavenumbers near a clamped transmission eigenvalue.

papers.title: Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calderón problem
papers.abstract: We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calderón problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.

papers.title: Embodied Communication: Sensing-Induced Reliability Fields and Capacity Bounds
papers.abstract: This paper introduces embodied communication, a new wireless communication modality in which information is imprinted onto environmental states and recovered by the receiver through sensing. No dedicated communication transmitter is activated, and no additional communication spectrum is occupied; instead, the sensed environment itself becomes the carrier of information. The key insight is that sensing must be reinterpreted for communication. Rather than asking how accurately an unknown physical state can be estimated, embodied communication asks how reliably two states can be distinguished. We formalize this idea through a multi-snapshot radio frequency (RF) sensing model and derive a sensing-induced reliability field that quantifies the distinguishability between physical states. This field turns embodied symbol design into a geometric packing problem shaped by the sensing resolution of the infrastructure. For this embodied channel, we characterize the finite-snapshot $ε$-capacity through achievable designs and converses. We develop lattice-based codebooks, obtain a closed-form hexagonal design under a main-lobe approximation, and establish information-theoretic and geometric upper bounds. We further investigate the sensing-duration tradeoff: more sensing snapshots improve reliability, but also lengthen each embodied symbol, leading to a finite optimal sensing time. These results expose a latent communication pathway in sensing-enabled infrastructure and show how the environment can be transformed from a passive backdrop into an active information carrier.
papers.comments: Keywords: Embodied communication, ISAC, ambient modulation, Sensing distinguishability, lattice packing

papers.title: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
papers.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $ΣA_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

papers.title: On the global convergence of gradient flow for wide shallow models beyond homogeneous nonlinearities
papers.abstract: A surprising phenomenon in the training of neural networks is the ability of gradient descent to find global minimizers of the training loss despite its non-convexity. Following earlier work, we investigate this behavior for wide shallow models. Existing global convergence results primarily concern models with positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities, such as ReLU activations, and models with scalar output weights and bounded nonlinearities, such as sigmoid activations. We study a broader class of models, including multi-head attention layers and two-layer fully connected networks with bounded or asymptotically positively one-homogeneous activations and vector output weights. Building upon (Chizat and Bach, 2018), we prove that, in the limit of infinitely many hidden neurons or attention heads, non-minimizers of the training loss are unstable under the mean-field gradient flow dynamics by constructing "escape regions" in the parameter space. Our global convergence statements are conditional in the following sense: if the mean-field gradient flow converges for the Wasserstein 2-distance, then its limit must be a global minimizer. We revisit the bounded nonlinearity, scalar-output setting of (Chizat and Bach, 2018), giving an escape region construction adapted to unbounded nonlinear parameter domains. We also propose new constructions for nonlinearities with at most linear growth under a non-degeneracy assumption and for asymptotically positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities. Finally, we show the well-posedness and stability estimates for the mean-field training dynamics under sub-Gaussian initializations.

papers.title: An energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of ferronematic equilibrium states and its numerical realization
papers.abstract: We develop an energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of two-dimensional ferronematic equilibrium states. The problem is formulated as the minimization of the harmonic energy of two two-dimensional vector fields, both with prescribed length, together with an additional nonlinear relation on the orientation of the two vectors. The finite element setting is based on piecewise continuous finite elements on a weakly acute triangulation. The numerical realization of the energy-decreasing algorithm employs a decomposition-coordination framework and a Uzawa-like iteration. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the computational performances of the algorithm.

papers.title: Self-similar dendrites with finite boundary and P-sprouts
papers.abstract: Each self-similar dendrite K with a finite self-similar boundary defines a finite acyclic edge-labeled bipartite graph G, called the sprout of K. The paper shows that the sprout G determines the combinatorial properties of the dendrite K and its topological structure.

papers.title: Two Results on Outer-String Graphs
papers.abstract: An \emph{outer-string representation} of a graph $G$ is an intersection representation of $G$ where vertices are represented by curves (strings) inside the unit disk and each curve has exactly one endpoint on the boundary of the unit disk (the anchor of the curve). Additionally, if each two curves are allowed to cross at most once, we call this an \emph{outer-$1$-string representation} of $G$. If we impose a cyclic ordering on the vertices of $G$ and require the cyclic order of the anchors to respect this cyclic order, such a representation is called a \emph{constrained outer-string representation}. In this paper, we present two results about graphs admitting outer-string representations. Firstly, we show that for a bipartite graph $G$ (and, more generally, for any $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free graph $G$) with a given cyclic order of vertices, we can decide in polynomial time whether $G$ admits a constrained outer-string representation. Our algorithm follows from a characterization by a single forbidden configuration, similar to that of Biedl et al. [GD 2024] for chordal graphs. Secondly, we answer an open question from the same authors and show that determining whether a given graph admits an outer-1-string representation is NP-hard. More generally, we show that it is NP-hard to determine if a given graph $G$ admits an outer-$k$-string representation for any fixed $k\ge1$.
papers.comments: 17pages, 14 figures, appears in the proceedings of GD 2026

papers.title: Characterization of stability radii for robustly asymptotically stable dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems
papers.abstract: We study linear time-invariant dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems. We characterize when the systems are robustly asymptotically stable and derive exact conditions and bounds when this property is lost under structure-preserving perturbations.

papers.title: A tree-like fractal Dirichlet space lying between strong and weak elliptic Harnack inequalities
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a self-similar fractal configured as an infinitely branched tree and equip it with a regular self-similar Dirichlet form. Fixing a typical metric ball, we compute accurately the effective resistance between an inner point and the boundary of this ball. Based on this result, anomalous behaviour of the mean exit time from such balls is shown -- the ratio between whose supremum and infimum can be arbitrarily large. Under properly selected self-similar measure, we further show the weak elliptic Harnack inequality holds but the strong analogue fails.

papers.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a normed space
papers.abstract: We prove that the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of every real or complex normed space $X$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $X$.
papers.comments: 7 pages, v3 generalizes v2 to clouds of arbitrary normed spaces

papers.title: Mechanisms and Pathways of Extreme Events in Partially Observed Stochastic Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Extreme events occur across the natural, engineering, and socioeconomic sciences, where rare but high-impact episodes can lead to disproportionate consequences and pose challenges for prediction and risk management. Existing studies have mainly focused on the statistics, sampling, forecasting, and attribution of extremes from observable variables. We develop a mathematical framework for studying the mechanisms and pathways of extreme events in partially observed stochastic dynamical systems with hidden variables. By integrating data assimilation with information-theoretic and trajectory-based diagnostics, we infer latent precursor dynamics, quantify their uncertainty, and determine how their influence propagates toward an observed extreme event. Conditional Gaussian models provide a tractable analytical setting for closed-form diagnostics, while the framework extends more broadly through numerical methods. From a trajectory-wise viewpoint, we compare filtering and smoothing distributions to identify the onset of hidden precursors and quantify their temporal influence range. From a statistical viewpoint, we construct event-conditioned hidden-state distributions to identify sensitive triggering directions, representative latent pathways, and distinct candidate pathway classes through clustering. Three case studies illustrate the methodology. In an intermittent stochastic model, hidden damping dynamics emerge before observed bursts, and filter-smoother discrepancies provide an onset diagnostic. In a stochastic model with damping and forcing, separate damping-induced, forcing-driven, and mixed pathways to extremes are identified. In a nonlinear topographic-flow model, distinct mechanisms and pathways for blocking and unblocking patterns associated with observed extreme events are revealed.

papers.title: Deformed seminorms, anisotropic sectors and Phragmén Lindelöf principles for $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$\allowbreak difference operators
papers.abstract: We study the deformed derivative of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba on spaces of holomorphic functions, with the induced geometry and growth principles. The deformed derivative maps the holomorphic functions on a disc of radius $ρ$ into those on the disc of radius $ρ/β$, $β$ being the upper limit of the $n-$th roots of the deformed numbers, and this loss of radius is optimal. For two root structure functions the deformed gauge equals $\max\{|z|,1/φ_{1}\}$, so that deformed discs are Euclidean above a minimal radius; Borel Carathéodory and vector valued Cauchy Hadamard theorems follow. On factorial weighted Banach spaces the deformed derivative has norm $1/r$ and spectrum the closed disc of radius $1/r$. A deformed Borel transform identifies these spaces with weighted Wiener algebras, yields the Gelfand theory, and shows that the associated Fréchet space is nuclear. We establish logarithmic convexity and subharmonicity results, Phragmén Lindelöf and Lindelöf principles in the anisotropic sectors of half aperture $θ\sup_{k}k^{-1}\log[k]$ and in their curved variants, with sharp critical orders, and a rigidity theorem: under Gaussian growth of the deformed factorials, functions of finite deformed exponential type are entire of order zero and cannot be bounded on a ray unless constant. A dominant term principle shows that, for a large dominant root, the deformed exponential and trigonometric functions have only real simple zeros, localized between explicit geometric means of deformed numbers, whereas the deformed exponential series has nonreal zeros when the two roots have sum at most two.

papers.title: Propagation of Regularity for Schroedinger Equations with Time Dependent Potentials
papers.abstract: The dynamics of Schrödinger equation with time dependent potentials of general time dependence is considered. It is shown that for localized in space potentials, there is propagation of regularity which is uniformly bounded in higher Sobolev norms. Unlike the cases where the solution scatter, and then propagation is proved via a standard bootstrap argument, the solutions considered here have a part that does not scatter, as expected in general. For this we introduce propagation estimates that work directly in (e.g.) $H^2(\mathcal{R}^3).$

papers.title: Admissibility of Adaptive Monotone Step-Down Multiple Testing Procedures Under Arbitrary Covariance Dependence
papers.abstract: We study finite-sample admissibility for simultaneous testing of multivariate normal means under a vector loss whose components are the usual individual $0$--$1$ losses, with an arbitrary known positive-definite covariance matrix. For the two-sided problem, we establish admissibility for a broad class of procedures that rank active hypotheses using locally adaptive, strictly increasing transformations of suitably standardized conditional residuals. The result also covers residual-based sequential procedures with positive stage-specific cutoffs common to all active hypotheses at each stage, without requiring the cutoffs to be nonincreasing. The proof derives the interval structure of the acceptance sections from two properties: the previously rejected indices remain invariant while the hypothesis under study is active, and the stopping rule ensures that a perturbation leading to its rejection cannot defer that rejection beyond the stage at which the procedure at the unperturbed observation stops while accepting it. We also establish the corresponding one-sided result for locally adaptive, strictly increasing transformations of signed residuals, under both point-null and composite-null formulations and their respective vector losses. Together, these results extend vector-loss admissibility beyond the original Maximum Residual Down (MRD) procedure and identify a broader monotone ordering structure induced by covariance-adjusted residuals. We also show that the two-sided and one-sided classes are almost-everywhere limits of finite-support Bayes rules under their corresponding additive total losses; this representation, however, does not assert admissibility under those losses.

papers.title: A high-order IMEX-DG solver for atmospheric dynamics: rotating tests on non-conforming meshes
papers.abstract: We present a high-order implicit-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (IMEX-DG) solver for the compressible Euler equations that accounts for rotational effects within an atmospheric framework. Time integration follows a second-order additive Runge-Kutta scheme, treating stiff acoustic modes implicitly and advective terms explicitly. The solver is built on the deal.II finite element library, combining matrix-free operator evaluation, adaptive non-conforming mesh capabilities, and distributed-memory parallelism. The inclusion of rotation extends the framework to large-scale atmospheric dynamics, where the Coriolis force plays a central role in geostrophic balance. Its incorporation into a high-order matrix-free DG discretisation is, however, non-trivial, as it requires a careful formulation of the discrete rotational operator. Two alternative treatments of the rotational and gravitational source terms within the solution strategy, based on nonlinear fixed-point iterations, are therefore introduced and compared in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. A discrete analysis of the rotational operator is also carried out in order to derive a formulation suitable for efficient matrix-free implementation. The proposed formulation is verified through convergence studies on rotating inertia-gravity wave benchmarks and further assessed in fully three-dimensional simulations of stratified flow over orography on both uniform and adaptive meshes. The numerical results show that the rotating IMEX-DG framework has the expected accuracy and stability properties while correctly capturing the asymmetry and wave structures induced by rotation in large-scale atmospheric flows.

papers.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
papers.abstract: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.

papers.title: Residual-Weighted Randomized Jacobi: Sharpened Bounds via Residual Concentration and Asynchronous Extension
papers.abstract: We study randomized stationary methods for symmetric positive definite linear systems in which component $j$ is selected with probability proportional to $|r_j|^\ell$. This family interpolates between uniform sampling on the nonzero residual components ($\ell \to 0^+$) and Gauss--Southwell relaxation ($\ell \to \infty$). For $\ell = 2$ we sharpen the one-step analysis using the inverse participation ratio (IPR) of the residual, $ν^2(r) = n\|r\|_4^4/\|r\|_2^4$, which is $1$ for a uniform residual and approaches $n$ as it concentrates. The resulting bound multiplies the guaranteed expected-progress coefficient of uniform sampling by the IPR (and the expected progress, for constant-diagonal $A$). We extend the analysis to asynchronous execution via the Avron--Druinsky--Gupta (ADG) framework, obtaining, under an a priori envelope on the IPR, an epoch-based reduction bound in which the IPR controls both the progress coefficient and the certified delay window. Synchronous runs on three structured problems and eight Matrix Market matrices support the sharpened bound, and shared-memory experiments show an IPR trajectory nearly insensitive to concurrency. There, committing a buffered residual value (consistent reads, the easier case for ADG) led to divergence at high concurrency on every problem, while re-reading the component at update time (inconsistent reads) diverged in a minority of runs on one problem. We conjecture a feedback-damping mechanism, test its predictions, and find that sufficiently small fixed steps and an adaptive IPR-driven step-size rule removed the instability in every run, at a cost in speed.

papers.title: On the Variety of Hyperspace Selections
papers.abstract: If $f$ is a continuous selection for the Vietoris hyperspace $\mathcal{F}(X)$ of the nonempty closed subsets of a space $X$, then the point $p=f(X)\in X$ is not as arbitrary as it might seem at first glance. In fact, the set $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ of all these points reveals certain information about the variety of Vietoris continuous selections for $\mathcal{F}(X)$. Thus, for a connected space $X$, we will show that every point $p\in \mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is not only noncut, but also an endpoint of $X$. Another result of this paper is that in an arbitrary topological space $X$, the closure of the set $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is always a totally disconnected subset. Furthermore, we will also show that $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is a closed subset of every first countable totally disconnected space $X$.

papers.title: On Santaló's Problem
papers.abstract: This paper investigates an isoperimetric-type problem posed by L. A. Santaló, concerning convex surfaces in hyperbolic 3-space that minimize total mean curvature among all convex surfaces with fixed surface area. This problem asks for a characterization of the minimizers and for the optimal form of a Minkowski-type inequality in hyperbolic 3-space. In this work, we propose a conjectural description of the minimizers under certain regularity assumptions. We also construct a new family of convex surfaces as as potential minimizer candidates and establish a property of the singular points of any minimizer.
papers.comments: 32 pages, 2 figures. Provided more detailed numerical computation in proof of Theorem 1.2

papers.title: Analogues of the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function and related problems
papers.abstract: Upper bounds for the Riemann zeta function $ζ(s)$ as $\Im(s)\to\infty$ have been extensively studied in connection with the Lindelöf Hypothesis. In particular, the Lindelöf Hypothesis is one of the most important open problems in analytic number theory. It is also known to be equivalent to certain mean value estimates, which provide a fundamental connection between pointwise upper bounds and integral mean values of zeta-functions. In this paper, we consider an analogue of the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function $ζ_r (s,a,(w_1,\dots,w_r)) = \sum_{m_1=0}^\infty \cdots \sum_{m_r=0}^\infty (a+m_1 w_1+\cdots+m_r w_r)^{-s} $ for $\Re(s)>r$, with $a,w_1,\dots,w_r>0$, and establish equivalent conditions in terms of integral mean values. We treat the rank-one case and, under a polynomial growth assumption on the derivative, the general-rank case. The $\Q$-rank of $\langle w_1,\dots,w_r\rangle$ specifies the region considered in our statements; the equivalence argument itself does not establish that its left boundary is a critical line.

papers.title: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
papers.abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices required for the activation process to spread to all remaining vertices of $G$. In this article, we consider the odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and the bipartite odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\), and prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The first formula confirms the quadratic-growth conjecture proposed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.

papers.title: Existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle, helping to establish the universality of the C-type route to chaos in families of non-invertible maps of the plane. Families of two-dimensional non-invertible maps, with at least two parameters and critical points of fold type, exhibit a distinct type of critical scaling, the C-type. An accumulation of parameter values leads to an infinite collection of coexisting attracting cycles of periods $4^n$ or $2\cdot 4^n$. Asymptotically, period quadrupling is accompanied by parameter-space scaling and state-space scaling governed by particular universal constants. Kuznetsov et. al. explained this phenomenon in terms of a stationary orbit of period two of the renormalisation group (RG) transformation for period-doubling. We prove the existence of the corresponding renormalisation two-cycle in a Banach space of analytic maps and gain rigorous bounds on the corresponding universal state space scaling constants. This result provides a further step in proving a series of outstanding conjectures concerning distinct universality classes for period-doubling. It extends the recent results for unidirectionally-coupled maps (the FS-type) to bidirectionally-coupled maps, and generalises the framework from fixed points to periodic orbits of the corresponding renormalisation operators. It also provides a further step in establishing the conjectured picture that the C-type universality class is born from the FS-type class via a period-doubling bifurcation in the dynamics of the RG transformation itself. The proof relies on rigorous computations to establish that a variant of Newton's method for the two-cycle is a contraction map. The C-type scaling regularity is known to occur in a number of dynamical systems of interest, perhaps most notably in biologically-plausible models of nephron blood pressure autoregulation.

papers.title: Proper edge coloring with rainbow diamonds
papers.abstract: Motivated by the B-coloring defined by Gyárfás and Sárközy, we introduce a new edge coloring called \emph{D-coloring}. For a graph $G$, a D-coloring of $G$ is a proper edge coloring such that every diamond subgraph is rainbow. The \emph{D-chromatic index} of $G$, denoted by $χ'_D(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a D-coloring of $G$. Denote by $Δ$ the maximum degree of $G$. We propose a Brooks-type conjecture stating that $χ'_D(G)\le \frac{1}{2}Δ^2+\frac{1}{2}Δ$ and verify this conjecture for $Δ\le 5$. We also prove a general upper bound $χ'_D(G)\le \frac{9}{16}Δ^2+\frac{1}{2}Δ$.

papers.title: Geometry of Holomorphic One-forms on Smooth Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon X\to A$ be a morphism from a smooth projective variety to an abelian variety. We show that if an irreducible component of the exceptional set of a birational map from $X$ to its good minimal model has general type image in $A$, then every 1-form pulled back from $A$ has a zero. For the Albanese map, this yields a sharp dimension bound for spaces of nowhere vanishing holomorphic 1-forms, which refines the Popa-Schnell inequality. Furthermore, we investigate the structure of the spaces of holomorphic 1-forms with zeros, and show that they are linear for large classes of varieties. Also, we construct a delicate example of a smooth projective subvariety of an abelian variety for which the holomorphic 1-forms with positive-dimensional zero loci do not form a linear subset. Finally, we study algebraic surfaces admitting holomorphic 1-forms that have zeros and do not arise from cohomology jump loci.
papers.comments: This version corrects a LaTeX macro error in Proposition 3.13. The proof of Theorem 2.2 in the previous version contained an error, so we have rewritten most of Section 2. The revised section presents two new, more general results (Theorems 2.1 and 2.11) on the behavior of the zero loci of holomorphic 1-forms under birational modifications

papers.title: Algebraic Hodge generic points are dense
papers.abstract: Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \subset \mathbb{C}$. We show that the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to $f$ are analytically dense in $S(\mathbb{C})$. In fact, in the spirit of the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large monodromy assumption, we prove the density of the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ where the periods of the fibre do not satisfy extra relations 'up to degree $δ$'. As a by-product, we also establish new instances of the Mumford-Tate conjecture, beyond the realm of abelian motives. When the base $S$ is a curve, we provide quantitative estimates for points satisfying these properties. The main technical contribution is a new result on relations satisfied by solutions of $G$-operators, which relies on height estimates due to Bombieri and André.

papers.title: Non-Isomorphic Optimal Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: We present eighty-nine optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs that are non-isomorphic to previously known optimal Cayley graphs with the same degree and diameter. For each graph, we provide comprehensive data on its parameters and structural invariants. Comparison with known constructions reported by Marston Conder on the Combinatorics Wiki and in related works reveals significant differences in girth, algebraic connectivity, domination number, automorphism group structure, cycle distributions, distance-related properties, and other graph invariants. These findings show that optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs are frequently non-unique. The new examples enlarge the catalogue of known optimal graphs and provide benchmarks for investigations in degree-diameter problems, algebraic graph theory, and extremal graph theory. Since some of the graphs were identified through randomized search techniques, the collection is not exhaustive.

papers.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.

papers.title: Gelfand--Kirillov dimensions of highest weight modules for basic classical Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain explicit formulas for the Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimensions of simple highest weight modules over basic classical Lie superalgebras. For the type II orthosymplectic superalgebras $D(m,n)$ and $B(m,n)$, we describe the associated varieties determined by highest weights relative to two Borel subalgebras. This gives algorithms valid for arbitrary complex highest weights, without integrality or typicality hypotheses. In type $B$, we further derive a formula for $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$, distinguishing between integral and half-integral weights. For $G(3)$, $F(4)$ and $D(2,1;α)$, finite odd-reflection procedures give exact GK dimension formulas and finite-dimensionality criteria. We also describe the dependence on $α$ for $D(2,1;α)$. In type I, the GK dimension equals that of the simple even highest weight module for the distinguished Borel subalgebra. The computations rely on established ordinary Lie algebra formulas involving Lusztig's $\mathbf a$-function and Robinson--Schensted (RS) insertion.

papers.title: Cascading Smoothers for Multigrid
papers.abstract: Multigrid methods are among the most effective frameworks for solving large-scale sparse systems. However, achieving their hallmark linear scaling and rapid convergence crucially depends on an effective smoother algorithm, whose design is often highly problem-dependent. This paper develops a new approach, referred to as cascading smoothers due to their operation as an ordered sequence of single-step block-diagonal smoothers. Each level in the cascade is optimised to maximally damp the output of prior steps via a Frobenius norm minimisation of the corresponding error propagators. In particular, we develop an additive (resp., multiplicative) formulation analogous to Jacobi (resp., Gauss-Seidel). Applied within a standard multigrid V-cycle, we show they are remarkably effective across a wide array of problems, including finite difference, finite element, and discontinuous Galerkin discretisations applied to Poisson, elliptic interface, and Stokes systems as well as multiphase variants. In every case, cascading smoothers closely match or significantly outperform their optimally-damped classical counterparts, yet require no parameter tuning apart from a few discrete solver choices. Additionally, the approach is highly parallelisable and robust to geometric and operator complexities such as unstructured meshes and high-contrast coefficients.

papers.title: Dynamic Programming without Contractivity
papers.abstract: Optimality results in dynamic programming are usually derived from contraction arguments, which require discounting or uniform bounds on termination times. We show that, in many useful settings, contractivity can be replaced by a simple global stability condition that requires no rate or uniformity. Under this condition and mild order-theoretic assumptions, we obtain existence of optimal policies, uniqueness of the value function as a solution to the Bellman equation, and convergence of value function iteration and of Howard and optimistic policy iteration. Applications include optimal stopping without discounting, where contraction methods can fail, and Bayesian sequential analysis.

papers.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
papers.abstract: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by training learnable components through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size when the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection is numerically unstable under repeated eigenvalues. We address the first with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that reduces memory from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n + \mathrm{nnz}(A))$, and the second with a stable backward rule based on the Dalečkii--Krein representation of the Fréchet derivative. Together, these enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm starts for COSMO. On standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs, ranging from max-cut and Lovász $\vartheta$ to robust estimation and control, the learned policies outperform tuned COSMO on every problem class, reducing iterations to tolerance by up to 60$\times$, and transfer without retraining to instances up to 10$\times$ larger in the size parameter while retaining 2--5$\times$ speedups. Our matrix-free solver implementation also batches naturally on the GPU, solving 64 Lovász $\vartheta$ SDPs 14$\times$ faster than sequential COSMO. When embedded in sequential convex programming for nonlinear covariance steering, our learned optimizers outperform the interior-point solver Clarabel in terms of both success rate and solve time.

papers.title: Schubert cells for the super affine Grassmannian of $GL_{n|m}$
papers.abstract: We study Schubert cells in the affine Grassmannian of the general linear supergroup $GL_{n|m}$, focusing explicitly on the low-dimensional cases $n|m = 1|1$ and $2|1$. We define the affine super Grassmannian as an fpqc sheaf, describe its bounded-lattice filtration by finite-dimensional superschemes, and provide coordinate descriptions, equations, and morphisms for the cells that arise in low dimensions. For $GL_{2|1}$ the cells in the positive and negative chambers split as odd vector bundles over jet schemes of the projective line, and cyclic cells of $GL_{n|m}$ are jet schemes of projective superspaces. In the mixed-sign chamber the transition functions acquire nilpotent corrections in the even coordinate, and all cells except one are non-split. We also introduce decorations, which record the odd directions of the cells on the lattice graph.

papers.title: Convergence of Scalar Curvature of Long Time Kähler-Ricci Flow on Kähler Manifold
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the long time Kähler-Ricci flow on a compact Kähler manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n$ with semi-ample canonical bundle. We establish a uniform $μ$-entropy estimate and a uniform Sobolev inequality along the normalized Kähler-Ricci flow. As a consequence, we prove that the scalar curvature of the Kähler metrics along the normalized Kähler-Ricci flow converges uniformly on $X$ to the negative Kodaira dimension $-κ$ of $X$. In the noncollapsing case $κ=n$ we also obtain the rate of convergence $-Ce^{-t}\leq R(t)+n\leq C(1+t)^{-1}$ and $\fint_X|R(t)+n|ω(t)^n\leq Ce^{-t}$.
papers.comments: 27 pages. Added discussion and results on the noncollpasing case, all comments are welcome

papers.title: On $H=W$ in Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove ``$H=W$" in the context of a Banach function space $X(Ω)$. Let $Ω$ be a subset of ${\mathbb R}^n$ and denote by $W^1_X(Ω)$ the collection of all those $f\in X(Ω)$ whose distributional derivatives $\partial_jf$ are contained in $X(Ω)$. Our main result provides a small collection of ``universal" hypotheses on $X(Ω)$ that ensure $W^1_X(Ω)$ is equal to $H^1_X(Ω)$, the formal closure of ${Lip}(Ω)\cap W^1_X(Ω)$ with respect to the norm \[\|f\|_{W^1_X(Ω)} = \|f\|_{X(Ω)} + \|\nabla f\|_{X(Ω)}.\] The main theorem has two corollaries. The first gives a slightly stronger set of hypotheses for ``$H=W$", and the second gives density of $C^\infty_c({\mathbb R}^n)$ in $W^1_X({\mathbb R}^n)$.
papers.comments: Revised to include several important references missing in first version

papers.title: Bipartite cuts in Ramsey-Turán style
papers.abstract: We prove that every $K_5$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/18+o(1))$ edges, where the constant $1/18$ is best possible. The proof method is related to extensions of Turán Theorem in edge-weighted settings, and part of the proof uses flag algebra. Using a similar flag algebra formulation, AI proved that every $K_6$-free and $K_7$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/12+o(1))$ and $n^2(1/9+o(1))$ edges, respectively. These constants are best possible.

papers.title: Spectral Properties of Dense Barabási-Albert Graphs
papers.abstract: Preferential attachment graphs model networks whose growth produces highly uneven degree distributions, describing many real-world systems. Their adjacency spectra are important because they allow graph-theoretic questions to be studied through the eigenvalues of matrices. We analyze the adjacency matrix of a dense Barabási-Albert (B-A) multigraph, where the number of edges added at each step is proportional to the final number of vertices. First, we compute the large-$n$ limit of the expected adjacency matrix and show that it is described by a rank-one limiting kernel, viewed as a continuous analogue of the adjacency matrix. After centering and scaling, the fluctuations form a random matrix with a computable variance profile. Using the quadratic vector equation approach, we derive the limiting bulk spectral distribution. We also determine the asymptotic location of the leading eigenvalue generated by the rank-one mean component.

papers.title: Birational Algebraic Topology
papers.abstract: Over any qcqs scheme $S$, we show that inverting dense open immersions in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, $log\mbox{-}\mathcal{H}^\Box(S)$, and $\mathcal{P}_Σ(\mathrm{Sm}_S)$ yields the same birational $\infty$-category $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$. Unlike in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, all Nisnevich truncations and homotopy sheaves (including $π_0^{nis}$) of birational spaces remain birational, and hence $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is Postnikov complete. Moreover, the birational localization $L_{bir}$ commutes with the bar construction, ensuring effective delooping for every grouplike object in $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ and yielding an unstable birational higher-connectivity theorem. Building on these results, we establish birational analogs of the van Kampen theorem, the higher Galois theory of coverings, and the Freudenthal suspension theorem. When $S$ is geometrically unibranch with finitely many generic points, we show that $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is in fact an $\infty$-topos of homotopy dimension zero. Over a perfect field, we identify discrete birational group sheaves with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves whose $\mathbb{G}_m$-contraction vanishes, and deduce that $S^{2,1}$-nullification $L^{2,1}$ agrees with $L_{bir}$ on pointed $L^{2,1}$-connected spaces. Finally, over any field, we prove that $L_{bir}$ preserves generic values of $π_0^{\mathbb{A}^1}$ on motivic colimits of proper schemes; over perfect fields, it therefore detects their $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectivity and yields an equivalence $\mathbb{H}_0^{\mathbb{A}^1} \simeq \mathbb{H}_0^b$ for them, answering a question of Asok and Haesemeyer in greater generality.
papers.comments: 50 pages. Several topos-theoretic results moved here from "On the internal homotopy theory of the motivic homotopy category"; results on proper motivic spaces strengthened and made self-contained

papers.title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehatΞ_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehatΞ_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite étale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $μ_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.
papers.comments: v2: some typos fixed. v4: sections 5-7 added

papers.title: Involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction
papers.abstract: We determine all involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction that extend the involution of the original $*$-algebra. We also find all algebra isomorphisms between the resulting Cayley doubles that extend the identity automorphism of the original $*$-algebra, and consequently classify the resulting $*$-algebras up to such $*$-algebra isomorphisms. As applications, we show that Cayley doubles of algebras without zero divisors admit exactly one additional extension of the original involution in the 2-torsion-free case and none otherwise, prove that the classical Cayley-Dickson involution is the unique scalar involution, and obtain a classification of the $*$-algebras arising from $\mathbb{R}$ up to dimension 4.
papers.comments: 19 pages; minor update; made corrections to Proposition 8 and its proof

papers.title: The number of composite class sizes in finite groups
papers.abstract: We consider finite groups with at least three conjugacy class sizes that are composite numbers and we prove that, in that situation, the number of prime class sizes is bounded by the number of composite class sizes. The analogous result for (non-)prime-power class sizes is also addressed.

papers.title: Finite-core Volterra reductions for the Riemann phase kernel
papers.abstract: We derive exact same-sign formulas for a Riemann theta phase kernel and give a Volterra representation with its boundary and integrated tail terms. The formulas apply to finite theta cores, and the boundary-plus-tail identity also holds for the full theta series. We give an outward-rounded fourteen-node counterexample to nonnegativity of the exact endpoint-B form on the active closed-trace core in the original application. Continuity of the defining kernel transfers the negative value to a smooth witness supported outside the trace interval. As a result, the original energy is unbounded below on every nonempty affine trace fiber that retains this vertical direction. We specify a coercive modification and its changed Euler equation. Positivity of the original full-coordinate Weyl kernel and the zeta-facing application remain unresolved.
papers.comments: Substantive revision. Corrects the original continuum closure claims in Section 15.7 and Appendix C. Adds a certified endpoint-B counterexample and its trace-fiber minimization consequence. Ancillary checker included

papers.title: Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative trace-norm propagation of chaos for finite-dimensional quantum mean-field systems governed by Belavkin equations under continuous diffusive measurements. Our results concern random reduced states conditioned on the observation records of the entire particle system, rather than states averaged over these records. We allow arbitrary one-particle density matrices, general measurement operators, and both perfect and inefficient detection. Two regimes of initial data are considered. For initial states approaching a tensor product in trace norm, without requiring permutation invariance, we establish explicit convergence rates, improved from an inverse fourth-root to an inverse square-root rate when the one-particle initial state is faithful. More importantly, for permutation-invariant initial states, convergence of the two-particle marginal to a product suffices for propagation of chaos, even when the full initial state remains far from a tensor product. Quantitative convergence rates are obtained in this setting, including a sharper estimate under faithfulness. Our proofs combine purification, fully observed dilation, and uniform stability of linear Zakai equations with a relative-entropy method for the joint observation law and conditional quantum state. The latter controls the interacting dynamics through entropy-production estimates and extends to arbitrary-rank initial states by regularizing only the reference dynamics. These results provide a rigorous foundation for low-dimensional approximations of continuously monitored interacting quantum systems, including those with initially correlated states.

papers.title: Fixed-parameter tractable computation of Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomials via tensor networks
papers.abstract: We give a thorough analysis of the time complexity of computing Reshetikhin--Tuareg knot polynomials via tensor contractions on the associated tensor networks, showing that the computation is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter at most linear in the tree-width of the input knot diagram. In particular, this gives a simpler proof to the sub-exponential bound $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$ for the time complexity of computing any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial. We present along with this paper, in SnapPy, the first general-purpose implementation of this algorithm, which computes any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial given its $R$-matrix and ribbon element. We stress the remarkable efficiency of our implementation by demonstrating that: (1) our implementation is several orders of magnitude faster than existing packages on computing the colored Jones polynomial; (2) our implementation is able to compute the Jones polynomial of (i) census knots with large width and over 200 crossings and (ii) some generic random knots with over 2000 crossings, in several hours using less than 10GB RAM, whereas Regina is not able to compute the Jones polynomial of these knots within a memory constraint of 160GB.

papers.title: Coupling and Maximal Inequalities for Graph-Dependent Empirical Processes
papers.abstract: We develop maximal inequalities for empirical processes indexed by graph-dependent observations. Our bounds separate the complexity of the indexing class from two features specific to graph dependence: the geometry of the underlying graph and the cost of coupling graph-separated blocks to independent copies. The coupling construction combines a novel graph-adapted dependence coefficient with a coloring of a block partition. As an application, we derive Glivenko--Cantelli results and characterize the associated effective sample size. A central implication is that graph-dependent empirical processes need not exhibit a generic root-$n$ rate: convergence is jointly determined by function-class complexity, graph geometry, and the decay of dependence with graph distance. We specialize the results to graphs with polynomial and exponential growth and to directed dyadic graphs. Finally, we apply the results to network autoregressive models, nonlinear local-propagation models, and treatment-interference settings.

papers.title: Approximate Controllability of the generalized Burgers-Huxley equation in one dimension
papers.abstract: The generalized Burgers-Huxley (GBH) equation is a prototype model that describes the interplay among reaction, convection, and diffusion. In this article, we explore the controllability of this model by means of an interior control supported in an arbitrary non-empty open subset of the domain. We establish that the GBH equation is not globally approximately controllable in a given time. However, it is possible to steer the system from any steady state to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of another steady state in some suitable time by means of a localized interior control, provided that both steady states lie in the same connected component of the set of steady states.
papers.comments: Updated the abstract and literature review in the introduction, and improved the proofs of theorems and propositions. Main results remain unchanged

papers.title: Stroboscopic Ergodic Averages and Radial Symmetry in the Vortex Model
papers.abstract: We study the point-vortex model in the plane in the case of $N$ vortices of equal positive circulation, and we investigate the long-time behaviour of the empirical vorticity measure. We conjecture that, for almost every initial datum, the time average of the empirical measure exists and is invariant under rotations about the centre of vorticity. We prove the conjecture for $N=3$ by exploiting the integrability of the system. For $N\ge 4$ we reduce the problem to a question about a measure-preserving dynamical system on the shape space: after replacing time with a suitably chosen rotation angle as independent variable, radiality is equivalent to the independence of stroboscopic ergodic averages from the initial phase along a single trajectory. We formulate this reduction as a general ergodic problem, discuss its scope through elementary counterexamples, and verify the required hypotheses in explicit regions of the phase space for $N=3$ and $N=4$.

papers.title: The structure of FAC posets and the Aharoni--Korman conjecture
papers.abstract: A poset $P$ is said to satisfy the finite antichain condition, or FAC for short, if it has no infinite antichain. Such posets exhibit rich and complex structure, and it was conjectured by Aharoni and Korman in 1992 that any FAC poset $P$ possesses a chain $C$ and a partition into antichains such that $C$ meets every antichain of the partition. While a counterexample to this conjecture was recently discovered, in this paper we prove that the conjecture does hold true for a broad class of countable posets. In particular, we prove that the Aharoni--Korman conjecture holds for countable FAC posets containing no saturated chain $D$ such that either $D$ or its reverse $D^*$ is of the form $\bigoplus_{x\inω} D_x$, where each $D_x$ is infinite and co-well-founded. The proof of this result rests on novel structural theory for countable FAC posets, which may be of independent interest. One result states that every countable FAC poset is either scattered (contains no copy of the rationals) or may be broken up into a dense collection of scattered posets which reflect the structure of the poset as a whole. This provides a general reduction from arbitrary countable FAC posets to the far more tractable scattered ones. We also develop an extension $H(P)$ of a poset $P$ which includes ``limit points'' of $P$ and allows for intricate arguments involving these points. Amongst other points, one way in which $H(P)$ differs from existing poset completions and extensions is that it is sensitive to the order-type of a chain. Finally, we highlight a number of intriguing problems in this area which remain open.
papers.comments: 51 pages. The content here used to be part of 2411.16844 (which now contains just the counterexample), and has been substantially rewritten

papers.title: A Gallager-Type Redundancy Bound for Binary Fano Coding
papers.abstract: Binary Fano codes build a complete prefix code by repeatedly splitting the sorted list of symbol probabilities into two halves whose total probabilities are as close to each other as possible. Krajči, Liu, Mikeš, and Moser proved in 2015 that the redundancy $R$ of this code satisfies $R\le1-p_n$, where $p_n$ is the smallest symbol probability. We prove that $R<U(p_1)$, where $U$ is a piecewise function of the largest symbol probability $p_1$ with $U<1$. In particular, $R<p_1+4-\tfrac53\log_2 5$ for every source, and $R<\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_2 5$ when $p_1<\tfrac12$. The bound equals the supremum of the redundancy for $p_1\ge\tfrac12$ and on an interval just below $\tfrac13$, and we give a lower bound for the other values of $p_1$. Unlike the bounds for Huffman codes, the proofs do not use the sibling property. They work directly with the Fano split rule, mainly through the facts that every split is nearly balanced and that the redundancy is a sum of one term per internal node of the tree.

papers.title: Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings
papers.abstract: In this paper, our aim is to establish several Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings $f=h+\overline{g}$ in the unit disk $\Bbb{D} = \{z\in\Bbb{C}: |z|<1\}$. Under various boundedness assumptions on the analytic part $h$, we obtain explicit univalence radii and corresponding schlicht disk radii that improve upon existing estimates in the literature. We also establish new Landau-type theorems under novel hypotheses. We provide examples to illustrate our results, and comprehensive numerical tables present quantitative values of the radii for various parameter choices, demonstrating the effectiveness of our results.

papers.title: The Stability of the Backward Problem for Photoacoustic Imaging in Attenuating Media via Carleman Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the backward problem in time for photoacoustic tomography (PAT) in attenuating media. It is well-established that photoacoustic imaging in attenuating media can be accurately modeled by spatial fractional-order damping. This inverse problem is ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. In this work, we construct a novel class of Carleman estimates independent of spatial variables, and by virtue of these estimates, we establish conditional stability estimates for this problem for the first time. Building upon this, we propose a Tikhonov-type regularization functional and derive its associated adjoint system. Furthermore, leveraging the established conditional stability results, we derive the convergence rate of the proposed regularization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings through extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
papers.abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<φ\leπ$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $π/3$.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 0 figures. Revised and retitled. This version adds the uniform comparison of harmonic weights, its first correction, and the sharp range of the odd-even sign law. An 11-page proof supplement and verification scripts are included as ancillary files

papers.title: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
papers.abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\toγ_\varepsilon(8πν)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $γ_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.
