papers.comments: The title has been revised, the results strengthened, and the overall presentation improved

papers.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $φ$ and $ψ$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^ψ$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^φ$ and $G_x^ψ$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $φ$ and $ψ$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $φ$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.

papers.title: A structured quasi-Newton augmented Lagrangian algorithm for nonlinear least squares with linear and nonlinear constraints
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm for solving nonlinear least-squares problems subject to a mix of nonlinear constraints, linear equalities, and bounds. The nonlinear constraints are handled through an augmented Lagrangian reformulation of the objective, while the linear constraints are kept explicit. Each outer iteration therefore requires the approximate minimization of the augmented Lagrangian over a polyhedron, which we carry out with a gradient projection technique combined with a trust-region step computation. To capture the second-order information specific to the least-squares structure, we approximate the Hessian of the augmented Lagrangian by a Gauss--Newton term corrected by a structured quasi-Newton update, activated by a hybrid switching rule. The correction is built from a secant equation that we derive for the augmented Lagrangian itself. The outer iteration follows the augmented Lagrangian framework of Conn, Gould, Sartenaer and Toint for linearly constrained subproblems, for which we provide an explicit inner solver: a trust-region method whose Cauchy point is computed along nested faces of the polyhedron, without any projection onto it, and safeguarded by classical active-set devices, namely the release of bounds based on least-squares multiplier estimates and $\varepsilon$-active bounds. We prove that this inner solver satisfies the stopping rule required by the outer analysis, which yields global convergence of the overall method to a first-order critical point, and report numerical experiments. Our method outperforms an augmented Lagrangian solver built on the same outer update rules but without least-squares structure, and is competitive in computation time with a state-of-the-art solver for nonlinear programming.

papers.title: A few remarks on the Baez-Duarte Criterion
papers.abstract: We study exponentially damped Möbius approximants in $\mathscr H=L^2([1,\infty),dt/t^{-2})$. With \[ γ_n(t)=\left\lfloor\frac tn\right\rfloor -\frac{\lfloor t\rfloor}{n},\qquad f(u)(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}μ(n)e^{-nu}γ_n(t),\] we compute the relevant scalar products, characterize the Möbius coefficients as the unique coefficients giving pointwise convergence to the constant function, and prove $\langle1 \mid f(u)\rangle\to1$. Vasyunin's formula expresses $F(e^{-u})=\|f(u)\|_2^2$ as an arithmetic cotangent sum. In the final section we give a criterion that would help in the analysis of asymptotics of $F(x)$ as $x\uparrow 1$.

papers.title: Shifted-Binomial Coordinates of Dilated Binomial Polynomials: Multinomial Decimation and Arithmetic Structure
papers.abstract: For integers $m\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, let $d=m+r-1$ and consider the unique expansion \[ \binom{mn}{d}=\sum_{k=1}^{d+1}T_{m,r,k}\binom{n+k-1}{d}. \] By a standard multisection of a rational generating function, the coordinates are a residue-class subsequence of multinomial coefficients: \[ T_{m,r,k}=[x^{mk-1}](1+x+\cdots+x^{m-1})^{m+r}. \] From this representation we obtain the exact support, a counting interpretation by words by drops (Theorem~\ref{thm:drops}), a reflection criterion (the nonzero row is palindromic precisely when $r\equiv2\pmod m$), and log-concavity, hence unimodality, of the nonzero row. An integer-valued polynomial argument gives the universal divisor $m/\gcd(m,r-1)$ of each row, and a prime-adic computation of the fixed divisor of $\binom{mX}{d}$ gives the exact greatest common divisor of each row, a sharpness criterion, and a family of rows in which the universal divisor is arbitrarily far from sharp. We also obtain the row sum $m^{m+r-1}$, a Catalan-number specialization, and explicit coefficient arrays for $m=2,3,4,5$. The methods are finite differences, multisection of rational generating functions, and fixed divisors of integer-valued polynomials.

papers.title: Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Lattès family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.

papers.title: Singular limit for nonlocal conservation laws with non-locality in density and velocity
papers.abstract: We study the singular limit of a generalized nonlocal conservation law intro- duced in [18]. The nonlocal equation incorporates non-locality both in density and velocity. We derive entropy solutions of the underlying Burgers equation as a singular limit. The main ingredient of the proof is a nonlocal Oleinik type estimate, extending the method of [7]. The nonlocal Oleinik estimate provides uniform bounds on the total variation, thereby enabling to pass to the limit in the regularization parameter.
papers.comments: 30 pages. Major revisions: an entirely new section has been added. Expanded introduction

papers.title: Nilpotent quiver varieties with multiplicities and symmetrisable crystals
papers.abstract: We construct analogues of Nakajima's nilpotent quiver varieties for quivers with multiplicities, by developing new stability conditions for framed nilpotent quiver representations with multiplicities and exploiting their interplay with Hecke correspondences. Using these new quiver varieties, we extend Saito's geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals of irreducible highest-weight representations of Kac--Moody algebras from the symmetric to the symmetrisable case.
papers.comments: v2: corrected inaccuracies, 38 pages; v1: 35 pages

papers.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
papers.abstract: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.

papers.title: Non-vanishing uniqueness threshold for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation in dimension at least three
papers.abstract: We study the threshold for the existence of exactly one unbounded cluster for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$ for $d\geq 3$. By recent results of Grebík and Recke and d'Achille et al., this "uniqueness threshold" $p_u(λ)$ tends to zero as the intensity $λ$ of the underlying Poisson point process tends to zero, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation defined on an ambient space from a family of geometric spaces that includes Cartesian products $\mathbb{H}^{d_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb{H}^{d_k}$ with $k,d_1,\dots,d_k\geq 2$. In contrast, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$, Benjamini and Schramm have shown that $p_u(λ)$ tends to one as $λ$ tends to zero, and $p_u(λ)>1/2$ for all $λ>0$. An unpublished argument of D'Achille and Curien shows that for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, the uniqueness threshold satisfies $p_u(λ)\leq 1/2$ for all $λ>0$. Here we will show that $\inf_{λ>0}p_u(λ)>0$ for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$. This answers a question of Grebík and Recke. The ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is a random tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^d$ introduced recently by D'Achille et al. In a sense that can be made precise, it corresponds to the $λ\searrow 0$ limit of the Poisson-Voronoi tessellation. Via a minor adaptation of our proof, we are also able to show that the uniqueness threshold of the ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is strictly positive.

papers.title: National-scale scheduling of long-distance electric vehicle charging under plug capacity
papers.abstract: Can today's U.S. public charging network serve long-distance trips by electric vehicles (EVs), and at what cost to travelers? We plan the charging stops of 2.2 million long-distance trips that need en-route charging, from a 1% sample of a one-month simulation, through the contiguous U.S. fast-charging network. Plans value detour, charging, and waiting time. Charging to a fixed battery level makes each trip's problem a shortest path, solved exactly; common modeling shortcuts can reverse the cost comparison. For trips competing for plugs, we compare four coordination methods, from none to reservations by departure time; the best two come within 2.2% and 6.1% of the best known solutions on small cases. First, if every plug serves every EV, existing fast chargers can reach 98.5% of the trips that need to charge, excluding those with an overly long link, with under four stops and about seven minutes of detour. Second, charging speed and electricity price decide the cost comparison: at \$0.15 per kWh, the EV is cheaper only for travelers valuing their charging time below \$11 per hour with 50 kW, or \$111 per hour with 350 kW chargers; at \$0.45 per kWh, it costs more at either speed. Third, without coordination, long queues form at several hundred small stations at 50 kW while nearby larger ones are less busy. If every trip books a plug, almost all waiting disappears on all trips at 350 kW for under a minute of extra detour, and at \$0.15 per kWh the EV trip stays about 21% cheaper.
papers.comments: 35 pages, 3 figures, 12 tables; includes supplementary material

papers.title: Strictly paired ${\rm CR}$ linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: This paper studies real-linear automorphisms of $\mathbb C^2$ through the ranks of their complex-linear and conjugate-linear blocks. Particular emphasis is placed on strictly paired CR (SPCR) automorphisms of $\mathbb R^4$, for which both blocks have rank $1$. Such a map is complex-linear on one complex line and conjugate-linear on a complementary complex line. Equivalently, the SPCR automorphisms form the double coset ${\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)\,σ_0\,{\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)$, where $σ_0(z_1,z_2)=(z_1,\bar z_2)$ is a mixed real-linear involution whose fixed locus is a real hypersurface. We show that the SPCR locus is a $12$-dimensional submanifold of $M_2(\mathbb C)^2$ and carries a CR structure of CR dimension $4$ and CR codimension $4$ on an explicit open dense subset. We also construct canonical diagonal and genuinely non-diagonal examples.

papers.title: On Leray's Theoreme de Structure for a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations: an improvement of the result
papers.abstract: In this note we furnish a new result concerning the well known théorème de structure by Leray related to a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations. We are able to furnish a new estimate on the left endpoint of the unbounded interval of regularity.

papers.title: On the Kähler MMP and the transcendental base-point-free theorem
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the minimal model program for big gklt Kähler pairs, and in particular we prove Tosatti's transcendental base-point-free conjecture.

papers.title: A Lower Bound on the Sliced Wasserstein Comparison Constant for Translated Measures
papers.abstract: We provide closed-form expressions for standard 1-Wasserstein distance ($W_1$) and Sliced 1-Wasserstein distance ($SW_1$) for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Furthermore, we construct an explicit lower bound for the constant $c_d$ established by Carlier, Figalli, Mérigot, and Wang between $W_1$ and $SW_1$ [1] for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Sliced Wasserstein distances are computationally efficient and used in image generation and other applications, which raises natural questions in computational efficiency versus theoretical correctness. A lower bound on the constant $c_d$ gives information about the cost of that efficiency.
papers.comments: 2nd version: extended Propositions 1 & 2 to finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, fixed typos and added acknowledgments

papers.title: Multilevel limits of spiked random matrix corners processes
papers.abstract: We consider the largest eigenvalues of submatrices of the classical Gaussian random matrices with a finite rank spike in the critical BBP regime. We show that they converge to a multilevel interlacing particle system whose lowest level is the Airy$_β$ point process. Our construction and scaling limits extend in a natural way to non-classical $β>0$.
papers.comments: v2: revisions, new title. v3: corrected typos. 25 pages

papers.title: Proper-Score Observation-Driven Filters: Tracking Efficiency, Estimation, and Continuous-Time Limits
papers.abstract: Observation-driven filters usually update a time-varying parameter with the score of the predictive log density. Replacing the logarithmic score by another proper scoring rule changes both the target the filter tracks and the precision with which it tracks it. These filters form a subclass of the PRADA models of de Punder (2026), and we study their properties at the level of the filtered path. In an in-fill framework, the local tracking error is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. Optimised over the gain, its invariant variance is the geometric mean of the target's volatility and an effective observation noise determined by the scoring rule. Tracking efficiency is the squared correlation between the scoring-rule driver and the true score at the rule's own target. In scale models it equals the asymptotic relative efficiency of the corresponding static minimum-score estimator. The resulting frontier quantifies the robustness--efficiency trade-off. Under Gaussian innovations, density-power and CRPS volatility filters raise minimal tracking risk by 3% and 11%. Under Student-$t_5$ innovations, the Gaussian log-score filter raises it by 58% in the limit, and by more at daily frequency. We also give primitive conditions for bounded scale-invariant drivers, a matrix version, a population self-tuning result for the gain, minimum-score estimation theory whose invertibility conditions hold at the fitted values, and diffusion limits. An international equity application separates the roles of the predictive density and the scoring rule.

papers.title: A note on some upper bounds for the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator
papers.abstract: For two square complex matrices $A,B,$ and a real number $q$, the $q$-deformed commutator of $A$ and $B$ is defined as $AB-qBA$. We give some upper bounds on the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator in the case $q\ge0$. All of the inequalities derived in this paper generalize the Böttcher-Wenzel inequality.
papers.comments: 12 pages. The gaps in the proofs of Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 2.1 have been fixed

papers.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $Σ/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichmüller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(ψ)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlevé I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the lower bound $5.686\ldots$ and the upper bound $12.566\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$. Note that the lower bound shows that the Nehari sufficient squared bound $4$ does not hold on average.

papers.title: An asymptotic Liouville-type theorem for systems of Lane-Emden equations on RCD*(-K,N) spaces via gradient estimates
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish elliptic gradient estimates for positive solutions of the Lane-Emden system on metric measure spaces satisfying the synthetic Ricci curvature-dimension condition $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$. Our approach combines the weak differential calculus and the Bochner inequality available in the $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$ setting with suitable auxiliary function arguments, extending classical gradient estimate techniques to nonsmooth spaces. The resulting estimate is valid for all exponents $α,β>0$ and all $N\in[1,\infty)$, with no dimensional case distinction and with explicit constants. As an application, we prove a quantitative, asymptotic Liouville-type theorem on $\mathrm{RCD}^*(0,N)$ spaces: for positive solutions that are bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, the normalized gradients $|\nabla f|/f$ and $|\nabla h|/h$ are bounded by a quantity that is of order $\max\{α,β\}$ and hence tends to zero as the exponents tend to zero (with comparable size). We also explain why the method gives no rigidity for large exponents, which is consistent with, but does not prove, the existence of nonconstant solutions there. These results generalize corresponding results from the smooth Riemannian setting and contribute to the study of nonlinear elliptic systems on spaces with synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds.

papers.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.
papers.comments: accepted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

papers.title: Comeager hereditary families of compact sets are big
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Polish space and let $\mathcal K(X)$ be its Vietoris hyperspace. A family $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal K(X)$ is hereditary if it is downward closed under inclusion. Matheron and Zelený asked whether every comeager hereditary family in $\mathcal K(X)$ contains a dense hereditary $G_δ$ subfamily. We give an affirmative answer in ZFC.

papers.title: Boundary Layers and Finite-Section Asymptotics for Small Polygons
papers.abstract: In large even polygons of unit diameter, computed angle profiles oscillate near the vertex carrying the pendant diameter. We study the half-line variational problem behind this observation of Bingane and Mossinghoff. Its unique positive equilibrium approaches the regular state with alternating multiplier $(-3+\sqrt5)/2$. We determine the sharp energy errors for two ways of closing a finite section and enclose the limiting cubic coefficient in a rational interval of width below $9.4\times10^{-29}$. An explicit scaling identifies these energies with the cubic coefficients of the finite polygon constructions. Transferring the profile to unrestricted area maximizers is a further, conditional result: under the stated geometric hypothesis, the profile gives the $n^{-3}$ term of their maximal area. The recurrence, its finite-section estimates and the enclosure can be checked independently of that hypothesis.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 1 figure. Revised title and abstract. The half-line recurrence and finite-section results stand independently; the application to unrestricted area maximizers is conditional on the stated geometric hypothesis. Includes verification code and a rational certificate

papers.title: Entrywise Positivity Preservers on Green Matrices
papers.abstract: We classify entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness on Green matrices with positive parameters. For each fixed \(n\ge2\), PSD preservation is equivalent to \(f\) being nondecreasing and \((f(tr^{i+j}))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) being PSD for all \(t>0,r>1\). For \(f\in C^{2n-2}\), this is equivalent to \(f'\ge0\) and positive semidefiniteness of \(((t\,d/dt)^{i+j}f(t))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) at every positive \(t\). These fixed-order classes strictly decrease with \(n\); their intersection consists exactly of \(f(t)=\int_{[0,\infty)}t^α\,dμ(α)\), where \(μ\) is a finite positive measure and the integral is finite for every \(t>0\). At each fixed order, entrywise Loewner monotonicity is equivalent to \(f\in C^1\) and \(f'\) belonging to the corresponding PSD preserver class. In all orders, monotonicity itself implies smoothness. Nonnegative minors of orders one and two on every strict three-by-three Green input already force \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(t)=ct^α\), with \(c>0\) and \(α\ge0\). They give TN output in every order; the nonzero members also preserve PSD Green structure. We also classify PSD, TN, and Loewner-monotone extensions to the closure allowing zero entries. No regularity is assumed except in the differential criterion.

papers.title: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
papers.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.
papers.comments: 16 pages, no figures. v3 Some mathematical errors and inaccuracies have been corrected. An important citation has been added. Wording has been changed (including abstract). AI was used to tidy this up (acknowledged in declaration). v2 The last conjecture was removed as this was shown to be false via counterexample. This counterexample is now discussed in Proposition 2

papers.title: Fujiki Class $\mathcal C$ Varieties and a Kähler Criterion
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that flips and divisorial contractions preserve the Kähler condition (for strongly $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial compact Kähler generalized klt pairs with $B+β_X$ big), and we give a criterion for varieties in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$ to be Kähler. We also prove the existence of small $\mathbb Q$-factorializations for generalized klt pairs and of dlt modifications for generalized pairs.

papers.title: Polynomial permutation stability, soficity, and universal polynomial groups
papers.abstract: We introduce polynomial permutation stability for maps between groups, extending ordinary permutation stability from homomorphisms to polynomial maps defined by iterated finite differences. We show that a group $G$ is polynomially permutation stable in degree $s$ if and only if its universal polynomial group $\operatorname{Pol}_s(G)$ is permutation stable. While every finite group is polynomially permutation stable in degree two, we prove that the cyclic group of order six is not stable in degree three. More precisely, we construct a finite-index direct-product subgroup of $\operatorname{Pol}_3(C_6)$ to which an instability theorem of Ioana applies. We also show that polynomial sofic approximations characterize the usual class of sofic groups. In degree two, we obtain a split exact sequence relating $\operatorname{Pol}_2(G)$ to a restricted wreath product, with applications to soficity and property $(T)$. A quotient-transfer principle yields infinite, finitely presented, nonperfect groups that are polynomially permutation stable in every degree. Finally, we obtain nonamenability and largeness results for higher-degree universal polynomial groups of finite groups.
papers.comments: 28 pages: 28 pages: Additional results and examples have been incorporated; certain issues identified in the previous iteration have been rectified

papers.title: Pinchoff by surface diffusion
papers.abstract: Since Nichols and Mullins analysed the instability of cylindrical wires in 1965, numerical and asymptotic studies have predicted a self-similar neck at pinchoff under surface diffusion. Yet even the existence of a finite-time singularity for the flow of a smooth closed surface has remained open. We construct the first such examples, and establish their stability, modulo a finite-dimensional space. The same shrinking neck closes the central hole of an embedded torus in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and separates the lobes of a genus-zero dumbbell. In both cases the surface remains embedded until the singular time $T$ and converges smoothly away from the pinching point. Writing $A(t)$ for the waist radius and $r(z,t)$ for the radius near the neck, we prove that $A(t)=\{4μ(T-t)\}^{1/4}(1+o(1)), \quad A(t)^{-1}r(A(t)ζ,t) \longrightarrow U(ζ) \quad\text{in }C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}).$ The profile $U$ above is also for the first time rigorously constructed here. It was numerically computed by Wong-Miksis-Voorhees-Davis, and identified by Bernoff-Bertozzi-Witelski as the ground state of a family of conical shrinkers. Our proof also yields a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows that admit positive symmetric conical shrinkers.
papers.comments: 127 pages, 3 figures. This revision extends the pinchoff construction to embedded dumbbells and proves a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows. The computer-assisted proof certificate is included as ancillary material

papers.title: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
papers.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linear elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

papers.title: Orbits of submaximal dimension for Sylow $p$-subgroups of finite classical orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup in a classical orthogonal group over a finite field with $q$ elements of characteristic $p$ large enough. The coadjoint orbits of the group $U$ play the key role in the description of irreducible complex characters of $U$. In the paper, we provide a classification of such orbits of pre-maximal dimension. As a corollary, we compute the number of all orbits mentioned above. It turned out that each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q - 1$ with integer non-negative coefficients, which agrees with the Isaacs' conjecture.

papers.title: Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
papers.abstract: Recently, three related papers [arXiv:2412.13941, arXiv:2009.00897, arXiv:2409.03626] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [arXiv:1410.2540] using stackings and by [arXiv:1410.2579] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [arXiv:2412.13941] and [arXiv:2409.03626]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.

papers.title: Sturm--Liouville-Type Parity and Oscillation of a Cubic Spline Eigenbasis
papers.abstract: We study the eigen-structure of the kernel matrix arising from cubic smoothing splines on equally spaced knots. Using matrix-theoretic methods, we show that its positive eigenvalues are simple, that the associated eigenvectors alternate between even and odd, and that the eigenvector for the $k$th largest positive eigenvalue has exactly $k+1$ sign changes. Building on established results on oscillatory and centrosymmetric matrices, we provide a more explicit proof of the known oscillation property of the eigenvectors and establish their alternating parity. We then verify, by a separate argument, that both properties extend to the associated continuous cubic spline eigenfunctions, showing that the resulting spline basis exhibits both an alternating parity structure and an oscillation pattern analogous to that of classical Sturm--Liouville eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
papers.abstract: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $Γ$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.
papers.comments: 45 pages, v2: Revised and expanded, including the Yoneda--Frobenius criterion, the Calabi--Yau realization theorem, a quadratic recognition theorem for $d$-stability, and Auslander--Reiten mesh and twisted Ginzburg presentations

papers.title: A remark on polycyclic groups of birational automorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an algebraic variety of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of zero characteristic. Suppose that $G$ is a virtually polycyclic subgroup in the group $\mathrm{Bir}(X)$ of birational automorphisms of $X$. We show that the virtual derived length of $G$ does not exceed $2d$. Moreover, if $X$ is a surface, the bound can be improved to $3$, and this value is optimal.
papers.comments: 13 pages; numerous corrections and minor improvement of the main result

papers.title: A 21-Coloring of the Plane Without Monochromatic Unit-Area Rectangles
papers.abstract: Erdős and Graham asked whether every finite coloring of the plane must contain a monochromatic rectangle of any prescribed area. Kovač gave a negative answer by constructing a $25$-coloring with no monochromatic rectangle of area $1$. We reduce the number of colors to $21$ by replacing the square cells in his construction with regular hexagons.

papers.title: Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes
papers.abstract: Let X be a spectrally negative Lévy process observed up to an inde- pendent exponential time T with parameter γ > 0. We study the joint law of the maximum drawdown and the maximum drawup of X on [0, T ]. The path is decomposed according to the two possible orderings of its in- fimum and supremum. Conditional on the values of these extrema and on their ordering, the resulting pre-, intermediate, and post- components are independent. We identify their laws as Doob h-transforms of killed spec- trally negative Lévy processes and express the corresponding distribution functions explicitly in terms of the γ-scale functions W (γ) and Z(γ) and their derivatives. Combining the conditional laws with the joint densities of the extrema yields integral representations of the joint distribution and moments.

papers.title: Classification of abstract Bose field models
papers.abstract: We classify a class of abstract Bose field models in quantum field theory up to unitary equivalence. The class includes abstract free Bose field models, abstract van Hove--Miyatake models, and infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models. Moreover, as an application of our classification, we classify quadratic interaction models. In particular, our results answer a question of A. Arai concerning the classification of infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models.
papers.comments: 25 pages. Corrected typos and improved readability

papers.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
papers.abstract: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(α\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/α))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(Γ(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/Γ(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(Γ(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_γ\le n)\le n/γ\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(η>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\logγ)/Γ(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([γ,(1+η)γ+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

papers.title: Bounded Ratios of Lorentzian Polynomials II: Quadratic Derivatives
papers.abstract: We study bounded monomial ratios for Lorentzian polynomials. We prove that, in degree $d\geq2$ and $n$ variables, the bounded ratios from quadratic derivatives generate all bounded ratios for every $M$-convex support if and only if $n\leq3$, $d=2$, or $(n,d)=(4,3)$. For four-variable cubics, the proof uses a decomposition into $M$-concave functions. We construct explicit counterexamples with full support for four-variable quartics and five-variable cubics, then extend these two examples to all remaining pairs.

papers.title: The phase coordinates transformation in Moyal noncommutative framework 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator and Painlevé second equation
papers.abstract: This work aims to explore the physical application of Moyal noncom- mutative formalism with the the presentation of new transformations which connect the old canonical coordinates to purly noncommuting phase coordi- nates through the parameters describe the Moyal noncommutative deforma- tion. These transformations are consistent with the Moyal noncommunica- tive brackets and build sixteen components traceless anti-symmetric tensor. This formalism incorporates space-space and space-momentum noncommu- taivity rather then noncommutativity (Heisenberg quantum commutation ) only for the canonical coordinates. The transformations imply to construct noncommutative analogs of 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator with its superintegrability and Painlevé second equation. The associated deformed Hamiltonians additionally involve some extra symmetries and reveal a deep physical understanding of about the additional symmetries with noncommunicative structure. The Painlevé second noncommutative coordinates transformation are also efficiently applied to generate the first Yablonskii Vorobev polynomial with Painlevé second parameter transformation.
papers.comments: This work requires some more detailed calculations. We will add these which are substantial and then we resubmit it

papers.title: The density of long runs of non-$r$-free integers
papers.abstract: Fix $r\ge2$ and let $D_k$ be the natural density of the $n$ such that none of $n+1,\dots,n+k$ is $r$-free. We prove that $\log(1/D_k)=\frac{r-1}{ζ(r)}k\log k+\frac{r}{ζ(r)}k\log\log k-C_rk+o(k)$, where $C_r=\frac{1}{ζ(r)}((r-1)\logζ(r)+r-1+r\log\fracπ{r\sin(π/r)})$; for $r=2$ this is $C_2=\frac{6}{π^2}(1+\log\frac{π^4}{24})=1.4595513\dots$. This determines Mirsky's constant $α(h)$, the density of the $n$ with $s_{n+1}-s_n=h$ in the squarefree numbers, to the same precision. Previously the only known estimate was $\logα(h)\le-\frac54 h\log\log h+O(h)$; ours improves this by a factor of order $\log h/\log\log h$, and is two-sided. The upper bound rests on the observation that the primes $p\le z$ with $\prod_{p\le z}p^r\le\sqrt k$ sieve a window of length $k$ with no freedom of alignment, so that at least $(1/ζ(r)+o(1))k$ positions must be covered by $r$-th powers of distinct primes exceeding $k^{1/r}$. The resulting sum over injections is $m!e_m$ with $m\sim k/ζ(r)$, evaluated by a saddle point. For the lower bound the Chung-Erdos inequality recovers the full contribution of $m!e_m$ rather than merely its largest term, which is what makes the linear coefficient explicit. As a consequence the first-moment threshold for gaps between $r$-free numbers is $\frac{ζ(r)}{r-1}\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}(1-\frac{(1+o(1))\log\log\log x}{(r-1)\log\log x})$; for $r=2$ the constant is $π^2/6$, that of Erdos's 1951 lower bound. We also prove that every covering system of length $k$ has modulus at least $\exp((\frac{r}{ζ(r)}+o(1))k\log k)$, so the Chinese remainder construction yields only $ζ(r)/r$, half of $π^2/6$ when $r=2$. Erdos's bound is thus equivalent to the assertion that the first run of $k$ consecutive non-$r$-free integers occurs at the first-moment threshold, not at the scale set by the minimal modulus of a covering system.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 7 tables. v5: Updated the abstract; added content to the applications paragraph in the introduction; updated data and fastCD version in Section 5; updated disclosures in Section 7 and added a statement on code availability. Code: https://git.tanuki-cd.com/algebraity/fastCD

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
papers.abstract: Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

papers.title: Polarforming-Enabled Power-Splitting SWIPT: A GNN-Based Optimization Approach
papers.abstract: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is a critical technology for the future of the Internet of Things (IoT). However, ensuring a stable power supply in such networks remains a significant challenge. This work introduces dynamic polarization control as an additional degree of freedom (DoF) in SWIPT systems. We propose a system where both the base station (BS) and the users can adjust their antenna polarization, a technique known as polarforming. In addition, each user device is capable of splitting the incident signal to perform simultaneous information decoding (ID) and energy harvesting (EH). The resulting non-convex optimization problem, which involves strongly coupled variables, is addressed using a graph neural network (GNN) that predicts the beamforming, polarization, and power-splitting variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-based dynamic polarforming optimization significantly outperforms fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under imperfect channel state information (CSI). Moreover, joint polarforming and GNN-based optimization maintains robust SWIPT performance under both polarization mismatch and imperfect CSI.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
papers.abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.
papers.comments: 51 pages, 4 figures. Revised version: the introduction and the appendix have been revised, the terminology and notation have been refined, and the remark regarding asymptotics has been removed

papers.title: A Single-Loop Method with Optimal Leading-Order Oracle Complexity for Optimization and Game Stationarity in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a single-loop first-order framework for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, with matching leading-order upper and lower bounds for optimization and game stationarity in a projected zero-respecting oracle model. We propose a single-loop projected damped extragradient method coupling projected extragradient updates with dual momentum and a moving proximal center. Each iteration uses at most three gradient evaluations, without nested subproblems. For game stationarity, a deterministic best iterate has first-order residual below $\varepsilon$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}Δ_φ\varepsilon^{-5/2})$, where $L$ is the gradient Lipschitz constant, $D_Y$ bounds the dual feasible-set diameter, and $Δ_φ$ is the initial-point-dependent value-function gap. For optimization stationarity, a uniformly selected iterate has expected squared Moreau-envelope gradient norm at most $\varepsilon^2$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^2D_YΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-3})$. Matching lower bounds are $Ω(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}Δ_φ\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ for game stationarity and $Ω(L^2D_YΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-3})$ for optimization stationarity over projected zero-respecting first-order methods. Under dual strong concavity, the same framework achieves leading first-order oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtκLΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-2})$ under both criteria, where $κ$ is the dual condition number. Matching lower bounds hold for both criteria in the same oracle model. To our knowledge, this is the first work to close the oracle complexity gap for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization under both stationarity criteria by simultaneously improving upper and lower bounds in the projected zero-respecting oracle model.

papers.title: Radial Limits and Euler Exponents of a False Theta Series with Character Modulo 8
papers.abstract: Let $T_k=k(k+1)/2$ and let $N_n(q)$ be the series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}(2k+1)^{2n+1}q^{T_k}$ for $k\ge 0$. We study the false theta function $D=N_0$ and the moment quotients $N_n/D$. We prove an exact transformation formula for twists of even order. It expresses each moment as a convergent series of derivatives of the Dawson integral, with the dual twist and its phase determined by a quadratic Gauss sum. The formula gives the finite radial values of the moments at roots of unity as nonzero cyclotomic integers and yields congruences between them. Inside the unit disc we consider the quotient of $D$ by the theta series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}q^{T_k}$. Each nonconstant coefficient of this quotient is minus twice a positive integer that counts divisors and restricted partitions. These counts give a Lyndon-word formula for the exponents in the formal Euler product of $D$. The factorization also identifies the unique real zero in $(-1,1)$. A comparison with a cubic polynomial shows that this simple zero is the only zero in $|q|<1/2$.
papers.comments: 22 pages. Substantially revised and retitled. Adds a Dawson-integral transformation and a partition interpretation giving a Lyndon-word formula for the Euler exponents. The coefficient divisibility and 2-adic interpolation results are in v1

papers.title: The smallest square tileable by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles
papers.abstract: Croft, Falconer and Guy (Unsolved Problems in Geometry, Problem C5) exhibit a tiling of the 27 x 27 square by eight pairwise incomparable integer rectangles and remark that it is not known whether 27 is the smallest side length of a square that can be tiled by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles, no restriction being placed on the number of tiles. Knuth has since stated, in a 2019 draft of a section of The Art of Computer Programming, that 27 is indeed the smallest. We give a complete, independently reproducible proof: for every integer n <= 26 and every k >= 2, the n x n square admits no tiling by k pairwise incomparable integer rectangles. The proof combines two structural reductions with an exhaustive search over the 167538 surviving candidate tile sets, carried out by two independently written programs. The same search shows that at least eight tiles are needed at n = 27 and that the tile set of Croft, Falconer and Guy is the only one that tiles this square; it does so in exactly two arrangements up to symmetry. We also give explicit eight-tile tilings of the n x n square for every n >= 27, and seven-tile tilings for every n >= 34. With the classical lower bounds (every tiling of a rectangle by two or more pairwise incomparable rectangles uses at least seven, and no square of integer side less than 34 can be tiled by seven pairwise incomparable integer rectangles), this determines the least number of tiles for every square: there is no tiling for n <= 26, eight tiles are needed for 27 <= n <= 33, and seven for n >= 34. The complete software, build instructions and output logs are included as ancillary files.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 2 figures. v2: cites Knuth (TAOCP Vol. 4B), who stated that 27 is smallest; proves the tile set at n = 27 unique (two arrangements up to symmetry); gives 8- and 7-tile tilings of all larger squares and the least number of tiles for every square; corrects references. Ancillary files: verification software (two independent programs, self-checking) and all output logs

papers.title: Fractal Hyper-Trees I. Combinatorial foundations: definition, enumeration, invariants, morphisms and the algebra $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: Fractal Hyper-Trees (FHTs) are hypergraphs organized in levels: each level consists of disjoint connected clutters, and every edge strictly contains each lower component that it meets. Connected clutters and Schr{ö}der hierarchies are the two extreme cases. Every FHT decomposes uniquely into the children of its top component, which carry smaller FHTs, and a host, an arbitrary connected clutter on these children. This gives an exact recurrence by size and depth and a species equation; the counts begin 1, 1, 4, 23, 231, 16947, 490083358 and are exact through nine vertices. Four interior moves (fusion, fission, aggregation, explosion) connect the FHTs on a given vertex set; every FHT on at least two vertices descends to the star by moves at distance at most one from the root, and $κ-1$, with $κ$ the number of edges, is its distance to the star. For FHTs with automorphism group $S\_4$, twisting the real group algebra by the sign character gives $\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{H}\oplus M\_3(\mathbb{C})$, the finite algebra of Connes' description of the Standard Model. Conversely this algebra determines the group up to isomorphism and the class of a real 2-cocycle. The axioms select neither the group nor the twist: with the twist fixed as the sign of the action on the vertices, the algebra occurs exactly when $\mathrm{Aut}\,F\cong S\_4$ and some automorphism is odd on the vertices, at every size $v\ge4$. Every finite group is the automorphism group of a flat FHT, and every faithful action on a finite connected simplicial complex is rigidified into a flat FHT with the same reduced integral homology. All computations are deposited and their kind (exhaustive, sampled, exact or numerical) is stated.
papers.comments: 91 pages, 3 figures. v2: complete revision; the ultrametric part is moved to a separate article. Programs: GitHub SaloneJJ/FHT-Structures-and-Sperner-Enumerations, release v9.2 (Zenodo)

papers.title: Affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures
papers.abstract: In 2025, the affine dual curvature measures $\widetilde{C}_m^a(K,\cdot)$ of convex body $K$ were introduced by Cai, Leng, Wu, and Xi, and the even Minkowski problem for the affine dual curvature measures was solved. In this paper, the necessary and sufficient condition of affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures with $m>1$ are proposed.

papers.title: Positive normalized solutions for a singular regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: We study a singular Dirichlet problem driven by a regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian under a prescribed modular constraint. We construct nonnegative constrained minimizers for nonsingular approximating problems and, under the stated variational and boundary-control hypotheses, obtain a positive normalized weak solution as the reaction regularization vanishes. The approximation preserves the prescribed modular and yields subsequential strong Sobolev convergence of the states together with convergence of their constraint multipliers, while the gradient regularization remains fixed. Finally, we present a normalized singular problem on the unit disk as an illustrative example.

papers.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
papers.abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.
papers.comments: Result was generalized to a fixed point property result for a large class of Banach spaces (including Lp spaces and theta-Hilbertian Banach spaces) and not Hilbert spaces. The general criterion for fixed point property was simplified

papers.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
papers.abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.

papers.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
papers.abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schrödinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.

papers.title: Exact Ehrhart Series of Birkhoff Polytopes via Constant Terms and Finite-Field Evaluation
papers.abstract: The Ehrhart series of the $n$th Birkhoff polytope is $\sum_{r\geq0}H_n(r)z^r$, where $H_n(r)$ counts nonnegative integer $n\times n$ matrices whose row and column sums all equal $r$. We present an exact method for computing this series using constant terms and finite fields. A root filter expresses $H_n(r)$ as a weighted sum of the values $h_r(M)^n$, where $h_r$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial and $M$ ranges over multisets of $m$th roots of unity with $m=r+1$. Constant-term cancellation reduces the evaluation of $h_r(M)$ to a sum over repeated elements $a$ of $M$. For a particular $a$ of multiplicity $μ_a$, the computation uses a generalized Todd coefficient of degree $μ_a-2$. Sums of $h_r(M)^n$ over selected multiplicity classes are handled using symmetric function techniques. Together with the remaining individual evaluations, this gives $O_n(m^{n-5}+m^4)$ field operations for each admissible prime and fixed $n\geq5$. An explicit bound and the Chinese remainder theorem recover the integer counts, and Ehrhart symmetry determines the full series. The same method applies to the World Cup problem, which counts the same matrices with diagonal entries required to be $0$. We prove correctness and compute complete Birkhoff series through order $14$ and World Cup series through order $13$. The Birkhoff series for orders $10$--$14$ and the World Cup series for orders $9$--$13$ are tabulated in the appendices.

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
papers.abstract: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

papers.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
papers.abstract: How much information can a single neuron remember? How many memories can neural networks retrieve without creating false memories? These questions are related to a basic question: how many Boolean threshold functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_0+\langle a,x\rangle)$, $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, are there? In this paper, we show that the number $T_n$ of distinct Boolean threshold functions is \[ T_n=2\binom{2^n-1}{n}\bigl(1+O(n^{-99})\bigr). \] Equivalently, the capacity of a single threshold neuron is $n^2-\log_2(n!)+1+O(n^{-99})$ bits, improving the $O(n)$ error term in the result of Kahn--Komlós--Szemerédi to $O(n^{-99})$. To prove this, we show that, for $1\le r\le n-1$, and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ are chosen at random from $\{-1,1\}^n$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left\{ \langle v_1,\ldots,v_r\rangle\cap\{-1,1\}^n =\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_r\} \right\} =1-O(n^{-99}). \] In the context of the Kanter--Sompolinsky Hamiltonian for memory retrieval, this identifies $r=n-1$ as a sharp threshold, at which, for almost every collection of $r$ memories, the only ground states are these memories and their negatives, confirming a weaker form of the Kalai--Linial--Odlyzko conjecture. It also settles a recent open problem posed by M. Anthony on the specification number of Boolean threshold functions. In addition, we show that, for every $1\le r\le n-1$, \[ \mathbb P\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\text{ are linearly dependent}\} =2\binom r2\,2^{-n}+O\!\left(2^{-n}e^{-cn}\right), \] confirming a conjecture of Kahn--Komlós--Szemerédi.
papers.comments: Lean verification is available at https://github.com/XinyuanXie-hub/BooleanThreshold and in the Palomar entry at https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-20-000020&version=1

papers.title: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.
papers.comments: v2: presentation improved. A finite regular cover of each approximating space is shown to be equivariantly a product with a torus, so the global Seifert fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action, and a principal torus bundle over manifold limits. New Appendix A on equivariant comparison over local groups, and an index of the notation and of the dependence of the constants. 80 pages

papers.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
papers.abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 1 figure. Adds Theorem 2, the uniqueness of the extremal polyhex, with a proof generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz and formalised in Lean

papers.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal matching covered graphs
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is {\em matching covered} if each of its edges lies in a perfect matching. A matching covered graph is {\em minimal} if the removal of any edge results in a graph that is no longer matching covered. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B 23 (1977) 127--138] proved by ear decompositions that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ edges, and this bound is sharp for all even $|V(G)|\ge6$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (4) (2026) 559--606] determined the extremal graphs achieving this upper bound. In this paper, we prove that every minimal matching covered nonbipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(5|V(G)|-10)/2$ edges. Moreover, we show that if $G$ is not bicritical, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-14)/2$ edges and if $G$ is 3-connected and has at least 14 vertices, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-26)/2$ edges. All three bounds are sharp, and all the corresponding extremal graphs are characterized.

papers.title: Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
papers.abstract: Two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions arise from differential recursions with rational initial data: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. At order $p=3$, their rational coefficients yield the triangles OEIS A140136 and A336110, together with a positive palindromic numerator triangle for the odd sector. In general, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn companions, and an explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual series. The Narayana quadratic ($p=2$) and the $S_4$-symmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia quartic ($p=3$, with two tetrahedral edge resolvents) serve as explicit low-order benchmarks. For every $p \ge 3$, we prove that the distinguished reduced generating function has exact algebraic degree $2(p-1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(x,h^{p-1})$ and that every Horn companion is algebraic. Over $h$, the rational uniformization lifts to the Fermat curve $s^{p-1}+w^{p-1}=1$ of genus $(p-2)(p-3)/2$ with generic monodromy and Galois group $S_{2(p-1)}$. This uniform cover establishes the universal boundary factorization at $H=h^{p-1}=0$ and explains the cubic characteristic factor $\mathcal{A}_p^3$ (carrying a projective $S_3$ action) in the discriminant via $(2,3)$-cusp geometry, illustrated by exact sextic and octic equations and higher-order slices. Conversely, a nonexact differential on the Fermat curve combined with full $S_{2(p-1)}$ monodromy proves that the distinguished self-dual function is transcendental for all $p \ge 4$. The complete factorization of the generic reduced discriminant remains open.

papers.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

papers.title: Asymptotically Hölder gradient regularity for degenerate or singular parabolic normalized $ p$-Laplace equations
papers.abstract: We study bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular parabolic equation \[ u_t-|Du|^γΔ_p^{\mathrm{N}}u=f \qquad \text{in } Q_1, \] where \[ Δ_p^{\mathrm{N}}u := Δu+(p-2) \left\langle D^2u\frac{Du}{|Du|}, \frac{Du}{|Du|} \right\rangle, \qquad -1<γ<\infty,\quad 1<p<\infty, \] and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $α\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,α)>0$ such that \[ |p-2|+|γ|\leq\varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+α,\frac{1+α}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient Hölder exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $ 1 $ as $(p,γ)\to(2,0)$. This extends the result of Andrade and Santos (Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{61}, Paper No. 196, 2022) for $γ=0$ to the joint regime $(p,γ)\to(2,0)$ and answers affirmatively the question raised in Remark~1.1 therein.

papers.title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support Kähler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.
papers.comments: Corrected the proof of the main theorem. The revised theorem gives explicit generators for the field of meromorphic functions under the additional assumption that there are no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms. This assumption is automatic for LVMB manifolds with one or two indispensable indices

papers.title: Montesinos Knots with Delta-Unknotting Number One
papers.abstract: The $Δ$-unknotting number for a knot is defined as the minimum number of $Δ$-moves needed to deform the knot into the trivial knot. In this paper, we discuss Montesinos knots whose $Δ$-unknotting number is equal to one. We propose a conjectural characterization of Montesinos knots with $Δ$-unknotting number one and provide examples admitting distinct $Δ$-moves, each of which deforms the knot into the trivial knot. Furthermore, we present examples illustrating the relationship between the locations of $Δ$-moves and $X$-moves for knots with $u^Δ(K) = 1$, considering separately the cases $u(K) = 1$ and $u(K) = 2$.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 21 figures, 6 tables. Additional examples have been included to illustrate the relationship between the locations of $Δ$-moves and $X$-moves for knots with $u^Δ(K) = 1$, considering separately the cases $u(K) = 1$ and $u(K) = 2$. Minor corrections and revisions have also been made throughout the paper

papers.title: A homotopical enhancement of Neisendorfer's algebraic models
papers.abstract: We give an $\infty$-categorical enhancement of Neisendorfer's equivalences between the homotopy categories of rational simplicial sets, commutative dg algebras (cdgas), cocommutative dg coalgebras (cdgcs) and dg Lie algebras (dgls), where these objects have respective hypotheses of connectedness, nilpotency and finite type.
