We do so by proving that linear duality is a partial Quillen equivalence between weak finite type connected cdgcs and cdgas, and that Quillen's Chevalley--Eilenberg adjunction is a partial crossed derivable equivalence between cdgcs and dgls, a concept we introduce in this paper to axiomatize precisely the behavior of this adjunction.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.
papers.comments: 15 pages. v2 now covers all positive characteristics and simplicial rings

papers.title: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Ampère equations with periodic measures
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Ampère equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $μ$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $μ(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $μ_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^nμ(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,μ_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,dμ(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,α}(\overlineΩ)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Ampère problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.
papers.comments: We establish optimal higher-order convergence rates for periodic measures in the newly added Section 5. Title and introduction revised. 49 pages

papers.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
papers.abstract: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.

papers.title: Generalized Commutator on Octonion Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be an octonion algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and let $A,B\in\mathcal O$, not both zero. We study the image of the generalized commutator $Φ(x,y)=A(xy)-B(yx)$ on $\mathcal O$. We prove that $Φ$ is surjective if and only if either one of $A$ and $B$ is invertible and $A\neq B$, or $A$ and $B$ are nonzero zero divisors and $A-B$ is invertible. In the remaining cases, the image of $Φ$ is a hyperplane or a four-dimensional maximal totally isotropic subspace of $\mathcal O$, except when $A$ and $B$ are linearly independent zero divisors and $A-B$ is not invertible, in which case the image spans a six-dimensional subspace. Along the way, we show that every octonion of trace zero is a commutator. We also prove that the image of $Axy-Byx$ on any quaternion algebra over $F$ is a vector subspace, extending a result of Panja S., Saini P. and Singh A. (Images of polynomial maps with constants, Mathematika 71 (2025), no. 3, Paper No. e70031) for $2\times 2$ matrices over algebraically closed fields, and we give examples of other generalized polynomials whose images are not vector subspaces.

papers.title: A Single-Loop, Constant-Batch First-Order Penalty Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent advances in penalty-based methods for stochastic bilevel optimization (SBO) have eliminated the need for second-order derivative oracles. However, for stochastic nonconvex-strongly convex bilevel problems, existing first-order methods typically rely on nested loops and/or large batch sizes for attaining $O(ε^{-6})$ or $O(ε^{-4})$ sample complexity under standard bounded-variance assumption or mean-square smoothness assumption. Achieving these rates with a single-loop penalty method and a constant batch size remains challenging due to a large penalty value needed for an accurate approximation. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic SIngle-loop COnstant-Batch first-order penalty method (SICO) that combines two complementary ingredients. First, it performs one stochastic-gradient update per-iteration for both the original lower-level and penalized problems, with a projection that controls the separation between their iterates. Second, it applies an exponential moving average to stabilize the upper-level gradient estimator. We show that this combination achieves $ O(ε^{-6}) $ sample complexity using only $O(1)$ stochastic-gradient samples per iteration under unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Under the additional mean-square smoothness assumption on the lower-level stochastic gradients, the same algorithm improves the complexity to $O(ε^{-4})$ also with $O(1)$ batch size. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to match the best-known convergence rate for fully first-order SBO methods using a single loop and a constant batch size. This result addresses an open problem posed in the literature.

papers.title: Spectral Erdős--Gallai Theorems for the \(\mathcal A_α\)-Tensor of the \(s\)-Clique Hypergraph
papers.abstract: The generalized Erdős--Gallai theorem determines the maximum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no matching of $t$ edges. We study its spectral analogue for the $\mathcal A_α$-tensor of the $s$-uniform clique hypergraph. For $n\geq2t-1$, $3\leq s\leq2t-1$, and $0\leqα\leq1$, we determine the maximum $α$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex graphs with no matching of $t$ edges, and characterize all extremal graphs. When $t<s\leq 2t-1$, the unique extremal graph up to isomorphism is a $(2t-1)$-clique with isolated vertices. When $3\leq s\leq t$, the extremal graphs are selected from this graph and the join of a $(t-1)$-clique with an independent set. We give the exact order at which the join becomes extremal and determine when both graphs attain the maximum.

papers.title: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations: Construction and Optimal Sobolev Approximation
papers.abstract: We construct fully deterministic finite-dimensional spaces for Sobolev approximation using shallow neural networks with a localized activation $σ$, either Gaussian or tanh-difference. For a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and a prescribed regularity index $s>0$, the approximation space at frequency resolution $M$ is\[ V_M^Ω=\operatorname{span}\left\{ σ\!\left(\frac{ω_i\cdot x-b_{j,M}}{\varepsilon_M}\right): 1\le i\le J_M,\quad 1\le j\le K_{i,M} \right\}. \]All parameters are prescribed explicitly and independently of the target function. The offset cutoff depends on the direction and the domain, with an exterior margin tending to zero. The feature count satisfies $N_M=\sum_{i=1}^{J_M}K_{i,M}\asymp M^d$. For sufficiently large $M$, we construct a bounded linear operator $\mathcal A_M^Ω:H^s(Ω)\to V_M^Ω$ that achieves the optimal approximation rate \[ \|u-\mathcal A_M^Ωu\|_{H^m(Ω)} \le C N_M^{-(s-m)/d}\|u\|_{H^s(Ω)} \] for every $u\in H^s(Ω)$ and every integer $0\le m<s$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions illustrate the approximation behavior in $L^2$ and $H^1$.

papers.title: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations: Condition Number Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper gives bounds on the spectral condition numbers of Sobolev Gram matrices for deterministic ridge features with Gaussian or tanh-difference activations. In earlier work we showed that the shallow neural network spaces spanned by these features attain optimal Sobolev approximation rates. For either activation $σ$, the construction uses $N_{σ,M}\asymp M^d$ features at resolution $M$ on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$. For each fixed integer $m\ge0$ and all sufficiently large $M$, the raw $H^m(Ω)$ Gram matrix $G$ and its column-normalized counterpart $\widetilde{G}$ are positive definite and satisfy \[ \max\{κ_2(G),κ_2(\widetilde{G})\} \le \exp(CM)\quad (d=2), \] and \[ \max\{κ_2(G),κ_2(\widetilde{G})\} \le \exp(CM\log(M+1))\quad (d\ge3), \] where $C$ is independent of $M$. On the unit ball in every dimension $d\ge3$, matching lower bounds show that the order of the exponent is sharp for both matrices.

papers.title: Non-degeneracy and Fibering with Applications to Diophantine Approximation
papers.abstract: Motivated by applications in Diophantine approximation, we develop a new fibering mechanism for non-degenerate manifolds in $\mathbb{R}^n$, showing that they admit local decompositions into families of non-degenerate curves with uniform quantitative non-degeneracy estimates. Our construction applies to $l$ non-degenerate $C^N$ manifolds under the optimal regularity assumption $N\geq\max\{n,l\}$, requiring no additional smoothness. Furthermore, we show that this uniform quantitative local control can be globalised into a qualitative statement, so that almost every point of a non-degenerate manifold lies on a non-degenerate curve contained in the manifold. The resulting quantitative fibering estimates are also stable under sufficiently small $C^n$ perturbations at each fixed spatial scale. The method provides a framework for extending fibering based results in Diophantine approximation from curves to manifolds. Such applications are considered in the paper.

papers.title: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.

papers.title: Fourier Restriction Beyond Dimension Data: A Multiscale Moment Criterion
papers.abstract: We establish an exact restriction criterion for weighted Moran measures with uniformly bounded one-level frame bounds: for every $2<s<\infty$, $L^2(μ)\to L^s(\mathbb R)$ extension holds if and only if $\widehatμ\in L^s(\mathbb R)$, equivalently, if and only if $\sum_nG_{s,n}<\infty$, where $G_{s,n}$ sums the $s$th powers of the magnitudes of the $n$th digit mask at its nonzero grid frequencies. The proof combines finite-frame stability and multiscale iteration with disjoint resonant frequency grids. The criterion determines the critical restriction exponent and characterizes its attainment when it lies in $(1,2)$. We construct singular continuous spectral Moran measures with common scales, digit cardinalities, exponential spectrum, maximal mask magnitudes at nonzero grid frequencies, and a global Fourier decay bound sharp along a common resonant sequence, yet different critical restriction exponents. For any prescribed finite positive summability exponent of these maxima, we determine the optimal interval of critical restriction exponents and realize both endpoint attainment and failure at every interior point with the same fixed data. These measures can simultaneously satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm F}^θμ=θ$ for $0\leθ\le1$ and $D_q(μ)=1$ for $1<q\le\infty$, with local dimension one at every support point. Finite-field spectral constructions realize every critical restriction exponent in $[1,2]$ with these dimensional data and exhibit sharp logarithmic endpoint transitions. They also yield singular continuous measures with Fourier dimension zero, restriction for all $1\le p<2$, and stretched-logarithmic Fourier decay with an optimal exponent. Finally, all-scale $L^q$-dimension formulas yield explicit examples where dimensional criteria strictly improve the classical Stein--Tomas--Mockenhaupt range.
papers.comments: Removed the proof of the former Proposition 6.7; Shortened the abstract;Revised and expanded the proof of Lemma 2.1, and some other revisions

papers.title: Nonminimizing Attration of Stochastic Subgradient Methods on Semialgebraic Functions
papers.abstract: We construct a globally Lipschitz, coercive, semialgebraic function in two dimensions for which stochastic subgradient iterates converge to the origin, a Clarke critical point that is neither limiting critical nor a local minimizer. For power-law stepsizes, this attraction holds on open sets of initial points and linear tilts, uniformly over all noise sequences within a prescribed bound. The example shows that subdifferential regularity cannot be removed from the generic guarantee of convergence to local minimizers established by Davis, Drusvyatskiy, and Jiang (2026). For the same tilted objectives and initial points, the unique Clarke subgradient flow converges to a strict local minimizer. Thus, convergence of continuous-time flows to local minimizers cannot by itself justify the corresponding guarantee for discrete subgradient methods, even with diminishing stepsizes.
papers.comments: 16 pages, 2 figures. This revision adds a proof that the Clarke subgradient flow converges to a strict local minimizer from the same open set of initial points for which the discrete iterates converge to the nonminimizing origin

papers.title: Postcritically finite endomorphisms II: algebraic core and Fatou set
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a postcritically finite endomorphism of the complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^N$ of degree at least two. We prove that at every periodic point of $f$, the non-superattracting tangent directions span the tangent space of a periodic projective subvariety which is rationally connected. This phenomenon strongly constrains both the dynamics and the geometry of postcritically finite endomorphisms. In particular, we show that every Fatou component of $f$ is preperiodic and is eventually mapped into the basin of a superattracting cycle.

papers.title: Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.
papers.comments: 7 pages. Revised version. The construction has been simplified by replacing SU(3) with SO(3), reducing the dimension of the example from 11 to 6. The self-intersection set is now determined explicitly. The exposition and proofs have also been revised

papers.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
papers.abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $σ$-complete, lattice-$σ$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

papers.title: A Sharp Basis-Mass Inequality for Binary Matroids without a Fano Minor
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a binary matroid of rank $r$ with no $F_7$-minor, and let $B_M^\star$ denote the maximum of its basis-generating polynomial over nonnegative weights of total mass $r$. We prove the sharp inequality $B_M^\star\leq 2^r/(r+1)$, with equality holding if and only if the simplification of $M$ is isomorphic to $M(K_{r+1})$. Binary matroids with no $F_7$-minor also form the largest minor-closed class of matroids on which this inequality holds. For each fixed rank $r$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-element rank-$r$ matroid maximising the number of bases in this class is graphic.

papers.title: Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.

papers.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
papers.abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with $|x_3|$ of size at most $M$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$, using a smooth weight $Φ(x_3/M)$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and hence to geodesics in the hyperbolic plane. Under this correspondence, $x_3$ is small exactly when the geodesic passes close to the point $i$. We count these geodesics by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $θ=7/64$ is the Kim-Sarnak exponent. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$, with $D_0$ a fundamental discriminant, the geodesics are closed. We obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+θ}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$. The main inputs are the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao for cycle integrals, the cubic moment bounds of Young and of Andersen-Wu, and a Hecke relation which reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$ we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+θ+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, which is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High; Fable 5.2 in the final stage), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
papers.comments: v3: rewritten to be self-contained (results unchanged): strategy overview, preliminaries on binary forms, hyperbolic geometry, spectral theory, L-functions. 63 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Written in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), see Subsection 1.7. Numerical checks as ancillary files. A film explaining the proof: https://drive.google.com/file/d/12j5xYgMBr0KrrZYOO3SiU-BPhcDnAd61/view

papers.title: Doubly commuting invariant and co-invariant subspaces
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_{i}$ be complex separable Hilbert spaces and $T_{i}\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{i})$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. On the Hilbert tensor product $\mathfrak{H}:=\mathcal{H}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{H}_{n}$, consider the operator tuple $(\tilde{T}_{1},\dots,\tilde{T}_{n})$ defined by $T_{i}:=I_{\mathcal{H}_{1}}\otimes \cdots \otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{i-1}}\otimes T_{i}\otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{i+1}}\otimes \cdots \otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{n}}.$ A closed jointly $(\tilde{T}_{1},\dots,\tilde{T}_{n})$-invariant subspace $\mathfrak{M}\subseteq\mathfrak{H}$ is doubly commuting if $(\tilde{T}_{1}\vert{}_{\mathfrak{M}},\dots,\tilde{T}_{n}\vert{}_{\mathfrak{M}})$ is doubly commuting. We prove that if the hereditary polynomials in each $T_{i}$ ($i=1,\dots,n$) are ultraweakly dense in $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_i)$, then $\mathfrak{M}$ is doubly commuting if and only if $\mathfrak{M}=\mathcal{M}_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{M}_n$, where each $\mathcal{M}_i\subseteq\mathcal{H}_i$ is a closed $T_{i}$-invariant subspace. As applications, this provides a unified framework for characterizing doubly commuting quotient modules of weighted Bergman spaces over $\mathbb{D}^{n}$ and tensor products of complete Nevanlinna-Pick spaces. It also characterizes doubly commuting jointly invariant subspaces for tuples of backward shifts and their adjoints on tensor products of de Branges-Rovnyak spaces $H(b)$ (for both extreme and certain nonextreme $b$), as well as for tuples of coordinate Volterra operators and its adjoints on $L^2((0,1)^n;\mathbb{C})$. In particular cases, we recover known characterizations of doubly commuting quotient modules of $H^2(\mathbb{D}^n)$ and doubly commuting submodules of its Jordan blocks. Finally, our framework extends naturally to mixed tensor products combining distinct factor spaces from any of these settings.
papers.comments: Substantially revised; main definition modified, new results added, and an additional section included

papers.title: On blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+Δu=u^p$. First, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we prove a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that the leading-order relativistic Euler system admits a smooth self-similar imploding profile whose associated normalized coefficients satisfy quantitative analytic radius conditions. Second, we verify both the existence of the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. Using the finite speed of propagation, we then obtain a threshold $p_0$, independent of the dimension, such that for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, there exist smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data whose solutions blow up in finite time. The proof combines three ingredients: a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, the growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.
papers.comments: The language has been polished. 123 pages, 1 figure

papers.title: Conditional limit theorems for open intermittent dynamical systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study conditional limit theorems for open intermittent systems endowed with big/small holes. The initial measure for the system can be a broad class of (non)invariant probability, including SRB and Lebesgue measures. Unlike the limit theorems for closed systems, we obtain unexpected new limits for both ``regular" and singular observables.

papers.title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
papers.abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
papers.abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.

papers.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. These are double affine versions of the quantum affine wreath algebras of Rosso and Savage. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite cyclic group, we obtain new double affine versions of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the supercentre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.
papers.comments: 33 pages, 2 figures. v2: fixed PDF and HTML version formatting, clarified some statements and the abstract

papers.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
papers.abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $α\in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,α}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_δ$ for the closed $δ$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,α})_δ$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,α}(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_α$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < δ< 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_α)_δ$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_α(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $γ((E_α)_δ)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/δ))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, with constants depending only on $α$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_α)_δ$ is at most $C_αγ((E_α)_δ)^{2α}$ for every $0 < δ< 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $α> 1/2$, and its exponent $2α$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $α$ tends to one.

papers.title: Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations
papers.abstract: We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $α\in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $α\in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.
papers.comments: 31 pages; minor edits; no new mathematical content from v1

papers.title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
papers.abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler--Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball and a Lipschitz test function, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + Σ^2 h^2 + h^4 \log^2\frac1h)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $Σ$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4 \log^2\frac1h$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $Σ^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error.

papers.title: Equivalence of Restricted and Full Division
papers.abstract: We prove over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$ that the restricted Euclidean division principle $\mathrm{pa17}^{-}$, which asserts division only for co-prime pairs, is equivalent to the full principle $\mathrm{pa17}$. The proof uses a transformation that preserves the quotient in division with remainder to reduce an arbitrary division problem to one for a co-prime pair. This answers Visser's Open Question 8.29 and shows that the restricted principle has the same strength as full Euclidean division over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$. An appendix further shows that $\mathrm{PA}^{-}_{\mathrm{jer}}+\mathrm{pa17}$ proves both the predecessor principle $\mathrm{pa14}$ and the subtraction principle $\mathrm{pa15}$.
papers.comments: 6 pages,Added an appendix deriving pa14 and pa15 from pa17

papers.title: Some results on representation type and Galois covering with application to the associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
papers.abstract: We prove some general results on representation types of special biserial algebras and on Galois coverings of quivers with relations. Moreover, combining these results with the covering theory of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras we determine the representation types of the associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras.

papers.title: Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study multilevel optimization problems in which the outer objective depends on a finite composition of implicit response maps defined by smooth inner functions. This model covers chains of strongly convex minimization responses, strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses, or a mixture of the two. We propose a fully first-order method that estimates the outer gradient through recursive response perturbations. The main difficulty with approximate responses is that an adjoint error at one level changes the perturbation vector at the preceding level. To control this propagation, we pair the unperturbed and perturbed updates at each level and track their scaled differences jointly with the forward response errors. The resulting tracking bounds are uniform in the perturbation radius $δ$. For the exact composite objective, we establish an $O(K^{-1}+δ^2)$ bound on the average squared gradient norm after $K$ outer iterations. For fixed problem data and finite depth, a suitable choice of $δ$ yields $ε$-stationarity in $O(ε^{-2})$ outer iterations with inner budgets independent of the target accuracy. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
papers.abstract: Let $χ_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,χ_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $ξ_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R$, we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2} Φ_L(u) e^{izu} du, \] where $Φ_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ Φ_L(u) := \frac{1}{2π}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} ξ_L \left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu} ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $ξ_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $Λ_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge Λ_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $Λ_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $Λ_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $Λ_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $Λ_L\le95241/320000=0.297628125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.
papers.comments: 95 pp., 10 figs. v2: Revised several sections and theorems. Improved the unconditional uniform bound and some individual bounds. Updated the numerical tables

papers.title: The Art of Toda Brackets: A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
papers.abstract: One of the fundamental aims of the present book is to provide a reference for the computation of unstable homotopy groups using methods developed by the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. The theory of Toda brackets is fundamental to the study of composition relations among homotopy classes. Appendix~A.3 brings together all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained primarily through Toda brackets, with explicit generators. Appendix~A.2 explains the conventions used to name the generators. The book presents calculations, with explicit generators, of the $2$-primary components of $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq28$ and all $n$, together with selected calculations in degree $29$; (two possible group structures remain for $π_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11))$). The odd-primary components in the range considered can be computed with little additional effort, essentially by consulting the relevant entries in existing tables. As a further check, we examine our result for $π_{23}(\mathit{SO}(9))$ using the unstable Adams spectral sequence.We also give some geometric applications.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.
papers.comments: Remark 5 and Lemma 1 are new, 96 pages, 14 figures

papers.title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.
papers.comments: Paper accepted for presentation at IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications 2026

papers.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(λ,p)=\sup_{\|u\|_{H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)}\le1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\bigl(e^{4πu^2}-1-λ|u|^p\bigr)\,dx, \qquad p\ge2, \] Chen--Jiang--Lu--Zhu gave the first classification of attainment away from the thresholds across the full range of $p$. We prove attainment at both thresholds for $p=2$ and at the unique threshold for each $2<p\le4$. At and above the upper quadratic threshold, $S(λ,2)=4πe^{1-2γ_{\mathrm E}}$, Nguyen's concentration level, where $γ_{\mathrm E}$ is the Euler--Mascheroni constant. At each endpoint, the centred radial extremals form a compact set and their $L^p$ masses determine the slope from within the attainment interval. For fixed $p>4$, we obtain the expansion \[ S(λ,p)=4π+\mathcal C_pλ^{-2/(p-4)} +D_pλ^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(λ^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \qquad λ\to\infty. \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting problem at unit $L^2$ mass, and $D_p$ selects the limiting profiles. For fixed $λ$ above the quartic threshold $λ_*(4)$, we prove \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(λ,p)-4π\bigr) =2\log\frac{λ_{\mathrm{loc}}}λ<0, \] where $λ_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. An exact radial transformation extends these results to every planar norm.

papers.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_χ)$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.

papers.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
papers.abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $Γ$, the canonical map $EΓ\to\underline{E}Γ$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

papers.title: Pattern-dependent stability of binary exponential perturbations
papers.abstract: We study how the arrangement of binary frequency perturbations affects the stability of exponential systems on an interval of length one. For frequencies $λ_n=n+s_nδ$, with $s_n\in\{-1,+1\}$, we represent synthesis in Fourier coordinates by a shifted-sinc operator $N_{δ,s}$ and identify its Gram operator as $G_{δ,s}=N_{δ,s}^*N_{δ,s}$. The optimal squared synthesis bounds are $1\pmρ_{δ,s}$, where $ρ_{δ,s}=\|P_-T_{2δ}P_+\|$ measures the interaction between the two sign classes. Using the finite-matrix representation of periodic perturbations, we prove that, for each fixed $0\leqδ<1/2$, the minimum lower bound among $p$-periodic binary patterns converges to the worst binary lower bound as $p\to\infty$. At Kadec's critical amplitude $δ=1/4$, the alternating pattern has a positive lower bound, whereas a step pattern reduces to a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has lower bound zero. Every fixed periodic pattern nevertheless remains a Riesz basis. We discuss the resulting periodic extremal questions and record a direct perturbation estimate giving explicit stability neighborhoods around stable reference patterns.

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.
papers.comments: 51 pages; Appendix A has been added and the proof of Lemma 4.2 has been revised to complete the argument for non-symmetric types; New references have been added

papers.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

papers.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.
papers.comments: 27 pages. Besse implies Zoll extended from spheres other than S^4 to all closed manifolds, and the Gromoll-Grove-type result from even-dimensional spheres to all even-dimensional manifolds

papers.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
papers.abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we obtain its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted Hölder seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for $F_o$-radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction and, for $1<p\le n$, on a splitting of the transformed function into its $F_o$-spherical mean and a mean-free part. Since $F^2$ is not a quadratic form unless $F$ is induced by a scalar product, the reduction of the radial part through spherical harmonics, used in the Euclidean case, is not available; we control the radial part directly, through a convexity inequality for $F^p$ with a quadratic remainder and sharp one-dimensional estimates, and the mean-free part through a Poincaré inequality on the boundary of the Wulff shape. For $p>n$ we use an anisotropic Morrey representation formula.
papers.comments: 23 pages, revised version of the paper

papers.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
papers.abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.
papers.comments: 11 pages; revision: introduction, proofs, conclusion and bibliography are extended

papers.title: The \(\mathcal A_α\)-Spectral Turán Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
papers.abstract: For integers $3\leq s\leq r$ and $0<α<1$, we study the maximum spectral radius of the convex combination of the degree and adjacency tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graph. For $n\geq r$, every extremal graph is complete $r$-partite. For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly in $α$, the only possible extremal graphs are $T_r(n)$ and $K_1\vee T_{r-1}(n-1)$. There is a unique parameter $α_n$ at which both attain the maximum; the former is uniquely extremal below $α_n$ and the latter above it. Writing $c=((r-1)/r)^{s-1}$, we show that $α_n=c+(s-1)c/n+O_{r,s}(n^{-2})$. The limiting maximum after normalization by $n^{s-1}$ is $\binom{r-1}{s-1}\max\{r^{1-s},α(r-1)^{1-s}\}$. A sharp row-quotient bound at $α=c$ identifies the limiting part proportions; local comparisons then determine the exact integer part sizes.

papers.title: Frangible prime gaps
papers.abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erdős. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.74161, 2.79201]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
papers.abstract: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanović's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.
papers.comments: 44 pages, includes computer-assisted proofs and supplementary Python/SageMath verification programs

papers.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $σ$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $σ$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,σ)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $σ$-preserving action $α$ satisfies that $\overline{α(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,σ)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $α$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $α:G\curvearrowright (D,σ)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $σ$-preserving action with $\overline{α(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

papers.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
papers.abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

papers.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].
papers.comments: 9 pages; we have now added the hypothesis from Theorem 4.2 to Theorem 4.5

papers.title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
papers.abstract: Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$. For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel. For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$. We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $σZ$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $σ\ge0$. The large-$σ$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls. Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.
papers.comments: 67 pages; minor changes compared to the previous version

papers.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-étale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This settles a case left open by Manin's construction. We also obtain unirationality results for Du Val del Pezzo surfaces of degrees $1$ and $2$, and discuss applications to the Hilbert property, equivariant unirationality, and the real plane Cremona group.
papers.comments: 16 pages. Corollaries 3-4 and Subsections 3.2-3.3 are new

papers.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
papers.abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

papers.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the Höegh-Krohn model.

papers.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
papers.abstract: How quickly can we construct the martingale with prescribed initial and terminal laws that is closest to Brownian motion in the sense of the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem? The construction requires the initial law of an auxiliary Brownian motion. One can take this law to be the distribution of a minimizer of the lifted Bass functional. In dimension one, Backhoff, Pammer and Schachermayer proved, under additional assumptions, that the gradient flow of this functional converges exponentially to a minimizer. We extend this result to arbitrary dimension. Under the assumptions of the paper, the gradient flow starting from a bounded random vector converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the minimizer with the same mean. We prove this by showing that, for a fixed random vector $X$ with the prescribed initial law, the lifted Bass functional is strongly convex on each set of $σ(X)$-measurable vectors with a prescribed mean and a common $L^\infty$ bound.
papers.comments: 36 pages, 0 figures. English version followed by the Russian version. Revised proof of strong convexity and exponential convergence in arbitrary dimension

papers.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Kollár and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.
papers.comments: 20 pages. Additional references, minor changes in Section 2.F and Lem.3.2, results unchanged

papers.title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
papers.abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.0-2.6$\times$.

papers.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
papers.abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.
papers.comments: 25 pages. Expanded exposition and clarified proofs, including a simplified proof of the Gaussian limit. Main results unchanged

papers.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $σ$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
papers.abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
papers.comments: Addition of a reference posted right after this post and a comment in the introduction.Maths are unchanged

papers.title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.

papers.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. This answers a question of M. Tkachenko (2014) and extends the separable case of the author's 1994 theorem on Tychonoff pseudocompact groups to regular spaces. The proof rests on a new result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is feebly compact and $Z$ is regular, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Previously this was known only when $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are Tychonoff. Using topological games of Banach-Mazur type, we extend the group theorem to regular separable Baire groups from a wider class of spaces, which contains all $p$-spaces, all feebly compact spaces and all products of a $p$-space with a feebly compact space. We also obtain local versions: the theorem holds for locally separable, locally feebly compact groups.

papers.title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $Δ\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ-1\}$, conjectured for all $Δ\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $Δ\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.

papers.title: Finite refutations in countably additive quantum probability
papers.abstract: We axiomatize countably additive quantum probability and prove a completeness theorem for finite refutation beyond compactness: inconsistency is witnessed by refutations each of whose branches ends in finitely many jointly unsatisfiable commitments. Adjoining the hypothesis that every event has a predetermined, context-independent outcome makes the theory inconsistent, although every finite subset of the resulting axioms has a model. For a countable theory of closed bounds on sentence values in our real-valued infinitary logic, inconsistency is equivalent to a winning strategy for a challenger in a game against a model builder. The challenger chooses each test in response to the builder's commitments, and the plays that follow a winning strategy form such a refutation. For the quantum theory with predetermined outcomes, every winning strategy must branch infinitely at some node. In the strategy we construct, countable additivity locates the four-dimensional subspace in which a finite Kochen-Specker parity argument applies. In their standard models, our axioms describe the closed subspaces and the density-operator probabilities of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. We prove in ZFC that the sets of probability values definable uniformly across standard models are exactly the $σ$-projective subsets of the unit interval.

papers.title: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.
papers.comments: 27 pages; the mathematical content of the second version is the same as the first one, but the material is now better organized, and the code and the experiments have been moved to a companion notebook

papers.title: The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
papers.abstract: In one dimension, the symmetric binomial tree replicates quadratic payoffs using the Delta of its own price function. For every $d\geq 2$ and every centered, isotropic, minimally complete $(d+1)$-state model with $d$ risky assets, by contrast, some quadratic payoff requires a replicating hedge different from that Delta. In this nonredundant finite-state setting, centered one-step payoffs are spanned by the $d$ asset innovations; centered second-order (Gamma) contributions are therefore represented as first-order trading gains, potentially inducing additional asset holdings. We call this effect Gamma-to-Delta aliasing and measure it by the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)=\mathbb{E}[(ξ^\top Hξ-\operatorname{tr}H)ξ]$, where $ξ$ is the normalized one-step innovation and $H$ the Gamma matrix. For quadratic claims the replicating holding exceeds the price Delta by exactly $\sqrt{h}\,\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)/2$, where $h$ is the time step. Trading this holding in a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)|^2/4$, a fixed multiple of the ordinary discrete-Delta error that does not vanish in relative terms as $h\downarrow0$. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete models is $\sqrt{d-1}$, so the worst-case relative excess variance is $(d-1)/2$; both are attained uniquely by the equal-probability regular simplex. For unit-Frobenius positive-semidefinite Gammas and for unit rank-one Gammas, the sharp minimax value is $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also show how aliasing trades off against unhedgeable quadratic risk when more states are allowed, and derive the leading implementation cost for smooth claims.
papers.comments: 23 pages. Abstract and introduction rewritten; references updated; main results unchanged

papers.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $Λ$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $Λ$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.
papers.comments: Corrected cross-reference formatting, added a GitHub link for computational reproducibility, and updated the AI-use declaration. Mathematical content unchanged

papers.title: A true $Π^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
papers.abstract: We give a true $Π^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehatφ$ denotes its interpretation on $ω$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehatφ$ is a $Π^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.
papers.comments: In this revision, a sketch of the proof of Theorem 2.3 is added, Remark 2.8 is expanded and two related references are added

papers.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.
papers.comments: V2 contains a new appendix showing that the proof also gives existence for certain families of maps which are only complex analytic on a neigbourhood of the real line

papers.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
papers.abstract: We study the Jacobians of a genus-two family with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We realize these abelian surfaces as factors of cyclic-cover Jacobians and determine their integral rank-two monodromy. For the real embedding with $\sqrt5>0$, the projective image is the Hecke group $Δ(2,5,\infty)$; the conjugate real image is nondiscrete. After a finite base change, we give an explicit degree-four map from Cohen--Wolfart's Hecke cyclic curve to the genus-two curve.
