Four deck translates of the induced Jacobian pullback give an integral isomorphism from the fourth power of the surface to the eight-dimensional primitive order-$20$ factor, with an explicit nonproduct polarization. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ torsion-line covers are normalizations of quadratic fibre products of genus-one triangular modular curves. We also describe the associated split and nonsplit Cartan-normalizer covers. Finite-field hypergeometric traces give the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation with a twist by the quadratic character of $2$.

papers.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty II
papers.abstract: Building on our earlier work, we present an $L^2$-$L^1$ inequality for radial Fourier eigenfunctions, relating this to the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane. We also propose a generalisation of the aforementioned uncertainty principle, and draw a connection with entropic uncertainty.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].
papers.comments: A couple of flaws have been identified, and we hope they can be fixed in the near future

papers.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
papers.abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $Σ_{\max}^2<1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions. We also show that the asymptotic variance for the Schwarzian derivative is at least $5.68\ldots$, which defeats the hypothesis that the Nehari criterion would be almost sharp.

papers.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
papers.abstract: We develop a unified virtual element framework for compatible polytopal discretizations of differential forms in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. On general polytopal meshes, a central challenge is to construct de Rham subcomplexes and establish stability estimates with mesh-independent constants. We construct a trimmed complex of conforming virtual differential forms recursively from local Hodge--Laplace boundary value problems and obtain a complete subcomplex by imposing additional moment constraints. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom from which polynomial projections can be computed. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and each virtual complex has cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual complexes and in every form degree, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and thereby prove a mesh-uniform equivalence between the $L^2$ norm and the scaled degree-of-freedom norm. Through the cochain isomorphisms induced by the degrees of freedom, these norm equivalences yield uniformly bounded liftings of fully discrete data into the corresponding continuous spaces, in particular for the Discrete de Rham method. We also derive canonical interpolation error estimates and discrete Poincaré inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge--Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity.

papers.title: Ricci pseudo symmetric Anisotropic Fluid Spacetime admitting Hyperbolic solitons with Ricci vector field
papers.abstract: This work focuses on an anisotropic fluid spacetime with these unique forms of the stress-energy tensor associated with radial pressure and a transverse pressure p. In an anisotropic fluid spacetime , we mani- fest curvatures symmetry such as Ricci pseudo-symmetric and prove that Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime is generalized quasi- Einstein spacetime. We deduce the Einstein gravitational field equation of Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime. In the framework of pseudo-Riemannian geometry, specifically, we study the quasi-conformal Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime, which exhibit the dark matter era. Moreover, we discuss the hyperbolic Ricci soliton and Hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field. Finally, we turn up the char- acteristics of hyperbolic Ricci soliton and hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field.
papers.comments: The paper contains critical factual, unpolished methodological, and some invalid conclusions that could mislead researchers or be cited improperly

papers.title: Species sampling priors through exact augmentation
papers.abstract: Discrete random probability measures are central to Bayesian nonparametric modeling. In practice, their use often favors a few tractable priors with full weak support. Full support alone, however, does not specify how prior mass reflects beliefs about clustering, recurrence, discovery and other sample features. We develop a novel and general construction of species sampling process (SSP) priors from an index distribution and finite allocation probabilities, linked to these sample characteristics. Every proper SSP admits an exact two-stage representation through an almost surely finite index and a finite conditional measure. Averaging over the index recovers each realized SSP on every measurable set. Reversing this identity constructs priors whose tie probabilities, expected occupancy and discovery rates can be assessed without evaluating the infinite weights. We characterize compatibility among index laws, schedules and weights, and construct light-tailed, heavy-tailed and multimodal families with full weak support under suitable hyperpriors. A prior with paired weights combines full weak support with invariance under size-biased permutation in its defining order, an explicit finite index law and partition prediction. Exact simulation, recursive reweighting and finite posterior augmentation follow. Examples distinguish prior elicitation, exact averaging and fixed-level approximation.
papers.comments: Main text: 35 pages, 2 figures; supplementary material: 59 pages, 2 figures

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,α}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,α}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

papers.title: Quasisymmetry of self-similar carpets
papers.abstract: We classify self-similar carpets obtained by repeating a fixed pattern in the same orientation on a square grid. All boundary cells are retained. The first approximation has a nonempty family of Jordan polyomino holes with pairwise disjoint closures in the interior of the unit square. Every quasisymmetry between two such carpets is the restriction of a square symmetry. Thus quasisymmetric, bi-Lipschitz, and isometric equivalence coincide. Two patterns give equivalent carpets exactly when their subdivision parameters have a common positive power and their retained cells agree up to symmetry on the common grid. The criterion extends to patterns periodic from the first generation. We also construct an area-zero square carpet with uniformly relatively separated peripheral circles and a quasisymmetric involution that sends a corner into an open side. Its quasisymmetry group is dihedral of order eight, and its isometries are the four rotations. It belongs to the quasisymmetric class of the standard middle-third carpet and to a different isometry class.

papers.title: The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
papers.abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. We also prove that the intersection of two Grothendieck noncommutative $\cM$-bimodules is also Grothendieck. These answer several open problems in the literature.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a formula for the Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple determination of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even degree cohomology. This is then applied to the study of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we analyse the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,q}$ as well as ample divisor complements in orbifold K3 surfaces and Calabi-Yau threefolds, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.
papers.comments: 73 pages, 4 figures. Removed some unnecessary assumptions from Theorem A, added more computations (including CY3 compactifications) and fixed some typos. Comments welcome!

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. In the Szegő setting, local rigidity was established by Lu--Tian (2004) on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and, more recently, by Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026) on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces.
papers.comments: 49 pages. Various improvements on the presentation. Added an appendix with an example of Bergman logarithmic flatness without Szegő logarithmic flatness

papers.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval, and outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$. Near this threshold $a_*$ the distance between the two modes is of order $(a-a_*)^{1/2}$, and the width of the interval is of order $(a-a_*)^{3/2}$. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one. The proof bounds the sign changes of the first and second differences of the finite walk, including those created at the boundary, and passes them to the limit.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 2 figures. v3: revised exposition and redrawn Figure 1. Proposition A.3 is now Proposition 2.6, Lemmas A.4 and A.5 are now A.3 and A.4, Remark 1.4 is now Remark 4.1, and the proof of Proposition 3.7 is in the new Appendix E. Code, certificates and Lean files: https://github.com/apemm/elephant-bias-interval

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov, the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

papers.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
papers.abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

papers.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
papers.abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterized by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 3 figures; supplementary materials included (Sections SM1-SM7). Data and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23962730. Companion paper: arXiv:2610.27188

papers.title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. For such an operator with bounded measurable coefficients in dimension $n \ge 2,$ fix a center $x_0$ and a volume $V > 0,$ and let $E$ be the corresponding canonical set. We prove that a bounded open set $D$ of volume $V$ containing $x_0$ satisfies the mean value inequality at $x_0$ for every integrable subsolution on $D$ if and only if $E \subset D \subset \operatorname{int}\overline{E}.$ In particular, every such strong mean value set agrees with $E$ almost everywhere. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ''mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume contains the entire unit sphere and has a hole of positive measure inside the unit ball.

papers.title: On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.
papers.comments: 29 pages, fixed a couple of mistakes

papers.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
papers.abstract: A defender releases an integer-valued secret $X$ (a count, a discretised measurement, a clock value) as $Y = X + N$, where $N$ is an independent integer-valued mask whose expected absolute value, the expected distortion of the released value, is at most $c$. An adversary who knows the prior of $X$ and the law of $N$ observes $Y$ once and makes a single guess. We determine exactly how small the adversary's success probability, the posterior Bayes vulnerability, can be made, and which masks achieve it. For a secret supported on an interval of $m$ integers we give the optimum and an explicit optimiser for the uniform prior; by the maximal-leakage formula, the same mask minimises the worst-case-prior one-guess leakage for every prior with that support. For a biased bit, the simplest prior a defender can exploit, we characterise the masks that leak nothing on average, give the critical budget at which this becomes possible, and determine the entire cost-vulnerability frontier. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks, with infinitely many affine pieces accumulating at the critical budget, where the frontier meets the prior vulnerability with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both vulnerability and cost are exactly additive. The results give exact, prior-aware design guidance for additive integer noise against one-guess adversaries.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 3 figures. v3: adds explicit dual-multiplier proof of Corollary 21, expands Appendix B derivation, minor fixes. Verification scripts archived at Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24418378)

papers.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
papers.abstract: We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-\mathsf{r}ν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.

papers.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
papers.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with Hölder-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the Hölder topology.

papers.title: Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.

papers.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
papers.abstract: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
papers.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.
papers.comments: This is a substantially revised expository version with navigational aids and an extended literature review; not intended for publication

papers.title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

papers.title: Mixed Inner Variation and Global Hessian Integrability for Degenerate Monge-Ampère Equations
papers.abstract: We study the global Hessian integrability for nonzero convex solutions of the degenerate Monge-Ampère equations $\det D^2u=M(-u)^p$ with zero boundary values on arbitrary bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in the global Lipschitz regime $p>n-2$. We establish global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for every $0<\varepsilon<\min\{(p-n+2)/n,1\}$ and determine the optimal range of $\varepsilon$ in dimension two and on rectangular boxes. The flat faces of rectangular boxes and their intersections impose upper bounds on the admissible exponents of global Hessian integrability. A new input in the proof for general dimensions is a Caccioppoli-type estimate for the boundary Hessian mass using vector fields arising from a mixed second inner variation. For the sharp higher integrability result in the plane, we use the combined hodograph-Legendre transform to control the curvature of level sets.

papers.title: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
papers.abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.
papers.comments: 29 pages, Comments are welcome,v2: reference update

papers.title: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
papers.abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on $\mathbb{Z}$ or unilaterally on $\mathbb{N}_0$, inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gaussian constant $G=\varpi/π$ with the lemniscate constant $Γ^2(1/4)/(2\sqrt{2π})$ by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} 2k \operatorname{cosech}(k π) = G^2 + \frac{1}π. $$ Furthermore, by connecting these distributions to Fourier transforms of powers of the hyperbolic secant and applying the Poisson summation formula, we obtain closed-form evaluations for even moments and hyperbolic secant lattice sums, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathrm{sech}^4(k π) = \frac{2}{3} \left(G^4 + G^2 + \frac{1}π\right) $$ as polynomials of the Gaussian constant.

papers.title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
papers.abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.

papers.title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
papers.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_τ:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Zτ)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_τ(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_τ$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).

papers.title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
papers.abstract: We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other. For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.
papers.comments: 40 pages, 11 figures, 1 table; v2: affiliations and funding information added; declarations section added; minor edits, no changes in the mathematical content

papers.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining ordinary spectral flow on fixed-point spaces with minimal-overgroup nullities, we obtain a lower bound on the number of exact-stabilizer bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and requires endpoint invertibility only on the chosen fixed space, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. When the restricted Hessians have finite Morse index, the criterion involves only indices and nullities. We also treat varying form domains under explicit transport assumptions and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. As our principal application, we consider a Newtonian nine-body family consisting of two interlaced squares with fixed satellite masses and a varying central mass. We prove analytically that central configurations with two nonconjugate exact reflection stabilizers bifurcate at a common mass in $(142,150)$, displacing the central body from the centre of mass. The family contains a reported counterexample to Moeckel's linear-stability conjecture; our bifurcation proof is independent of that stability assertion.

papers.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$ u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
papers.abstract: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we give exact counting formulas as functions of $|X|$ in terms of finite sums and generating functions. Such pairs correspond bijectively to actions on $X$ of the semigroup presented by two generators and the prescribed relation. The proofs use images, fibers, and the decomposition of functional digraphs into directed cycles with rooted trees attached. Several constructions apply beyond these sixteen identities: they give recurrences for homomorphisms between arbitrary prescribed functional digraphs and formulas for pairs satisfying $f^a=g^b$, where $a,b$ are fixed positive integers. We also derive an explicit inclusion-exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$ for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$. This generalizes the enumeration of compositional square roots, recovered when $A$ is the identity map.

papers.title: Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

papers.title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
papers.abstract: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.
papers.comments: We correct some typos from the previous version

papers.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
papers.abstract: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's method. In fact, assuming PCC by itself without RH is sufficient to prove that asymptotically $100\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are both simple and on the critical line. We adapt the notion of horizontal multiplicity from Goldston et al. to show that the nontrivial zeros of Artin $L$-functions attached to irreducible linear representation of the Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ are almost surely simple and lie on the critical line without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). We will assume the appropriate version of PCC along with some other widely believed conjectures.

papers.title: Degenerate Preconditioned Proximal Point Algorithms as Forward Methods for Nonmonotone Inclusions
papers.abstract: We study degenerate preconditioned proximal point algorithms (PPPA) for finding zeros of nonmonotone set-valued operators in Hilbert spaces under solution-relative $(U,V)$-semimonotonicity, with possibly indefinite $U$ and $V$. With a closed-range preconditioner $P$, the reduced PPPA dynamics admit a forward representation through the complementary resolvent of a parallel composition, without requiring monotonicity or admissibility. Relative semimonotonicity of the range-restricted operator transfers to the reduced forward map, allowing our forward theory for possibly set-valued mappings to yield Fejér estimates and residual rates. Under suitable conditions, including demiclosedness of the reduced map at zero, the projected PPPA iterates and shadows converge weakly to a common projected zero. Without demiclosedness, a counterexample shows that the projected sequences may converge to a point outside the projected zero set, even when the original operator is continuous. Bounded recovery condition yields weak convergence of the full (non-projected) shadows. The monotonicity modulus $U$ yields additional results: under suitable conditions, $U\succeqτP$ with $τ>0$ gives strong and linear convergence of the projected PPPA sequences, while $U\succeq-σP$ with $0\leσ<1/2$ still permits local linear rates under metric subregularity. These strong convergence and linear rate guarantees extend to the full shadows when a Lipschitz recovery estimate holds, such as when $U$ is strongly monotone on $\ker P$. For Chambolle--Pock and Douglas--Rachford splitting, we establish Lipschitz recovery even when $U=0$ by exploiting the primal--dual structure. Under suitable parameter conditions, full-shadow convergence guarantees, including $R$-linear rates, extend to the original PPPA iterates.

papers.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I
papers.abstract: We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. Local cost inequalities reduce arbitrarily long switching cycles of a minimizer to six types. We exclude those types by geometric comparisons and rigorous finite verification, and identify the remaining short minimizer.
papers.comments: 430 pages. The author hopes that further work will lead to a shorter and more beautiful proof

papers.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
papers.abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $β_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leqβ=β_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $β\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.
papers.comments: v2: More and better examples, new section on 2-generator nilpotent groups

papers.title: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
papers.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

papers.title: A tight upper bound on non-overlapping codes
papers.abstract: Non-overlapping codes (also known as cross bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a $q$-ary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{q-1}{qe} +O(n^{-1/4})\right)\frac{q^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $q$ fixed, where $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm. The constant $(q-1)/(qe)$ improves, by a factor of $(q-1)/q$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). Indeed, constructions of large non-overlapping codes show that this constant is best possible. The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Strüngmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).
papers.comments: 19 pages. Compared to the previous version: a better asymptotic bound which is now tight; a shorter proof; new dedication

papers.title: Projector-Based Conic Formulations and Exact Decompositions for Distance-Based Assignment
papers.abstract: Given a set of fixed origin points and a set of variable target points in the same ambient metric space, we study distance-based assignment problems in which target placement and the assignment of origins to targets are determined simultaneously to minimize the overall distance-induced cost. We show that the assignment structure can be represented using orthogonal projection matrices. This observation leads to new mixed-projection conic formulations that avoid the big-$M$ envelopes used in standard mixed-integer models. Building on these formulations, we develop exact decomposition algorithms that separate the discrete selection of assignment projectors from the convex conic subproblems for target location. We also derive semidefinite relaxation bounds and primal procedures that provide warm starts for the exact methods. The proposed approach establishes new connections between distance-based assignment, orthogonal projectors, and low-rank semidefinite optimization, and applies to general conic-representable metrics.

papers.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
papers.abstract: A strong edge coloring is an edge coloring where two edges receive different colors if they are incident or joined by a third edge. For a graph $G$, the strong chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_s(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a strong edge coloring of $G$. In this paper, using a local flag algebra method, we prove that for every graph $G$ of sufficiently large maximum degree $Δ$, $χ'_s(G)\le 1.6388Δ^2$, improving the bound $1.73Δ^2$ due to Davey, Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos, Kang, and Volec.

papers.title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

papers.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

papers.title: Critical Times for Local Controllability and Steady-State Transfer of a Water Tank
papers.abstract: We determine the critical times for a water tank governed by the one-dimensional Saint-Venant equations with horizontal acceleration as the control. Time is measured in units of the linear wave crossing time. For $C^1$ fluid trajectories and continuous controls, local exact controllability holds exactly for $T>T_c=2+d_c\approx 2.43674$, where $d_c$ is determined by two transcendental equations. In the same trajectory class, the system is locally controllable between still-water equilibria if and only if $T>2$. These thresholds confirm Coron's conjecture for steady-state transfer and give a larger value for local exact controllability. The same quadratic endpoint formula and nonlinear correction yield the positive results for both problems. At $T_c$, comparison with a critical plane curve gives the obstruction to local exact controllability. At $T=2$, the nonlinear flux forces small trajectories between still-water equilibria to be stationary.

papers.title: Synchronized Normalized Solutions for a Critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg System
papers.abstract: We study positive synchronized normalized solutions to the critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg system: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=λ_1|x|^{-2a}u+β_1|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(μ_1|u|^{p-2}u+να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^γ\right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla v) &=λ_2|x|^{-2a}v+β_2|x|^{-bq}|v|^{q-2}v\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(μ_2|v|^{p-2}v+νγ|u|^α|v|^{γ-2}v\right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} subject to the prescribed weighted masses \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx=ρ_1^2,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}v^2\,dx=ρ_2^2, \end{equation*} where $N\geq5$, $0\leq a<\frac{N-4}{2}$, $a<b<a+1$, $α,γ>1$, $α+γ=p=\frac{2N}{N-2(1+a-b)}$, $2<q<p$, $β_i,μ_i,ρ_i>0$ for $i=1,2$, and $ν>0$. The associated Lagrange multipliers $λ_1,λ_2\in\mathbb R$ are unknown. Under suitable algebraic compatibility conditions, we establish existence and multiplicity results for positive synchronized normalized solutions. The construction is based on synchronized reduction and critical energy estimates involving a finite-mass Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg extremal. In the mass-subcritical regime, we find two positive solutions with opposite energies when $β=β_1ρ_1^{q-2}=β_2ρ_2^{q-2}$ is sufficiently small. In the mass-critical and mass-supercritical regimes, we obtain a synchronized Pohozaev ground state below the critical energy threshold for sufficiently small $β$ and for all $β>0$, respectively. All these solutions satisfy $λ_1=λ_2<0$.

papers.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
papers.abstract: We prove the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume bound for lattice polytopes with $k\ge3$ interior lattice points: the Euclidean volume of such a lattice polytope is at most $6(k+1)$, with equality if and only if the polytope is affinely unimodularly equivalent to $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,3e_2,6(k+1)e_3)$. The inequality is strict when the minimum lattice width is at least three. Together with the known cases $k=1,2$, this completely resolves the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture.

papers.title: On the $φ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $φ^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.
papers.comments: Reflection positivity proof sketched, typos corrected, reference added

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties I. Fibrations over curves
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or the function field of a curve, and let $X\to C$ be a projective fibration over a curve over $K$. We prove a height inequality for relatively nef adelic line bundles $\bar L$ on $X$ with $L$ nef. For a nef, relatively ample line bundle $L$ over a finitely generated field, we deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model. Over $\mathbb{C}$, for an ample line bundle $L$ and a smooth positive polarization, the Euler--Lagrange equation is the Calabi--Yau equation. On the projective bundle $X=\mathbb{P}_C(E)$ of a vector bundle $E$ of degree zero, our energy on quotient metrics on $L=\mathcal{O}(1)$ agrees with Donaldson's functional when the determinant metric is fixed. We propose a construction of canonical heights on parameter spaces using envelopes of local energies.

papers.title: Character codegrees in $π$-separable groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_π(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $π$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(χ)=|G:\kerχ|/χ(1)$) are $π$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $π$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_π(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_π$-characters $\operatorname{B}_π(G)$.
papers.comments: There are errors in this article

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in\ZZ_{\ge0}$ as $λ$-lengths of essential simple ideal arcs based at a distinguished cusp of a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

papers.title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
papers.abstract: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of topology and latent states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian: a flexible generative transition can absorb graph-induced changes of the conditional mean, whereas a Gaussian transition discards the information in the residual shape. We develop a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, and a frozen diffusion emulator represents the conditionally centered residual. First, a score--topology duality expresses edge-wise likelihood gradients as edge projections of the residual diffusion score, so topology learning requires neither transition densities nor differentiation through the sampler. Second, we prove identifiability from intermittent observations, invariance of the population minimizer across noise levels, and global strong convexity above an explicit smoothing threshold for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. With known support and oracle state pairs, the asymptotic covariance approaches the Cramér--Rao bound as smoothing vanishes and is strictly smaller than that of any Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimator under an explicit non-Gaussianity condition; for unknown sparse support we characterize the boundary limit, and we quantify the topology bias caused by residual-score mismatch. Third, we couple score-driven graph updates with an approximately fully adapted generative particle filter and prove, for bounded residuals under explicit excitation and forgetting conditions, a mean-square closed-loop bound with a step-size-independent small-gain condition. Synthetic and real-data experiments confirm these gains under non-Gaussian forcing.

papers.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
papers.abstract: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(π/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. We also study orthogonal families in a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] For \(1<p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] For \(1<p\le2\), uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(s\) for every \(1\le s<p\), with a quadratic bound in the restricted type constant at \(s=2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} We also record the subcritical type implication for Pythagorean orthogonality and the sharp factor \(p\) for Roberts orthogonality. {For each \(1<p<2\), as the modulus of roundness \(ν_X(p)\) approaches \(2\), the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant tends uniformly to \(1\) over real Banach spaces of Rademacher type \(p\). The same limit holds for the ratio of the two constants restricted by mutual Birkhoff--James orthogonality.}

papers.title: The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.
papers.comments: 28 pages, 2 figures. v2: Added an AI use statement. v3: Added an appendix proving the width bound for SYS bands in all dimensions, with an application to SYS-enlargeable manifolds. Added statements on conflicts of interest and data availability, and corrected several typos. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: The isolation number of uniform hypertrees
papers.abstract: An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $ι(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Let $T$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. We prove that if $T$ has order $n$ and at least two edges, then $ι(T)\le\lfloor n/(2r-1)\rfloor$, where $r\ge3$. Moreover, the bound is attained for every admissible order. Furthermore, we characterize all hypertrees attaining it by a construction using six types of marked hypertrees of orders $2r-1$, $3r-2$ and $4r-3$. For connected graphs of order $n$ with at least two blocks, all of which are triangles, we obtain the sharp bound $\lfloor n/5\rfloor$ on the cycle isolation number and characterize the graphs attaining it.

papers.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $λ$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+λ=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.
papers.comments: 14 pages -- some cosmetic corrections were made in the previous version

papers.title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
papers.abstract: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $δ>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^δ(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^δ(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{δ\to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^δ(K)) |}{δ^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $δ$ instead of $δ^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

papers.title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
papers.abstract: For a crystallographic root system $Φ$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}Φ$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $ρ+ λ$, where $ρ$ is the Weyl vector and $λ$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $ρ$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

papers.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
papers.abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.
papers.comments: 31 pages. Comments welcome! v2: improved exposition a bit and clarified remark 1.6 (now 1.9) in the introduction (added Cor. 1.8)

papers.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square torus
papers.abstract: For each finite $s>1$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$. The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a finite-dimensional family of one-dimensional solutions of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier. At and above the index two, we match the second-order normal frequency shift separately on each triangle using harmonics of the axial solution. For every fixed $2<s<\infty$ we also obtain a solution for which $\log\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\asymp\sqrt{\log t/\log\log t}$ at every sufficiently large time.
papers.comments: This version extends the results presented in v1

papers.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
papers.abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{24}\in K$.
papers.comments: 88 pages. Refined version with Theorems 1.2-1.4 stronger

papers.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that complete expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in complex manifolds, provided their closures admit neighborhoods with holomorphic immersions into Euclidean space. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler--Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

papers.title: Interior $W^{2,p}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend Caffarelli's interior $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère equation to the $k$-Hessian equation, $3\leq k\leq n-1$, under sharp Sobolev or Hölder assumptions on the solution. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,β}$ for some $1-2/k<β<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1<p<\infty$; if the density is positive and belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^α$, then $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,α}$ for $0<α<1$. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we also establish global $W^{2,1}$ regularity on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{1,1}$ domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary values.

papers.title: Rigidity and Non-Rigidity of Disk Pseudo-Rotations below $C^2$
papers.abstract: For every $0<β\le1$, we prove $C^0$-rigidity of area-preserving $C^{1,β}$ disk pseudo-rotations with non-Brjuno rotation number. At the $C^1$ endpoint, every non-Brjuno rotation number of zero exponential type admits non-rigid examples. We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation. We show that this boundary conclusion fails in the bi-Lipschitz class by constructing non-rigid examples for every rotation number of finite positive exponential type. The proof of rigidity is based on a finite-information closing theorem under Hölder regularity. For the construction of counterexamples, we use disjoint supports instead of a summable perturbation scheme.
papers.comments: Minor formatting improvements throughout the manuscript. No changes to the mathematical results or proofs

papers.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
papers.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two.
